- **[B030]**            Windows LeakDetector Has No Throwing Path — All Servers Always "sent" →
                         Any Interception Returns NotDetected (False Negative)
- **Criticality:**      Critical (quick-guide #1 false "no leak" verdict, #2 real interception
                         undetected, #4 platform-divergent verdicts: macOS returns Inconclusive,
                         Windows returns NotDetected; resolution: Critical, not Medium, per
                         [syxx-researcher] 2026-07-10); analysis 2026-07-09, corrected 2026-07-10.
- **Location:**        Windows/Syxx.Kit/LeakDetector.cs:218-240 (TriggerQueriesAsync);
                         DNSResolver.cs:119-122 (QueryUDPAsync — no status check);
                         DNSResolver.cs:191-202 (QueryUDPDetailedAsync — never throws on
                         transport/protocol failure, returns Timeout response at :204)
- **Issue:**            Unlike macOS (which throws via `recordsOrThrow` on timeout/mismatch/truncated/
                         transport failure, DNSResolver.swift:265-266, 1178-1193), Windows
                         `QueryUDPDetailedAsync` (DNSResolver.cs:179-212) catches everything except
                         OperationCanceledException and returns a Timeout DNSResponse at :204.
                         Its caller `QueryUDPAsync` (:119-122) passes `.Records` through with no
                         status check. Therefore `TriggerQueriesAsync` (LeakDetector.cs:218-240) sets
                         `results[server] = true` for EVERY server — including total blackhole /
                         no-response / transport failure. The E007 all-failed guard (:125) is
                         unreachable dead code. Consequence chain: fully intercepted or blackholed
                         DNS → collector verify sees nothing → `leaked=false, observedResolvers=[]`
                         → `ReconcileVerdict` (LeakDetector.cs:206-213) returns NotDetected — a false
                         "no leak detected" where macOS honestly returns Inconclusive. Note: macOS is
                         NOT suspect-parity — it correctly records false via the throwing path.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Related D004 (collector signature verification). macOS LeakDetector verified
                         correct (throws on failure, per [syxx-researcher] 2026-07-10).
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix A — the real fix, S effort] In TriggerQueriesAsync call
                         QueryUDPDetailedAsync and count dispatch success ONLY for answered statuses
                         (Success/NoData/NxDomain/Refused/ServFail), mirroring macOS recordsOrThrow
                         semantics — Timeout / ResponseIdMismatch / Malformed / TransportError /
                         Truncated ⇒ false. This resurrects the E007 guard.
                         [Fix B — honesty, S] Rename the user-facing claim from "sent" to "answered"
                         (or tri-state answered/no-answer/unknown): even a genuine answer only proves
                         a responder exists, not delivery to the configured resolver — against an
                         on-path adversary the collector attestation is the only delivery proof.
                         (User approval needed for wording.)
                         Note: TXID match (proposed as Fix 1 in initial filing) is ALREADY
                         implemented (DNSResolver.cs:445-449) and does not fix this — a mismatch is
                         returned as a status, not thrown, and TXID cannot defeat an on-path
                         responder who reads the query.

                       - **Tool Name**            [syxx-researcher]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-10
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Disagree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       Ground 2 (legitimate delta, wrong stated basis) and
                                                ground 3 (wrong fix). The defect is WORSE than filed:
                                                it is not "any non-throwing response = sent" — on
                                                Windows there is effectively NO throwing path at all.
                                                DNSResolver.cs:119-122 `QueryUDPAsync` returns
                                                `(await QueryUDPDetailedAsync(query)).Records` with
                                                no status check, and QueryUDPDetailedAsync NEVER
                                                throws for protocol or transport failures — it
                                                catches everything except OperationCanceledException
                                                (DNSResolver.cs:191-202) and returns a Timeout
                                                DNSResponse (:204). So TriggerQueriesAsync
                                                (LeakDetector.cs:218-240) sets `results[server] =
                                                true` for EVERY server — including total blackhole /
                                                no response whatsoever — and the E007 all-failed
                                                guard at LeakDetector.cs:125 is unreachable dead
                                                code. Consequence chain: fully intercepted or
                                                blackholed DNS → Windows proceeds to collector verify
                                                → collector saw nothing → leaked=false,
                                                observedResolvers=[] → ReconcileVerdict
                                                (LeakDetector.cs:206-213) returns NotDetected — a
                                                false "no leak detected" where macOS honestly returns
                                                Inconclusive. macOS is NOT suspect-parity as the
                                                cross-ref guessed: queryUDP throws via
                                                recordsOrThrow (DNSResolver.swift:265-266,
                                                1178-1193 — timeout/mismatch/truncated/transport all
                                                throw), so triggerQueries (LeakDetector.swift:
                                                206-217) correctly records false. Proposed Fix 1
                                                (TXID match) is ALREADY implemented
                                                (DNSResolver.cs:445-449 rejects mismatches, :184-188
                                                retries) and fixes nothing here: a mismatch is
                                                returned as a status, not thrown, and TXID cannot
                                                defeat an on-path responder who reads the query.
                                                Quick-guide #1/#2 (false "no leak" verdict; real
                                                interception undetected; platform-divergent verdicts)
                                                → Critical, not Medium.
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   [Fix A — the real fix, S effort] In
                                                TriggerQueriesAsync call QueryUDPDetailedAsync and
                                                count dispatch success ONLY for answered statuses
                                                (Success/NoData/NxDomain/Refused/ServFail),
                                                mirroring macOS recordsOrThrow semantics — Timeout /
                                                ResponseIdMismatch / Malformed / TransportError /
                                                Truncated ⇒ false. This resurrects the E007 guard.
                                                [Fix B — honesty, S] Rename the user-facing claim
                                                from "sent" to "answered" (or tri-state
                                                answered/no-answer/unknown): even a genuine answer
                                                only proves a responder exists, not delivery to the
                                                configured resolver — against an on-path adversary
                                                the collector attestation is the only delivery
                                                proof, and the copy should say so (user approval
                                                needed for wording). Validation: unit test with a
                                                stubbed detailed response of Status=Timeout for all
                                                servers asserting LeakVerdict.Inconclusive ("All DNS
                                                dispatches failed"), plus a mixed answered/timeout
                                                case; adversarial fixture where every query is
                                                answered locally but the collector attests zero
                                                observations must NOT produce NotDetected without a
                                                caveat.
                       - **Proposed Code**        [
                                                  // LeakDetector.cs:222-240 — count only ANSWERED statuses as dispatch success
                                                  var resp = await DNSResolver.QueryUDPDetailedAsync(query);
                                                  results[server] = resp.Status is DNSResponseStatus.Success
                                                      or DNSResponseStatus.NoData or DNSResponseStatus.NxDomain
                                                      or DNSResponseStatus.Refused or DNSResponseStatus.ServFail;
                                                ]

- **[C007]**            AuthoritativeVantage MajorityConsensus Accepts Single-Responder Data as
                         Unquestioned Ground Truth
- **Criticality:**      Critical (false-"secure" verdict: 2-of-3 bootstrap blockade → single-source
                         delegation accepted → attacker-supplied NS can meet AA quorum → `.matches`
                         rules out tampering); analysis 2026-07-09, upgraded per [syxx-researcher].
- **Location:**        macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/AuthoritativeVantage.swift:213 (majorityConsensus);
                         Windows/Syxx.Kit/AuthoritativeVantage.cs:164 (same)
- **Issue:**            `MajorityConsensus()` requires ≥2 agreeing resolvers. When only 1 resolver
                         responds (the other 2 are blocked by the network, e.g. a corporate firewall
                         blocking 8.8.8.8 and 9.9.9.9 while allowing 1.1.1.1), it returns the single
                        set unconditionally: `if (sets.Count == 1) return sets[0]`. An attacker who
                        can block 2 of 3 bootstrap resolvers can force single-responder fallback and
                        supply arbitrary delegation data through the remaining resolver path. Since
                        authoritative truth anchors the entire comparison chain (Mirror, Witness),
                        this degrades ground truth across all downstream verdicts.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** B012 (single bootstrap resolver, FIXED — this is the MajorityConsensus
                         quorum-degradation residual). C007 on both platforms.
- **Dependency:** B031 (ALL call sites still pass a single-element bootstrap array — ProbePlan.swift:109,
                         SyxxCLI.swift:239). C007 Fix 1 cannot land BEFORE B031, or the authoritative
                         probe goes permanently inconclusive from every current call site (silently
                         disabling the A2 datapoint). Order: B031 first, then C007.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] When `sets.Count == 1`, return an `inconclusive`/`uncertain` ground
                        truth state instead of accepting single-source data.
                        [Fix 2] Mark the authoritative comparison as `Degraded` when ground truth
                        is single-source.
                        [Fix 3] Log which resolver was the sole responder.

                       - **Tool Name**            [syxx-researcher]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-10

                       - **Disagree Basis**       N/A

                                                  correction for macOS. The defect is NOT in

                                                  even says "otherwise returns the (only) set"),

                                                  cite is exact: AuthoritativeVantage.cs:164 `if
                                                  (sets.Count == 1) return sets[0];`. Not a duplicate:

                                                  consensus exists only because of it) and B011 added
                                                  the AA-answer quorum (.swift:116-122, .cs:81-88);
                                                  C007 is the degradation residual both left open —
                                                  when 2 of 3 bootstraps are blocked, the ENTIRE
                                                  delegation (NS hosts, then NS IPs via the
                                                  union loop .swift:91-99) is single-sourced, and the
                                                  B011 quorum is then satisfiable by ≥2
                                                  attacker-supplied NS IPs agreeing with each other.

- **[E013]**            Windows IPClassifier Misclassifies 198.18.0.0/15 as PrivateUse
- **Criticality:**      Low (blocking behavior correct; classification label wrong); analysis
                        2026-07-09.
- **Location:**        Windows/Syxx.Kit/IPClassifier.cs:65
- **Issue:**            198.18.0.0/15 (RFC 2544 Benchmarking) is mapped to `IPAddressClass.PrivateUse`.
                        `IsBlockingAnswer` correctly treats `PrivateUse` as blocking, so no false
                        verdict arises, but the misclassification degrades evidence provenance
                        accuracy. macOS classifies this range differently.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Residual of B025 (192.0.0.0/24 and 192.88.99.0/24 were fixed; 198.18.0.0/15
                        was not).
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Add `IPAddressClass.Benchmarking` and map 198.18.0.0/15 to it (or
                        map to `Reserved`).
- **Tag:**              OBSERVED (workflow agent).

                       - **Tool Name**            [syxx-researcher]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-10
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Disagree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       Ground 2 (wrong basis) — the entry's factual
                                                  premise "macOS classifies this range differently"
                                                  is FALSE. macOS IPClassifier.swift:64 is
                                                  byte-for-byte the same policy: `if ip[0] == 198 &&
                                                  ip[1] == 18 { return .privateUse } // 198.18.0.0/15
                                                  (benchmarking)` — the PrivateUse mapping is
                                                  deliberate, paritous, and blocking-correct on both
                                                  platforms; neither platform has a `Benchmarking`
                                                  class to map to. As filed, this is a cosmetic
                                                  label-provenance nit, not a platform delta.
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   Retarget the entry at the REAL defect sitting on
                                                  the very lines cited, present on BOTH platforms:
                                                  the check `ip[1] == 18` covers only 198.18.0.0/16.
                                                  RFC 2544's benchmarking block is 198.18.0.0/15 =
                                                  198.18.0.0–198.19.255.255, so every 198.19.x.x
                                                  address falls through the remaining branches
                                                  (IPClassifier.cs:66-70; IPClassifier.swift:65-69)
                                                  to PublicRoutable → `IsBlockingAnswer` returns
                                                  false → a resolver sinkholing to 198.19.x is
                                                  scored as a normal public answer: missed
                                                  blocking/redirection detection, quick-guide #2 →
                                                  criticality should be raised from Low to
                                                  Critical-track (High minimum). Real-world trigger:
                                                  198.18.0.0/15 is the standard fake-IP pool for
                                                  transparent-proxy/VPN clients (Clash, Surge) and
                                                  appears in enterprise filter sinkholes; an
                                                  interceptor choosing the upper /16 evades the
                                                  classifier on both platforms today. CONFIRMED by
                                                  code read; not executed. Since the defect is
                                                  identical on both platforms it is a B-domain
                                                  (verdict integrity) issue wearing an E number —
                                                  acceptable to fix in place with a note. Cross-ref
                                                  B025 (its 198.18 line inherited the same /16
                                                  truncation when ported).

                                                    // Windows/Syxx.Kit/IPClassifier.cs:65 (same fix at

                                                    if (ip[0] == 198 && (ip[1] == 18 || ip[1] == 19))

- **[B031]**            Refactor Call Sites Pass a SINGLE Bootstrap Resolver — Defeats the B012 Multi-Bootstrap Consensus Fix
- **Criticality:**      Critical (can cause false confidence; regresses a delta already marked
                        FIXED). Authoritative delegation anchors the highest-weight evidence
                        (`authoritativeDiverges` / `authoritativeDivergesConfirmed`).
- **Location:**         ALL FOUR FRONTENDS: macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/ProbePlan.swift:103-110
                        (`bootstrapResolvers: [trustedBootstrap]`); Windows/Syxx.Kit/ProbePlan.cs:105-110
                        (same single-element array); macOS/Sources/SyxxCLI/SyxxCLI.swift:237-240;
                        Windows/Syxx/Program.cs:260-262. GUIs route through ProbePlan: macOS
                        AppModel.swift:259, Windows AppViewModel.cs:135/162/183. Sink:
                        macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/AuthoritativeVantage.swift:211-213 (`guard sets.count >= 2
                        else { return sets[0] }`); Windows/Syxx.Kit/AuthoritativeVantage.cs equivalent.
- **Issue:**            B012's fix defaulted `AuthoritativeVantage.compare` to a 3-resolver bootstrap
                        set with majority consensus (≥2 agreeing) so one poisoned/blocked resolver
                        cannot control the NS delegation set. The new shared `ProbePlan.runMirror`
                        and BOTH CLIs override that default with a ONE-element array
                        (`localResolver == "1.1.1.1" ? "9.9.9.9" : "1.1.1.1"`). With a single
                        bootstrap, `majorityConsensus` degenerates to "return the only set" — consensus
                        can never engage even on a clean network — and NS→IP resolution is single-
                        sourced. An attacker who poisons the one chosen bootstrap steers the
                        "authoritative" ground truth. The macOS GUI now routes through ProbePlan
                        (`AppModel.swift:259`), so it is affected too.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** B012 (FIXED — this is a working-tree regression that silently undoes it at the
                        call site). Distinct from C007: C007 is the FUNCTION accepting single-responder
                        data when the network blocks 2 of 3; this is the CALLERS supplying only 1 by
                        construction, so consensus never engages even on a clean network. Checked
                        DELTAS.md A–F, DELTAS-fixed.md, SERVER_DELTAS.md — not a duplicate.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Pass the full 3-resolver default (or the default set minus the
                        resolver-under-test, still ≥2) from `ProbePlan.runMirror` and both CLIs.
                        [Fix 2] Guard `AuthoritativeVantage.compare` to treat a `<2`-element
                        `bootstrapResolvers` as `.inconclusive`/`.degraded` rather than silently
                        single-sourcing (overlaps C007 Fix 1).
- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED (call sites and consensus fallthrough read directly, both platforms).

- **[B032]**            macOS Infers "Encrypted DNS = yes (DoH/DoT)" From a VPN/Tunnel Interface — False Clean Transport Signal
- **Criticality:**      High (false confidence / missed detection). A hostile VPN/transparent-proxy
                        tunnel — the interception adversary Syxx targets — is turned into a CLEAN
                        transport signal.
- **Location:**         macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/NetworkKeyState.swift:387-393 (tunnel branch →
                        `EncryptedDNSStatus(state: .yes, "…tunneled through VPN interface(s)…")`),
                        :401-402 (`isDNSEncrypted()` now returns `state == .yes`); consumer
                        macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/Synthesis/Synthesizer.swift:360-372 (`.dnsEncrypted`
                        → `.negative` clean sub-signal); macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/Trust/Sentinel.swift:29.
- **Issue:**            Three defects in one change. (a) Mislabel: a resolver merely on a
                        `utun`/`ppp`/`ipsec`/`wg` interface is reported `.yes` with the user-visible
                        string "System DNS is encrypted (DoH/DoT)" — but a tunnel does not imply
                        DoH/DoT; the DNS inside may be plain Do53 and the tunnel endpoint may be the
                        tamperer. (b) False-confidence dampener: `.yes` emits a `.negative` (clean)
                        sub-signal in the DST engine, so a malicious VPN earns a clean transport
                        verdict that structurally suppresses the on-path/interception frame. (c)
                        Conservative-default regression: `isDNSEncrypted()` previously returned a
                        hardcoded `false` ("to prevent false security claims") and now returns `true`
                        off the tunnel heuristic, feeding Sentinel and `resolveSecurely`. The explicit
                        `scutil` Protocol=DoH/DoT branch (:375-385) is sound; only the tunnel inference
                        and the `isDNSEncrypted()` default are the problem.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** E014 (ex-E009) records the macOS-never-yes vs Windows-yes divergence and its
                        Fix explicitly recommends the SAFER direction — report `.unknown` unless DoH is
                        confirmed. This working-tree change moved macOS the OPPOSITE way (yes on a
                        weaker signal than Windows' registry template), so it is a new, distinct defect,
                        not the tracked parity item. Not a duplicate of B009/B021. SCOPE: macOS-only
                        (Windows NetworkKeyState.cs was not modified and has no tunnel heuristic), so
                        this also WIDENS the E014 divergence — macOS now reports `.yes` on two signals
                        (scutil Protocol OR tunnel interface) while Windows reports `.yes` only on a
                        registry DoH template: three different truth conditions for the same claim.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Return `.unknown` (not `.yes`) for the tunnel-interface case, or
                        downgrade its synthesis sub-status to `.inconclusive`; reserve `.yes`/
                        `.dnsEncrypted` for the confirmed `scutil` DoH/DoT branch. [Fix 2] Revert
                        `isDNSEncrypted()` to derive only from the confirmed-protocol path. [Fix 3] Fix
                        the observation wording so it never says "DoH/DoT" for a tunnel (user-visible
                        string — needs User approval before implementation).
- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED (code paths + clean-signal wiring); LIKELY (end-to-end verdict-flip
                        magnitude, not executed).

- **[F006]**            ProbeRunner Timeout Is Cooperative-Only (No Wall-Clock Bound) + Budget Under-Count + Stale C006 Doc Reference
- **Criticality:**      Low (efficiency / resource; no false verdict). Recorded because the Efficiency
                        value mandates bounded behavior for interactive CLI use.
- **Location:**         macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/ProbeRunner.swift:46-73 (`withThrowingTaskGroup` +
                        `defer { group.cancelAll() }`); budget under-count :66-72 (`accountedDuration
                        = budget.perProbeTimeout` on timeout); doc cross-ref :6-11.
- **Issue:**            The timeout task returns `nil` after `perProbeTimeout`, but structured
                        concurrency drains the child before `run` returns and cancellation is
                        cooperative — `DNSResolver.queryUDPDetailed`'s retry loop does not check
                        `Task.isCancelled` (per the module's own doc, up to ~4s past timeout). So a
                        "timed-out" probe still blocks the section for the full real duration, while
                        budget accounting records only `perProbeTimeout` — under-counting `elapsed`, so
                        a section can overshoot `totalTimeout`. Separately, the doc's "follow-up delta
                        C006" reference is wrong: C006 in DELTAS.md is the 8.8.8.8-fallback delta, not
                        a cancellation item — a reader chasing it is misdirected.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Not in DELTAS.md/SERVER_DELTAS.md. E001 (unbounded LAN cartography, FIXED) is
                        a different component. Not a duplicate.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Add `Task.isCancelled`/cancellation checks to `DNSResolver`'s retry
                        loop so the timeout is enforced at the transport layer. [Fix 2] Account real
                        elapsed (floored at `perProbeTimeout`) rather than always the cap. [Fix 3]
                        Correct or drop the `C006` reference.
- **Tag:**              LIKELY (structured-concurrency draining reasoned from code + the module's own
                        doc admission; not executed).

- **[F007]**            `DomainCanonical` "Every Domain Must Pass Through Here" Contract Is Unenforced — Only DimensionClient Uses It
- **Criticality:**      Low (Honesty §5 premature-abstraction / dead-contract; no false verdict — DNS
                        is case-insensitive on the wire and client comparisons are IP-based).
- **Location:**         macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/DomainCanonical.swift:3-11 (doc contract), :35 (length
                        guard); sole callers macOS DimensionClient.swift:86,94 and Windows
                        DimensionClient.cs:73,98. Raw domains flow uncanonicalized through
                        ProbePlan.runProphet/runMirror (ProbePlan.swift:24,84) and both CLIs.
- **Issue:**            The module header claims "every domain that enters the system must pass through
                        here so that `Example.com`, `example.com.`, `xn--…` are treated as one key," but
                        it is invoked only inside DimensionClient (the C004 fix). User input reaches DNS
                        queries, vantage comparison, and authoritative comparison without
                        canonicalization — the abstraction exists but its stated invariant is not
                        enforced. Also: the length guard (:35) measures pre-IDNA UTF-8 bytes, not the
                        encoded A-label length, so IDN names are mis-measured either way.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Not in any ledger. C004 (DimensionClient decode, FIXED) is the one place this is
                        used; this is the unenforced-contract residual. Not a duplicate.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Canonicalize at the ProbePlan/CLI entry boundary, OR downgrade the doc
                        claim to "used at the Dimension boundary." [Fix 2] Measure length on the encoded
                        A-label, not the pre-IDNA UTF-8 string.
- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED (grep-verified sole callers on both platforms).

- **[A019]**            Stripe `pending-mint` Idempotency Burns Webhook Retries After Keygen Outage
- **Criticality:**      Critical (paid customer can be charged but never receive a license after a
                        transient Keygen/mail path failure; retry path collapses to "duplicate" instead
                        of retrying fulfillment); analysis 2026-07-10.
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/fulfillment.py:73-95
- **Issue:**            Checkout fulfillment reserves `stripe_evt:<event_id>` as `"processing"` before
                        minting the Keygen license (`fulfillment.py:78,84`). If `_keygen_create_license`
                        fails or returns no key, the handler records `"pending-mint"` at :93-95 and
                        returns success-ish application state. On Stripe's later retry of the same event,
                        the first branch sees the existing `stripe_evt:` key and returns `"duplicate"`
                        at :78-79, so the mint is not retried. That turns a transient dependency outage
                        into a permanent paid-license delivery failure.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Same failure class as `Server/SERVER_DELTAS.md` SD-11; not previously present
                        as a main `DELTAS.md` entry. Distinct from A013: `kv_insert_once` stops duplicate
                        minting, but here it also prevents retrying a known-unfinished mint.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Treat `"pending-mint"` as retryable: if the idempotency key exists with
                        pending state, retry/reconcile rather than returning duplicate. [Fix 2] Mark a
                        Stripe event final only after a license is minted and customer mapping is stored.
                        [Fix 3] Return a retriable failure to Stripe or enqueue a reconciliation job when
                        Keygen is unavailable.
- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED (source-read; no live Stripe/Keygen run performed).

                                                  `stripe_evt:<id>` via `kv_insert_once(..., "processing")` (:78); on Keygen
                                                  failure `key` is falsy, :94 `kv_set(...,"pending-mint")`, :95 returns
                                                  "pending-mint". On Stripe's retry of the SAME event, :78
                                                  `kv_insert_once` fails (key already exists) → `not False` → returns
                                                  "duplicate" at :79, so `_keygen_create_license` is never retried. A
                                                  transient dependency outage becomes a permanent paid-license delivery

- **[A020]**            Server DNS Oracle Accepts Wrong-Question and Off-Source UDP Replies as Evidence
- **Criticality:**      Critical (server-side clean-vantage / authoritative ground truth can be poisoned
                        by a packet that only matches TXID+QR, undermining `/api/authoritative`,
                        `/api/diff`, `/api/trace`, and `/api/investigate` evidence); analysis
                        2026-07-10.
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/resolver.py:98-126,146-158,304-321,324-348
- **Issue:**            The server resolver validates transaction ID and QR bit, but never verifies that
                        the echoed question name/type/class matches the query. `_parse_response` skips the
                        question section without comparing it to the requested name/type
                        (`resolver.py:109-112`), and `_parse_sections` does the same for iterative

                        reply that guesses the TXID can be parsed as recursive or authoritative evidence
                        even if it answered a different question or came from a different peer.

                        response questions (`DNSResolver.swift:289-297,358-363`;

                        divergent ground truth.

- **[A021]**            Server Paid-Route Entitlement Trusts Unsigned Keygen `meta.valid` JSON
- **Criticality:**      High (server-side Pro entitlement is a TLS-only online boolean; a compromised
                        server trust store, pinned-proxy deployment, or Keygen-path hijack can forge paid
                        access to collector/ground-truth routes); analysis 2026-07-10.
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/licensing.py:101-132
- **Issue:**            `_validate_keygen` POSTs the supplied license key to Keygen and returns `"pro"`
                        solely from `meta.valid` in the JSON response (`licensing.py:118-132`). The server
                        does distinguish transient Keygen failures from invalid keys, which is good
                        tri-state behavior, but the accepted entitlement itself is not signed or verified
                        against a Keygen public key/offline license artifact. The paid server routes
                        therefore inherit the network/TLS trust boundary rather than a cryptographic
                        license-verification boundary.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Related to D003's client-side TLS-pinning note for Keygen/collector calls, but
                        distinct: this is the server's authorization decision for paid API routes, not a
                        client display or transport-pinning gap.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Verify a signed Keygen license artifact or signed validation response
                        before granting server-side Pro entitlement. [Fix 2] If Keygen cannot provide a
                        verifiable artifact, pin the Keygen service identity and cache only bounded,
                        auditable positive entitlements. [Fix 3] Treat unverifiable validation as
                        transient/unknown, not as a trustworthy paid-route authorization.
- **Tag:**              FIXED (Opencode 2026-07-11). Implemented Ed25519 response signature verification
                        (A021 Fix 1) — see below for evaluator notes.

                       - **Date**                 2026-07-10

                       - **Disagree Basis**       Confirmed live at licensing.py:101-132. `_validate_keygen` returns
                                                  `"pro" if meta.get("valid") else None` (:131-132) purely from the
                                                  unsigned JSON body. The tri-state handling is genuinely good — transient
                                                  HTTP/network failures return `"__transient__"` (:106,:124-125,:127-128),
                                                  401/404 return None (:122-123) — so this is NOT a false-clean-on-timeout
                                                  bug; it is a trust-boundary hardening gap: the entitlement rides TLS/

                                                   1. Captures raw response body + `Keygen-Signature`, `Digest`, `Date`
                                                      headers from the validate-key response.

                                                      key from the Keygen dashboard), verifies the Ed25519 signature
                                                      over reconstructed signing data `(request-target) | host | date |

                                                   3. Only trusts `meta.valid` if the signature verifies. Missing/
                                                      malformed/invalid signature → `None` (denial), never `"pro"`.
                                                   4. When `KEYGEN_PUBLIC_KEY` is empty (dev/test), skips verification

                                                  The tri-state transient/error path is unchanged (401/404 → None,

- **[A022]**            Ephemeral Collector Signing Key on Restart Silently Orphans All Attestations
- **Criticality:**      Critical (collector Ed25519 attestations become unverifiable after any server
                        restart, and would permanently break D011's client-side pinned collector pubkey;
                        auto-critical — unverifiable/forgeable evidence). Confirmed 2026-07-10.
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/leak.py:44-66 (`_ensure_collector_key`)
- **Issue:**            When `SYXX_COLLECTOR_PRIVATE_KEY` is unset, `_ensure_collector_key()` generates a
                        fresh in-memory Ed25519 key at startup and only logs a warning; the key is never
                        persisted. On every restart a new key is generated, silently invalidating all
                        prior collector attestations and breaking any client that has pinned the collector
                        public key (WS3.1 / D011). Evidence appears valid but is cryptographically
                        orphaned, with no user-visible error.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Hard blocker for D011's collector-pinning half; related to A006 (Ed25519 leak
                        attestation, CF-01). Surfaced as Appendix-B of HANDOFF-OPENCODE.md during WS3.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Fail closed: if `SYXX_COLLECTOR_PRIVATE_KEY` is unset in a non-dev run,
                        refuse to start (exit with a clear error) rather than minting an ephemeral key.
                        [Fix 2] Alternatively persist a generated key to disk (e.g. `/var/lib/syxx/
                        collector_key`) with 0600 perms; fail-closed is preferred for a trust anchor.
                        [Fix 3] Expose a stable key id so clients can detect deliberate rotation.
- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED (source-read, independently verified 2026-07-10; Claude-verified).

                       - **Tool Name**            [syxx-researcher]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-10
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree (defect was real) — FIXED. MOVE-TO-FIXED.
                       - **Disagree Basis**       Not a disagreement. Fix 1 (fail-closed) landed at commit f2861b5 and is
                                                  live in leak.py:44-80: with `SYXX_COLLECTOR_PRIVATE_KEY` unset and no
                                                  `SYXX_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL_COLLECTOR_KEY=1` escape, `_ensure_collector_key()`
                                                  raises RuntimeError (:67-77) instead of minting an ephemeral key. The
                                                  ephemeral branch (:57-66) is now a documented dev/test-only escape.
                                                  Fix 3 (stable key id) also present: `_COLLECTOR_KEY_ID` at :80. Fix 2
                                                  (persist-to-disk) intentionally NOT taken — the delta itself preferred
                                                  fail-closed, so this is complete. Caveat: commit note records the Ed25519
                                                  path was not runtime-exercised (`cryptography` absent in that sandbox);
                                                  the fail-closed raise IS the load-bearing behavior and is verifiable by
                                                  inspection.
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   MOVE-TO-FIXED citing f2861b5 (fail-closed, A022 Fix 1). Recommend one
                                                  runtime confirmation on a host with `cryptography` installed before final
                                                  sign-off, per §2 real-run primacy.

                        WS1 regression baseline.

- **[B036]**            AuthoritativeVantage Tests Lock In `Both Empty == Matches` Without Encoding the
                        Required Evidence Premise
- **Criticality:**      High (missing resolver/authority evidence can be treated as a clean consistency
                        signal; tests pass because they assert the softened behavior directly). Static
                        test audit 2026-07-10.
- **Location:**         macOS/Tests/SyxxKitTests/AuthoritativeVantageTests.swift:60-63
                        (`testMatchesWhenBothEmpty`);
                        macOS/Tests/SyxxKitTests/AuthoritativeVantageTests.swift:114-115
                        (`testClassifyDirect` asserts empty resolver/auth sets are `.matches`);
                        Windows/Syxx.Tests/SyxxKitTests.cs:1425-1429
                        (`ClassifyMatchesWhenBothEmpty`).
- **Issue:**            The classifier receives only answer sets, not the recursive resolver's status or
                        the authoritative response status. The tests nevertheless assert `.matches` when
                        both sets are empty. That assertion can only be safe if both sides are known,
                        parsed, validated negative answers; the test does not encode or verify that
                        premise. If a timeout, parse failure, delegation failure, or skipped resolver probe
                        is collapsed upstream to an empty answer set, these tests still pass while the
                        product converts "no evidence" into "consistent with ground truth."
- **Missing Failure
  Case(s):**            [1] Add a production-path test where the resolver side has no usable evidence
                        (timeout/transport error/parse failure) and authoritative no-data exists; expected
                        status must be `.inconclusive`, not `.matches`. [2] If "both authoritative no-data
                        and recursive no-data" is intentionally clean, model that as an explicit typed
                        negative-evidence input rather than a bare empty set, and add a failure case proving
                        empty-from-failure cannot reach `.matches`. [3] Keep the existing positive case
                        only after the required negative-evidence premise is visible in the API and test.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Related to B011/C007/B031's "ground truth before evidence" family, but this is a
                        current test assertion that preserves an empty-evidence clean match.
- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED (static test audit; no network-dependent tests run).

- **[B037]**            WitnessSigner Display-Integrity Guard Omits `resolverQueryOutcomes` — Tampered
                        Per-Resolver Display Verifies as Authentic
- **Criticality:**      Critical (forgeable evidence: a witness snapshot whose displayed per-resolver
                        outcomes were altered can still verify true); user to be made aware.
- **Location:**         macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/WitnessSigner.swift (verifySnapshot display-integrity
                        guard); Windows twin `Windows/Syxx.Kit/WitnessSigner.cs`.
- **Issue:**            The guard re-projects the display fields into a `SignedEvidencePayload` and
                        compares `rebuilt.queryId == evidence.queryId` and `rebuilt.comparisonResult ==
                        evidence.comparisonResult`, but does NOT compare `resolverQueryOutcomes`. The
                        signed evidence includes `resolverQueryOutcomes` (they are in `canonicalBytes()`),
                        so the Ed25519 check protects the SIGNED copy — but a mismatch between the
                        DISPLAYED per-resolver outcomes (`snapshot.comparison`) and the signed evidence
                        is unchecked. An attacker who alters a displayed per-resolver answer while the
                        aggregate verdict/answer-sets stay equal passes both the guard and the signature,
                        so a viewer sees tampered per-resolver evidence marked "authentic".
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Exposed by the missing witness corrupt-signature / display-coverage tests
                        (see B034-B036 audit cluster). E011/D015 landed the canonical DTO + guard.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Add `rebuilt.resolverQueryOutcomes == evidence.resolverQueryOutcomes`
                        to the guard on both platforms. [Fix 2] Add a §3 test: tamper one displayed
                        per-resolver outcome (verdict/sets unchanged) → verifySnapshot must return false.
- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED (source-read both platforms; no forged-snapshot run performed).

- **[B038]**            DualStack Renders `ipv4Suppressed` Censorship Signal on an A-Record TIMEOUT —
                        Failure Rendered as a Verdict (§1 Violation)
- **Criticality:**      Critical (a missing datum — A query timeout/transport failure — is reported as a
                        selective-IPv4-blocking/censorship signal; §1 "a failure must never render as a
                        verdict"); user to be made aware.
- **Location:**         macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/DualStackProbe.swift (`classify`, the
                        `aaaaOk && !aOk → .ipv4Suppressed` branch); Windows twin `DualStackProbe.cs`.
- **Issue:**            `classify` sets `aOk = aStatus == .success && !aAddrs.isEmpty`, then the guard
                        passes when `aaaaOk` is true, and `if aaaaOk && !aOk` returns `.ipv4Suppressed`
                        ("AAAA resolves but A does not — corroborate for selective blocking"). `!aOk`
                        conflates a GENUINE negative (`nxDomain`/`noData`) with a FAILURE
                        (`timeout`/`transportError`/`servFail`). So an A-query that timed out while AAAA
                        works is classified as a censorship-leaning signal instead of inconclusive — a
                        verdict on a missing datum. Only the `aOk && aaaaDenied` path checks for a genuine
                        negative; the suppression path does not.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Exposed by the missing DualStack failure-path test (audit set 1, offender #1).
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Gate `.ipv4Suppressed` on a GENUINE A negative (`aDenied`), i.e.
                        `aaaaOk && aDenied → .ipv4Suppressed`; a non-negative A failure with AAAA ok →
                        `.inconclusive` ("A did not resolve — transport failure, cannot audit"). [Fix 2]
                        Add a §3 test: A `.timeout` + AAAA success → `.inconclusive`, never
                        `.ipv4Suppressed`. Port to Windows.
- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED (source-read `classify`; no live dual-stack run performed).

- **[C009]**            Exfil Analyzer Flags a Benign Domain as `suspicious` — Possible False Positive
- **Criticality:**      High if confirmed (a false 'DNS exfiltration/tunnelling' signal on ordinary
                        traffic erodes trust and could mislead a verdict); UNVERIFIED. Observed
                        2026-07-10.
- **Location:**         macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/Forensics/ExfilAnalyzer.swift (classification →
                        `ExfilSuspicion`); observed via MonitorReportAnalyzerTests fixture.
- **Issue:**            While strengthening `testHighEntropyTunnelDomainIsAssessed`, a benign
                        co-domain in the fixture (from `benignRecords()`) came back with
                        `suspicion == .suspicious`. Either the entropy/label heuristic over-flags an
                        ordinary domain (a real efficacy false positive) OR the fixture contains a
                        domain that legitimately trips the heuristic. Not root-caused (did not
                        rabbit-hole, per instruction).
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Surfaced during the §3 test audit sweep. Related to the exfil/tunnelling
                        datapoint.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Reproduce: dump the flagged benign domain + its entropy/label metrics;
                        confirm whether it's a heuristic over-trigger or a fixture artifact. [Fix 2] If
                        a real FP, tighten the threshold / require corroboration (beacon cadence +
                        entropy + blocklist) before `.suspicious`; add a fixed benign-domain
                        false-positive regression test.
- **Tag:**              OBSERVED (test-fixture; not reproduced against real capture).

                       - **Tool Name**            [syxx-researcher]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-10
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree — STAY-OPEN, and UPGRADE from OBSERVED to CONFIRMED (root-caused).
                       - **Disagree Basis**       REPRODUCED and root-caused by source read (build is currently broken by
                                                  B033, so run-verification was not possible; this is a deterministic code
                                                  trace, not a live capture). Root cause is TWO-fold:
                                                  (1) FIXTURE ARTIFACT: every record in `benignRecords()` is stamped with
                                                    the SAME hardcoded timestamp "2026-07-06 12:00:00.000"
                                                    (MonitorReportAnalyzerTests.swift:18). For the benign domain
                                                    "example.com" the 12 identical timestamps produce 11 inter-arrival
                                                    intervals all equal to 0 → BeaconAnalyzer.score: `mean = 0`,
                                                    `cv = mean == 0 ? 0 : …` = 0 (BeaconAnalyzer.swift:53), and
                                                    `classification(for: 0)` → `cv < 0.05` → `.highlyRegular` (:66). So
                                                    `regular = true` in ExfilAnalyzer.
                                                  (2) REAL DESIGN FALSE-POSITIVE (the substantive part): "example.com" has
                                                    only two labels → `longestSubdomainLabel` returns "" → entropy 0 →
                                                    `highEntropy = false`. Yet ExfilAnalyzer flags
                                                    `else if highEntropy || regular { suspicion = .suspicious }`
                                                    (ExfilAnalyzer.swift:80-81). So `.suspicious` fires on CADENCE ALONE,
                                                    with zero encoded-label signal and no blocklist hit. The module doc
                                                    (:3-6) claims it "fuses three signals into one honest verdict," but the
                                                    code fires on ANY ONE of {highEntropy, regular}. Regular cadence alone
                                                    is ubiquitous in benign traffic (OS/telemetry polling, keepalives, NTP),
                                                    so this is a genuine live FP class, not merely a fixture quirk.
                                                  Secondary defect: BeaconAnalyzer treating identical/zero-mean timestamps
                                                  as the STRONGEST regularity (`.highlyRegular`) is a §6 degenerate-input
                                                  problem — coincident events carry no cadence signal and should be
                                                  `.insufficientData`, not maximal regularity.
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   UPGRADE to CONFIRMED, criticality High (real efficacy FP). Add fixes:
                                                  [Fix A] Do not emit `.suspicious` on `regular` alone — require corroboration
                                                    (regular + high-entropy, or regular + blocklist, or high-entropy alone
                                                    since an encoded label is itself strong). Single-signal `regular` should
                                                    be `.inconclusive`, not `.suspicious`.
                                                  [Fix B] BeaconAnalyzer: map zero-mean / identical-timestamp series to
                                                    `.insufficientData`, not `.highlyRegular` (BeaconAnalyzer.swift:53,65-68).
                                                  [Fix C] Fix the fixture to use distinct, realistic timestamps so
                                                    `benignRecords()` does not manufacture a zero-variance cadence
                                                    (MonitorReportAnalyzerTests.swift:18) — and add a fixed benign-domain
                                                    FP regression test asserting example.com → `.benign`/`.inconclusive`,
                                                    never `.suspicious`.
                                                  Fix A is the load-bearing efficacy fix; Fixes B/C harden the input and lock
                                                  the regression. Note: NX/blocklist `matches` was not exercised (SieveBlocklist
                                                  bundled lists) — the trigger here is purely the cadence path.

- **[D017]**            Windows `DatapointBag.Merge` Uses an Empty Separator Where macOS Uses U+0001 —
                        Section-Attribution Key Can Collide (Parity Divergence)
- **Criticality:**      Non-critical (fixed key set makes a live collision unlikely today); a latent
                        mis-attribution + a silent macOS/Windows parity drift of the exact class
                        AGENTS.md warns about. User to be made aware.
- **Location:**         Windows/Syxx.Kit/Synthesis/Report.cs:36 and :44 (`d.Key + "" + d.Value`);
                        macOS parity at Report.swift:50 and :57 (`d.key + "\u{1}" + d.value`).
- **Issue:**            macOS deliberately joins key and value with the U+0001 control char to build
                        the section-attribution lookup key, precisely so a (key,value) pair cannot be
                        confused with a different pair whose concatenation happens to match. Windows
                        drops the separator entirely (`+ "" +`), so `sectionsByKeyValue` is keyed on
                        the raw concatenation `Key+Value`. Two distinct (key,value) pairs whose
                        concatenations are equal would mis-merge their reporting-section lists. With
                        today's fixed key set (`local_resolver`, `target_answer`, `dns_encryption`,
                        `vpn`, `captive_portal`, `dnssec`, `observed_resolver`) no such collision is
                        reachable, so it is not currently a wrong-output bug — but it is a real
                        divergence from the macOS contract and a fragile foundation the moment a new
                        key or a colon-free value is added, and it belongs on record as a parity defect.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Surfaced during the B040-B042 report-layer audit; independent of them.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Use the same U+0001 (or any non-value byte) separator on Windows:
                        `d.Key + "" + d.Value` at both :36 and :44. [Fix 2] §3 parity test: two
                        datapoints crafted so `Key+Value` concatenations collide but the (key,value)
                        pairs differ → their sections must NOT merge; failure case: with the empty
                        separator the test detects the mis-merge.
- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED (source-read; separator divergence is direct in the two files).
- **[Reconcile note]**   Filed by the report agent as proposed-B043; moved to D017 (Platform Integration — parity/attribution, no live wrong-output).

                                                  control char to build the section-attribution

                        criticality rule 4; a leak submitter's resolver IP becomes cross-readable to
                        other users).
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/leak.py:119-121; Server/syxx_server/db.py:260-269;
                        Server/syxx_server/app.py:845-852
- **Issue:**            A leak submitter's resolver IP is mirrored into the shared `passive_dns`
                        index, survives the one-time `consume()`, is cross-readable by any caller of
                        `/api/passive-dns` (no ownership check), and is kept 30 days — a
                        PII/deanonymization leak that lets an unrelated user read the resolver IPs
                        of others' leak tests.

- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Do not mirror leak-zone observations into the passive index (or
                        namespace them non-queryable).

                        [Fix 3] Ownership-gate `/api/passive-dns` for leak zones.

                        resolver even when the authoritative walk is inconclusive — false-secure
                        under shared-upstream poisoning, where the first resolver to answer may be
                        the poisoned one.

- **[A030]**            /api/investigate Queries RRSIG With EDNS DO=0 — Signed Zones Always Reported
                        "unsigned"
- **Criticality:**      Non-critical (High); a detection feature that is structurally always-false
                        (server twin of the client DO-bit bug B046).
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/investigate.py:117-135;
                        Server/syxx_server/resolver.py:55-60
- **Issue:**            `/api/investigate` queries `TYPE=RRSIG` directly with EDNS DO=0, so
                        resolvers return no RRSIG and signed zones are reported "unsigned." The
                        DNSSEC-status feature is structurally always-false. This is the SAME
                        systemic EDNS-DO-bit-never-set bug as the client path B046, in a second code
                        path.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Systemic twin of B046 (client DNSResolver DO bit) — file both, cross-
                        referenced.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Set EDNS0 OPT DO=1.
                        [Fix 2] Read RRSIG from the covering-type query's answer/authority section
                        rather than a bare RRSIG query.
- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED (code) / systemic with B046

                       - **Tool Name**            [Claude]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-11
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       N/A
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   CONFIRMED by source verification of B046 — the
                                                  macOS `DNSResolver.swift:418-423` explicitly comments
                                                  "no DO bit" and sets the OPT flags to all zeros.
                                                  A030 is the server-side twin of the same structural
                                                  bug. The "DNSSEC-status feature is structurally
                                                  always-false" claim is correct — with DO=0, real
                                                  resolvers MUST strip RRSIGs per RFC 4035 §3.2.1.
                                                  Fix 2 (query the covering type with DO=1 and extract
                                                  RRSIG from the answer section) is more correct than
                                                  Fix 1 alone (a bare RRSIG type query is non-standard
                                                  and not widely supported). Both A030 and B046 should
                                                  be fixed together. Recommend the same commit touches
                                                  both paths.
                       - **Tool Name**            [Syxx-Researcher]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-11
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Disagree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       This path explicitly asks QTYPE=RRSIG
                                                  (`investigate.py:117-125`). Absence of DO does not
                                                  source-prove that an explicit RRSIG query always
                                                  returns empty. No real-resolver run is recorded, so
                                                  "structurally always-false" is unsupported.
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   Downgrade A030 to INFERRED pending a production
                                                  real-resolver run. A full validator should use
                                                  covering-type queries carrying DO=1 and parse the
                                                  answer/authority RRSIGs; adding DO to the existing
                                                  bare-RRSIG query alone is not proof of correctness.


                       - **Tool Name**            [Codex]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-13
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       _dnssec_observed directly queries DNSKEY/RRSIG
                                                  through _build_query, whose packet has no OPT/DO
                                                  record at
                                                  Server/syxx_server/investigate.py:117-135 and
                                                  resolver.py:55-60. Presence results are
                                                  structurally unreliable.
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   Use an EDNS(0) OPT RR with DO=1 or a validating
                                                  resolver API; preserve unknown when DNSSEC
                                                  material cannot be requested.

                       - **Tool Name**            [Claude]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-13
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       Confirmed: _dnssec_observed (investigate.py:117-135)
                                                  queries TYPE_DNSKEY/TYPE_RRSIG via _query_vantage;
                                                  the UDP path resolver.query -> _build_query
                                                  (resolver.py:55-60) emits no OPT/DO. The loop
                                                  RETURNS on the first non-erroring vantage; system
                                                  vantage raises for non-A/AAAA (query_system), so
                                                  the first UDP vantage answers with DNSKEY present
                                                  but RRSIG stripped (no DO) -> observed = has_dnskey
                                                  and has_rrsig = False; DoH vantages that would carry
                                                  RRSIG are never reached. Rebut earlier
                                                  Syxx-Researcher: RFC 4035 §3.2.1 requires a
                                                  validating recursive to strip RRSIG without DO, so
                                                  the "always-false" claim holds in the common
                                                  UDP-reachable case. Systemic twin of B046.
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   Set EDNS0 DO=1; better, read RRSIG from the
                                                  covering-type answer/authority rather than a bare
                                                  RRSIG query. "structurally always-false" is
                                                  marginally strong (a UDP-blocked, DoH-only network
                                                  could observe correctly) but directionally right.
                                                  Fix jointly with B046. Priority: high.

                        macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/Synthesis/Synthesizer.swift:379-385

                        interception_transport positive, with no connectivity control. Being offline

                        interception signal from ordinary connectivity loss.

                        EncryptedTransportProbe.{swift,cs}: `classify` gains `controlSucceeded`;
                        `probe` runs a cleartext Do53 control when DoH does not clearly succeed.
                        timeout/transportError → `.blocked` only if control succeeds, else
                        `.inconclusive` (offline / provider down never manufactures a block).

- **[B062]**            combine() Checks .positive Before .invalidated — Invalidated Premise Can
                        Still Read .positive

                        positive verdict.

- **Issue:**            `combine()` checks `.positive` before `.invalidated`, so an invalidated-
                        premise section can still read `.positive` and drive a verdict, rather than
                        the invalidation taking precedence.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Precedence ordering; related to B060.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Decide precedence (invalidation should win) or surface the conflict
                        explicitly.

                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       N/A
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   SOURCE VERIFIED. Synthesizer.swift:57-58 checks
                                                  `subs.contains(.positive)` BEFORE the `.invalidated`
                                                  check at line 61. This means an `.invalidated`
                                                  sub-signal can be overridden by a `.positive` from
                                                  the same section — the invalidation never fires if
                                                  any positive is present. Low criticality is correct
                                                  (no known current scenario where this produces a
                                                  wrong verdict, but the precedence ordering is
                                                  logically wrong). The fix (decide that `.invalidated`
                                                  should win over `.positive`) requires a design
                                                  decision: in most cases an invalidated premise should
                                                  take precedence because it means the evidence cannot
                                                  be trusted, but this could suppress legitimate
                                                  positive findings. Recommend surfacing the conflict
                                                  explicitly rather than silently resolving it.

- **[B065]**            Truncated DNS Replies Count as Successful / Clean Evidence in Both
                        Synthesis Adapters
- **Criticality:**      Critical; user made aware. An incomplete reply can become a negative
                        (clean) Prophet sub-verdict and can misclassify DNSSEC/EDNS posture instead
                        of making the component inconclusive.
- **Location:**         macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/DNSResolver.swift:179-187;
                        macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/Synthesis/Synthesizer.swift:77-88;
                        macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/DNSSECVerifier.swift:81-89;
                        macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/EDNS0Probe.swift:53-60;
                        Windows/Syxx.Kit/Synthesis/Synthesizer.cs:49-51, 88-99;
                        Windows/Syxx.Kit/DNSSECVerifier.cs:72-82, 100-104;
                        Windows/Syxx.Kit/EDNS0Probe.cs:30-39, 51-53
- **Issue:**            The shared DNS failure predicates omit `truncated`. On macOS,
                        `DNSResponse.didFail` returns false for `.truncated`; Windows repeats the
                        omission in `EvidenceAdapters.DidFail`, `DNSSECVerifier.Failed`, and probe-
                        local helpers. A `truncated` resolution therefore reaches the Prophet
                        adapter's default branch and contributes `.negative`, although the full
                        answer was never obtained. The same missing status makes an incomplete
                        DNSKEY/RRSIG exchange read `.unsigned` and an incomplete EDNS exchange read
                        `.notSupported`. This violates the no-verdict-before-evidence rule: TC=1
                        with failed TCP recovery must be invalidated/inconclusive, never clean or a
                        definitive capability result.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Related to E023, but not a duplicate. E023 addresses one cross-platform
                        zero-length TCP parsing case and its evaluator discusses
                        `ResolverQueryOutcome.didFail`; this delta concerns the separate
                        `DNSResponse`/adapter predicates used directly by Prophet, DNSSEC, EDNS,
                        ECS, VersionBind, OpenResolver, and canary paths on both platforms.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Define one canonical `DNSResponse` failure/usable-evidence
                        classification per platform and include `truncated` among failures.
                        [Fix 2] Remove the duplicated probe-local `DidFail` helpers and consume the
                        canonical typed classification.
                        [Fix 3] Add failure-path tests injecting `Truncated` into Prophet, DNSSEC,
                        and EDNS adapters; assert invalidated/inconclusive and ensure no negative,
                        unsigned, or not-supported conclusion is emitted.
- **Code Sample:**      [

                        // macOS DNSResolver.swift:181-187 — `.truncated` is omitted.
                        public var didFail: Bool {
                            switch status {
                            case .timeout, .transportError, .malformedResponse, .responseIdMismatch:
                                return true
                            default:
                                return false
                            }
                        }

                        // Windows Synthesizer.cs:49-51 — same omission feeds Prophet.
                        private static bool DidFail(DNSResponse r) =>
                            r.Status is DNSResponseStatus.Timeout or DNSResponseStatus.TransportError
                                     or DNSResponseStatus.MalformedResponse or DNSResponseStatus.ResponseIdMismatch;

                        // Both Prophet adapters then treat every other status as negative.
                        default: subs.append(.negative)

                        ]
- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED (source-traced on current working tree; no live packet-injection
                        run performed).

                       - **Tool Name**            [Codex]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-13
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree with revisions
                       - **Disagree Basis**       Live ResolverQueryOutcome.didFail includes
                                                  Truncated in VantageComparer.swift:24-30 and
                                                  VantageComparer.cs:26-30; the broad claim that
                                                  truncation is clean evidence is stale.
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   Agree the filed defect was valid, but live source
                                                  shows it fixed or superseded. Record the
                                                  remediation and remove it from the open ledger
                                                  only after the change is committed and a real
                                                  failure-path run confirms it.

                       - **Tool Name**            [Claude]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-13
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       Codex's rebuttal is wrong — it cites the WRONG
                                                  predicate. VantageComparer.swift:24-30 is
                                                  ResolverQueryOutcome.didFail, which the delta
                                                  explicitly excludes and E023 covers. The predicate
                                                  this delta names, DNSResponse.didFail at
                                                  DNSResolver.swift:181-188, still omits .truncated
                                                  (a real status, DNSResolver.swift:96 "TC bit set
                                                  and no usable TCP fallback"). Live traces confirm
                                                  the miss on both platforms: Prophet adapter
                                                  Synthesizer.swift:82-91 sends a truncated response
                                                  to default → .negative; DNSSECVerifier.swift:81
                                                  proceeds → .unsigned; EDNS0Probe.swift:54 → .not
                                                  Supported. Windows twins identical: EvidenceAdapters
                                                  .DidFail (Synthesizer.cs:53-55), DNSSECVerifier.
                                                  Failed (:100-104), EDNS0Probe.DidFail (:51-53) all
                                                  omit Truncated. NOT stale; live false-clean.
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   Agree, keep OPEN — reject the "fixed/superseded"
                                                  disposition. Priority high (missed-detection /

                                                  failure/usable-evidence classification per platform,
                                                  drop the probe-local DidFail helpers, and add
                                                  truncation-injection failure-path tests asserting
                                                  invalidated/inconclusive (never negative/unsigned/
                                                  notSupported). Validation: inject a TC=1 answer with

                                                  go inconclusive on a real run, not just green tests.

- **[A065]**            Server Outbound UDP Queries Lack Source Port Randomization — Spoofing Vulnerability
- **Criticality:**      Critical; relying only on 16-bit transaction IDs makes the walker vulnerable to off-path spoofing.
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/resolver.py:160-162
- **Issue:**            [CONFIRMED] The socket setup does not request randomized source ports from the operating system, relying on predictable sequential ports which reduces overall entropy against spoofing.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** SD-05 tracks the candidate; promoted here.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Explicitly bind sockets to randomized ephemeral ports or document OS-level randomization reliance.
- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED

                       - **Tool Name**            [Codex]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-13
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Debunked
                       - **Disagree Basis**       The code does not bind a fixed source port;
                                                  connected UDP sockets at
                                                  Server/syxx_server/resolver.py:156-170,343-357 let
                                                  the OS allocate ephemeral ports. Source alone does
                                                  not establish predictable sequential allocation,
                                                  and the project reference paper only shows
                                                  allocation is OS-dependent.
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   Archive absent runtime evidence. If retained as
                                                  hardening, require a real port-distribution
                                                  measurement on the deployment OS, citing DNS
                                                  Poisoning of Operating System Caches: Attacks and
                                                  Mitigations (SPR discussion).

                       - **Tool Name**            [Claude]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-13
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Disagree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       resolver.py:160-165 and :347-352 create the socket
                                                  and connect WITHOUT any explicit bind() to a fixed
                                                  port, so the OS assigns an ephemeral source port;
                                                  Linux/macOS randomize the ephemeral range (RFC 6056
                                                  algorithms are the modern default). The delta
                                                  asserts "predictable sequential ports" with no
                                                  code or runtime evidence — the code does the exact
                                                  opposite of binding a fixed port. Claim is
                                                  speculative and contradicted by source.
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   N/A — no fixed-port bind exists; source-port
                                                  entropy is OS-provided. Agree with Codex debunk.
                                                  Only refile with a measured port distribution on
                                                  the deployment OS showing non-randomization.

- **[D062]**            TextDiff Allocates Quadratic Memory on Attacker-Controlled Web Content
- **Criticality:**      High; a large changed page can freeze or OOM both Warp clients before the
                        output `maxLines` cap is applied.
- **Location:**         macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/TextDiff.swift:8-35;
                        Windows/Syxx.Kit/TextDiff.cs:15-45;
                        macOS/Sources/SyxxWarp/SyxxWarp.swift:110;
                        Windows/SyxxWarp/Program.cs:116
- **Issue:**            Both implementations allocate and fill an `(m+1)*(n+1)` LCS matrix. The
                        500-line cap truncates only after full O(mn) time and memory are consumed.
                        The archived KTRU-36 “fixed” defect is still live on fetched HTML.
