- **[D066]**            Native Clients Trust Unsigned Keygen meta.valid Responses
- **Criticality:**      High; a TLS interceptor or compromised trust root can grant/deny Pro and alter
                        which security probes/corroboration paths execute.
- **Location:**         macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/LicenseManager.swift:312-347;
                        Windows/Syxx.Kit/LicenseManager.cs:417-457
- **Issue:**            Both clients directly trust `meta.valid` over ordinary system TLS. Server-side
                        Keygen signature work does not protect these direct client requests, and no
                        signed/fresh entitlement artifact is verified locally.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** A021/D040/A056 concern server validation; D003 only mentions transport risk.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Verify Keygen’s signed response and freshness on both clients, or use
                        a canonical Syxx-signed entitlement. [Fix 2] Network/authenticity failure is
                        unknown and must not silently grant or revoke probe capability.
- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED

                       - **Tool Name**            [Codex]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-13
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/LicenseManager.swift:312-347;
                                                  Windows/Syxx.Kit/LicenseManager.cs:417-457 —
                                                  Production-source inspection shows: Both clients
                                                  directly trust `meta.valid` over ordinary system
                                                  TLS. Server-side Keygen signature work does not
                                                  protect these direct client requests, and no
                                                  signed/fresh entitlement artifact is verified
                                                  locally.
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   Verify pinned Keygen signatures or return unknown.

                       - **Tool Name**            [Claude]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-13
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       Live-verified. macOS LicenseManager.swift:339-347
                                                  fetches over URLSession.shared (no cert/key pinning)
                                                  and returns `validation.meta.valid` with no response
                                                  signature or freshness check; Windows
                                                  LicenseManager.cs:451-457 does the same via
                                                  `_httpClient`. Keygen offers Ed25519-signed
                                                  responses (Keygen-Signature) that neither client
                                                  verifies, so a TLS interceptor / rogue trust root
                                                  can forge `meta.valid`. The teeth are the REVOKE
                                                  direction: a forged deny silently disables Pro-gated
                                                  corroboration probes, degrading detection coverage.
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   Agree; keep D-domain, High. Verify a pinned Keygen
                                                  signature + freshness (or a canonical Syxx-signed
                                                  entitlement) on both clients; any authenticity/
                                                  network failure resolves to unknown and must not
                                                  silently grant OR revoke probe capability.

- **[C047]**            Mechanism Fingerprint Counts Unrelated Anomaly Classes as Corroboration
- **Criticality:**      Critical verdict-integrity defect. A mechanism label can be emitted without
                        two signals converging on that mechanism.
- **Location:**         macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/Synthesis/Scorers.swift:90-125;
                        Windows/Syxx.Kit/Synthesis/Scorers.cs:100-151;
                        DESIGN.md:163-180;
                        macOS/Tests/SyxxKitTests/ScorersContractTests.swift:111-143
- **Issue:**            CODE DEFECT and TEST DEFECT. The scorer finds the top mechanism class but
                        checks its minimum against the count of all distinct positive evidence IDs
                        globally. Two unrelated observations, such as an ECS privacy exposure and a
                        response-size local-compromise hint, pass the two-signal gate even though no
                        mechanism class has two supporting signals. The function then emits a
                        tentative fingerprint for whichever one-item class wins iteration/tie order.
                        The focused tests pass because their positive case encodes global distinct IDs,
                        not per-class convergence. DESIGN.md requires converging signals and independent
                        sources. Conflicting one-item classes require no fingerprint or an unresolved
                        referral, never a named mechanism.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Related B005, which specifies the sub-scorer data contract. This is the live
                        implementation and test violation of its corroboration rule.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Require at least two independent sources supporting the selected
                        mechanism class, not two IDs anywhere in the evidence set.
                        [Fix 2] Make tie handling deterministic and unresolved when classes do not
                        converge.
                        [Fix 3] Add a cross-class failure case and mutate the per-class gate to prove
                        the test fails.
- **Code Sample:**      [

                        // Scorers.swift:112-118
                        let topClass = signalsPerClass.max(by: { $0.value < $1.value })
                        let independentSignals = Set(positiveEvidence.map { $0.evidenceId }).count
                        guard independentSignals >= 2 else { return nil }

                        ]

                        - **Date**                 2026-07-19
                        - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree

                        - **Proposed Revisions**   Require >=2 independent sources supporting the selected mechanism class. Unresolved tie = no fingerprint.

- **[D077]**            macOS ContentWarp URL Encoding Nil Fallback Can Inject Proxy Query Parameters
- **Criticality:**      Medium; a malformed target URL can break the proxy query boundary and fetch the
                        wrong resource for warp comparison.
- **Location:**         macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/ContentWarp.swift:129-130, 210
- **Issue:**            `addingPercentEncoding(withAllowedCharacters: .urlQueryAllowed)` returns `nil`
                        when the string cannot be encoded. The nil-coalescing operator at line 129 falls
                        back to the raw unencoded `absoluteString`. If that raw string contains URL-
                        significant characters (`&`, `#`, `?`, `=`), the proxy URL's query parameter
                        boundary is broken — the target URL bleeds into additional query params. The
                        proxy server could misinterpret or truncate the target, causing the warp integrity
                        comparison to verify against a different resource. The same pattern recurs at
                        line 210 for script fetching. DELTAS-fixed.md records MACX-096, KTRU-08, and
                        KTRU-32 as previously identifying this defect class. The Windows equivalent
                        (ContentWarp.cs:117) was fixed with `Uri.EscapeDataString`, but the macOS side
                        remains broken.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** DELTAS-fixed.md MACX-096, KTRU-08, KTRU-32 previously flagged the same defect
                        class. Windows was fixed; macOS remains open.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Use `URL.addingPercentEncoding(withAllowedCharacters: .urlHostAllowed)`
                        or an explicit escaping function that returns `WarpResult.isInconclusive` on nil
                        instead of falling back to raw text.
                        [Fix 2] Apply the same fix at line 210 for script URL construction.

- **Code Sample:**      [

                        // ContentWarp.swift:129-130
                        let encodedTarget = targetURL.absoluteString.addingPercentEncoding(
                            withAllowedCharacters: .urlQueryAllowed) ?? targetURL.absoluteString
                        guard let proxyURL = URL(string: "\(proxyBaseURLStr)?url=\(encodedTarget)")

                        ]


                        - **Tool Name**            [opencode]
                        - **Date**                 2026-07-19
                        - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree
                        - **Disagree Basis**       
                        - **Proposed Revisions**   Confirmed: ContentWarp.swift:129-130 uses addingPercentEncoding(withAllowedCharacters: .urlQueryAllowed) → nil falls back to raw absoluteString. If raw string contains URL-significant characters (&, #, ?, =), proxy URL query boundary breaks — target URL bleeds into additional proxy params. Windows was fixed with Uri.EscapeDataString; macOS remains broken. Fix: use explicit escaping returning inconclusive on nil.

                        limiter is an Efficacy component: once OOMd, no protection remains.

                        eviction on each allow() call.

- **[A004]**            _body() Partial Read Can Silently Truncate POST Bodies
- **Criticality:**      Critical (silent data corruption on collector endpoints); user made
                        aware.
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/app.py:214
- **Issue:**            `self.rfile.read(n)` on a socket-based stream is NOT guaranteed to
                        return exactly n bytes. On slow connections, timeout, or premature
                        client disconnect, it returns fewer bytes. The truncated body is
                        parsed as JSON, producing a misleading 400 "invalid JSON" — or, on
                        binary endpoints, silently processes a partial payload. Affects
                        `/api/diff` and `/api/leak/token` POST endpoints whose body size
                        matters.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** None.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Replace bare read() with a loop reading until
                        `len(body) == length` or socket/stream EOF, then compare.
                        [Fix 2] Add a minimum-content-length guard for structured endpoints.

                                                  correction recorded under Revisions)

                                                  a buffered socket file — io.BufferedReader
                                                  .read(n) loops internally until n bytes or EOF,
                                                  so a merely SLOW connection does not short-read;
                                                  the truncation triggers are premature client
                                                  disconnect (EOF) and socket timeout. The defect
                                                  and impact stand as filed for those triggers

                                                  `self.rfile.read(length)`, and returned None for
                                                  oversize bodies, which downstream json.loads
                                                  would turn into a misleading TypeError path).

                                                  == 0`, returning the _BODY_INCOMPLETE sentinel
                                                  on EOF/OSError and _BODY_TOO_LARGE for >1 MiB,
                                                  and `_body_error()` (app.py:285-292) maps these
                                                  to explicit 400 "incomplete request body" / 413

                                                  silent truncation. Covered by

                                                  Critical is correct (silent partial payloads on

                        connection gets a dedicated thread. An attacker can open many
                        connections and send headers slowly, tying up threads indefinitely.
                        Rate-limiting (ratelimit.py) only applies after request parsing, so
                        pre-parse slow attacks bypass it entirely.

                        [Fix 2] Add a per-connection `socket.settimeout()` in the handler.

                                                  actually matters — plus `httpd.timeout`
                                                  (app.py:1001-1002) and a new
                                                  HTTP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT config (config.py:99,
                                                  default 30 s). Note Fix 1 alone
                                                  (`httpd.timeout`) would have been ineffective
                                                  for Slowloris: BaseServer.timeout only bounds
                                                  the accept loop, not per-connection reads — the

                                                  client sending one header byte every <30 s

                                                  rule 1, thread-exhaustion DoS). Keep open until

- **[A006]**            HMAC Secret Shared Between Session Tokens and Leak Attestations
- **Criticality:**      High (key-separation violation, cross-purpose key reuse); user made
                        aware.
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/licensing.py:17-25, 66-81; leak.py:27-30
- **Issue:**            `licensing.secret()` returns the same HMAC key for both session
                        tokens (verified server-side) and leak attestation signatures (sent
                        to clients for offline verification). If a leak attestation signature
                        is ever posted publicly (e.g., on Reddit as evidence), the HMAC
                        output + signed payload constitute a known-plaintext pair. While
                        HMAC-SHA256 is not reversible, reusing a key across two security
                        boundaries (server-only session vs. client-visible attestation)
                        violates cryptographic key-separation hygiene.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** None.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Derive separate sub-keys from the master secret using
                        HKDF-expand with distinct labels ("session" / "attestation").
                        [Fix 2] Use an asymmetric key pair for leak attestations so the
                        client can verify without holding the signing key.

                                                  implements this delta's Fix 2 (asymmetric
                                                  signatures): leak.py:33-38 now uses a dedicated
                                                  Ed25519 collector keypair explicitly
                                                  "independent of the licensing HMAC secret";
                                                  leak.py no longer imports licensing at all, and
                                                  licensing's HMAC secret is used solely for
                                                  session-token signing (licensing.py:54; grep
                                                  shows no other secret() consumer). Attestations
                                                  are now third-party-verifiable by design
                                                  (leak.py:1-13), which also retires the
                                                  known-plaintext concern — Ed25519 public
                                                  verification is the intended use. Key-separation
                                                  is complete; the HKDF Fix 1 is moot. Criticality
                                                  High was correct at filing. Two follow-up
                                                  observations for a SUCCESSOR delta (not grounds
                                                  to keep this one open): (a) if

                                                  generates an ephemeral key per process

- **[A007]**            Sequential Clean Vantage DNS Queries Adds Latency
- **Criticality:**      High (Efficiency — slow responses cause client timeouts); user made
                        aware.
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/app.py:636-643
- **Issue:**            The clean-vantage query loop tries public resolvers sequentially,
                        only falling back to the next after the first times out (3s). Under
                        the Verification & Honesty Protocol §3 (efficiency), slow single-
                        resolver responses cause client-side timeouts, leading to incomplete
                        data and potentially inconclusive verdicts. The two resolvers should
                        be queried in parallel with a short-circuit on first success.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** None.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Fire both resolver queries concurrently with
                        `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor` or `asyncio`.
                        [Fix 2] Return whichever answers first; log-defer the slower one.

                                                  first-then-fallback loop). FIXED in the
                                                  uncommitted working tree:
                                                  `_clean_vantage_answers` (app.py:139-163) now
                                                  submits both PUBLIC_RESOLVERS queries to a
                                                  ThreadPoolExecutor, takes the first non-empty
                                                  answer set via as_completed, cancels the
                                                  stragglers, and shuts the pool down without
                                                  waiting — Fix 1 + Fix 2 essentially as
                                                  proposed. Exercised by tests/test_routes.py:145
                                                  -172 (stubbed) and the live path; suite 59/59
                                                  OK. Behavior note, correct as implemented: an
                                                  empty answer set from the fast resolver does
                                                  not short-circuit — it waits for the other,
                                                  which is the honest choice (absence of records
                                                  from one vantage is not evidence). Criticality:
                                                  High is generous for a pure Efficiency delta
                                                  whose failure mode is an honest client-side
                                                  inconclusive (never a false verdict); Medium
                                                  would also have been defensible — no change
                                                  required, noting for calibration. Keep open
                                                  until committed, then move to DELTAS-fixed.md.

- **[A008]**            Recursive NS Resolution Can Query Arbitrary Upstream Resolvers
- **Criticality:**      High (unintended DNS-proxy behavior); user made aware.
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/resolver.py:382-392
- **Issue:**            If a delegation has no glue records, `resolve_authoritative`
                        recursively resolves the NS hostname by querying the root servers.
                        Since NS hostnames come from DNS responses controlled by an
                        attacker-who-owns-the-authoritative-server for a subdomain, this
                        can cause the Syxx server to issue DNS queries for arbitrary
                        names to arbitrary nameservers. Limited by a depth counter (16)
                        and timeout, but constitutes an unintended open DNS proxy.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** None.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] When glue is absent, cap recursive depth lower (e.g., 3)
                        and whitelist the root-server set.
                        [Fix 2] Validate that NS hostnames from delegation responses
                        resolve only to the domain's own hierarchy.

                       - **Tool Name**            [syxx-researcher]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-10
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Disagree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       Ground 3 (legitimate delta, wrong proposed
                                                  fix), plus a basis correction. Fix 2 —
                                                  "validate that NS hostnames ... resolve only to
                                                  the domain's own hierarchy" — would break
                                                  RFC-conformant DNS: out-of-bailiwick NS records
                                                  are ubiquitous and legitimate (e.g. example.com
                                                  NS ns1.cloudflare.com; RFC 1034 §4.2.2 places
                                                  no same-hierarchy requirement on NS targets).
                                                  Implementing Fix 2 would make the authoritative
                                                  walker return inconclusive/failed for a large
                                                  fraction of real zones — an availability defect
                                                  in the ground-truth oracle. Basis correction:
                                                  "queries ... to arbitrary nameservers" was
                                                  overstated even at filing — the no-glue
                                                  sub-resolution recurses via
                                                  resolve_authoritative, which always starts from

- **[B002]**            Resolver Provenance Spoof Vulnerability
- **Criticality:**      Critical (attacker-forgeable baseline → false-clean provenance); user made
                        aware.
- **Location:**         DESIGN.md:15; NetworkKeyState.swift; LAN/LANCartographer.swift,
                        LAN/ServiceProbePlan.swift; AuthoritativeVantage.swift:66-119;
                        DNSResolver.swift:194
- **Issue:**            "Resolver Provenance Confidence" is derived from NetworkKeyState resolver
                        discovery + syxx-lan ARP/MAC cartography + mDNS/service probes. ARP, MAC,
                        and mDNS are all forgeable by the on-link adversary Syxx exists to catch —
                        an attacker who ARP-spoofs the gateway MAC and answers mDNS makes a rogue
                        resolver classify as "expected router" (a false-clean provenance verdict).
                        The scorer itself is not yet shipped (design-stage): `grep provenance` finds
                        only a static label field at DNSResolver.swift:194. Its inputs already ship
                        untrusted, and the same attacker-controlled-baseline class is already live
                        in AuthoritativeVantage (NS + NS-IP resolution over the same on-path UDP
                        bootstrap it audits).
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** ex-DSN-001. Not a duplicate; live embodiment tracked as review finding
                        PRB-2.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Treat LAN identity (ARP/MAC/mDNS) as untrusted corroboration — may
                        lower/contextualize provenance confidence, never raise it toward
                        "expected/clean" alone.
                        [Fix 2] Surface any LAN-vs-independent-signal conflict as a provenance
                        warning; never silently resolve for the LAN view.
                        [Fix 3] Require ≥1 corroborating signal outside the on-link spoof surface
                        before high confidence; fix PRB-2 before the scorer ships.
- **Code Sample:**      [

                         // No scorer shipped — design-stage. Defective spec, DESIGN.md:15:
                         //   "Resolver Provenance Confidence: combine NetworkKeyState resolver discovery, syxx-lan
                         //    ARP/MAC cartography, mDNS/service probes ... to infer whether the active resolver is an
                         //    expected router ..."   (no statement that ARP/MAC/mDNS are attacker-forgeable)

                         ]

                                                  signal outside the on-link spoof surface" — on

                                                  validation path, this means provenance can never
                                                  reach high confidence. That's correct behavior,
                                                  but worth documenting explicitly as a known
                                                  limitation so users on isolated networks aren't
                                                  surprised. Add a sentence to the spec: "In
                                                  isolated networks where no external signal is
                                                  available, provenance confidence is capped at
                                                  moderate."

- **[B004]**            Correlated Signals Summed as Independent
- **Criticality:**      Critical (inflated confidence suppresses the Reddit referral); user made
                        aware.
- **Location:**         DESIGN.md:61-63; SynthesisEngine.swift:49-54, Conclusion.swift:149-239;
                        SynthesisEngine.cs:49-54, Conclusion.cs:119-189
- **Issue:**            Evidence weights are summed with a bare `scored[h]! += w` and no
                        independence term. Same-source signals double-count: F3 (stub entropy) + F9
                        (response size) over one capture population; authoritativeDiverges +
                        authoritativeDivergesConfirmed over one resolver-vs-authority exchange.
                        Additive LLR is valid only for conditionally-independent evidence; stacking
                        correlated weak signals inflates the winning probability and the top-two
                        margin, crossing the 75%/30-point gate and suppressing the referral.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** ex-DSN-003. Related B002 (both inflate confidence); review finding SYN-3.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Covariance-cap each correlated group — weight it at no more than its
                        strongest member.
                        [Fix 2] Assert independence per signal pair before additive combination.
- **Code Sample:**      [

                         // SynthesisEngine.swift:49-54
                         for e in evidence {
                             for h in threatHypotheses {
                                 let w = WeightRubric.getWeight(evidenceId: e.evidenceId, hypothesis: h)
                                 scored[h]! += w        // additive; no correlation / independence term
                             }
                         }

                         ]

                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree

                                                   strongest member" is correct but has a blind spot:
                                                   two weakly-correlated signals from the same probe
                                                   (e.g., stub entropy + response size) each slightly
                                                   below the correlation threshold could each pass the
                                                   independence check and still double-count. Recommend
                                                   adding a per-probe weight cap as a second line of
                                                   defense — no single probe's signals can contribute
                                                   more than X total weight to any hypothesis.

- **[B008]**            Clean Verdict Possible When All Sections Are Inconclusive
- **Criticality:**      Critical (false-clean disposition from inconclusive data); user made
                        aware.
- **Location:**         macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/Synthesis/SynthesisEngine.swift:60-74
- **Issue:**            The eligibility gate (`cleanBlocked`) only blocks `.clean` when a
                        section is `.untested` or `.invalidated`. A scenario where all
                        sections ran as `.inconclusive` or `.degraded` (not `blocksClean`)
                        can produce `.clean` because the benign prior (1.5) + negative count
                        (0) still gives clean = 1.5, while inconclusive = inconclusiveCount
                        * 0.8. With 1 inconclusive section, inconclusive = 0.8, clean = 1.5
                        — clean wins even though every section returned inconclusive.

- **[SRV-101]**         Ed25519 Leak-Attestation Migration Has Cold-Start Correctness Bugs (WIP)
- **Criticality:**      High (Efficacy — the in-flight HMAC→Ed25519 leak-attestation migration would
                        deterministically 500 on a cold /api/leak/verify as written; CF-01 evidence
                        path). Found via real-run validation, not py_compile. NOTE: uncommitted
                        working-tree WIP, not a shipped/released regression.
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/leak.py:135 (sign before key init) and :40,45,65 (global
                        name mismatch: `_COLLECTOR_PUB_KEY_DER` declared vs `_RAW` assigned). Only
                        caller: Server/syxx_server/app.py:770 (/api/leak/verify).
- **Issue:**            The in-progress HMAC→Ed25519 rewrite (1) calls `_COLLECTOR_PRIV_KEY.sign()`
                        before `_ensure_collector_key()` runs → AttributeError on a cold process; and
                        (2) declares `global _COLLECTOR_PUB_KEY_DER` but assigns
                        `_COLLECTOR_PUB_KEY_RAW` (a discarded local) → `collector_public_key()`
                        NameError. Both deterministic; masked because `leak.verify()` had no test.
- **Fix(es):**          [1] `_ensure_collector_key()` before `sign()`. [2] Consistent public-key
                        global name (`_COLLECTOR_PUB_KEY_RAW`). [3] Add tests/test_leak.py (cold
                        verify + tamper rejection), gated on `@unittest.skipUnless(leak._HAS_CRYPTO)`.
- **Status:**           **[done]** — committed 2026-07-08 as `8a213f8` (leak.py migration +
                        tests/test_leak.py + Server/requirements.txt declaring cryptography>=41.0.0).
                        The unit review that blocked the commit completed and surfaced two
                        pre-existing server bugs, fixed first as separate commits: `0f9f28c`
                        (/api/leak/verify checked `isinstance(result, str)` — dead since c84cbfc;
                        bad token → TypeError in_send, observed as HTTP 200 + "internal error";
                        now `result is None` → 404, with first route-level tests in
                        tests/test_routes.py) and `0a474e2` (missing module-level `import time` —
                        every /api/trial/anchor POST 500'd with NameError). All three verified by
                        live-handler runs; suite 46/46 in a venv (cryptography 49.0.0).
- **Lesson:**           "Green suite" + py_compile ≠ "feature works". Real-run validation found a
                        100%-cold-start crash inside an uncommitted crypto migration.

- **[A010]**            Rate-Limit / Exposure / Audit IPs Collapse Behind the Shipped nginx Proxy
- **Criticality:**      Critical (global DoS via one shared bucket; exposure verdict always wrong)
                        in
                        the script-installed deployment; analysis 2026-07-09.
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/app.py:200 (`_rate_key`), :730 (`_route_exposure`);
                        scripts/deploy.sh:243-246 (nginx proxy_pass, sets X-Real-IP)
- **Issue:**            The server never reads X-Real-IP/X-Forwarded-For (0 refs in app.py); it keys
                        on
                        `self.client_address[0]` = 127.0.0.1 behind local nginx. Every anonymous public
                        route shares ONE bucket `ip:127.0.0.1` — one client 429s the whole internet, no
                        real per-client limiting. `_route_exposure` sees 127.0.0.1, hits the loopback
                        guard, returns "not-applicable" for EVERY caller (feature dead) though nginx
                        already passes the real IP.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Related A005. Distinct from SD-14. Claude-verified.

                                                  (`git diff HEAD -- app.py` still shows the edits).
                                                  New `_client_ip()` at app.py:234-250 reads
                                                  X-Real-IP / rightmost X-Forwarded-For ONLY when the
                                                  socket peer is loopback (`self.client_address[0]`
                                                  is_loopback), so a direct internet client cannot
                                                  spoof the header — matches Fix [1]. Wired into
                                                  `_rate_key` (:255), `_route_exposure` (:806), and
                                                  audit calls (:539,:543,:599,:621). Spoof-guard is

                                                  via shared 127.0.0.1 bucket + dead exposure route).

                                                  would collapse all clients to the proxy IP again;
                                                  acceptable given the shipped nginx sets it.

- **[A016]**            Authoritative Walker Grants "authoritative" Verdict Without Checking the AA
                        Bit
- **Criticality:**      Critical (spoofable ground truth feeds the client's serverConfirmed
                        evidence); analysis 2026-07-09.
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/resolver.py:381-389
- **Issue:**            `resolve_authoritative` terminates the walk on any response whose answers
                        section is non-empty (or NXDOMAIN / no-referral NODATA) and labels it
                        `verdict: "authoritative"` whenever rcode is 0/3. The AA flag is captured
                        into the payload (`"aa": resp["aa"]`) but never required for the verdict. A
                        non-authoritative answer injected at any delegation level — a middlebox on
                        the server's own outbound UDP/53, or an off-path spoofer winning the 16-bit
                        txid race against a root/TLD query — becomes "ground truth";
                        /api/authoritative feeds it to clients, where the synthesis layer either
                        upgrades a benign divergence to the decisive authoritativeDivergesConfirmed
                        evidence (false near-proof of rewrite) or rubber-stamps a hijacked answer as
                        matching ground truth.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Broader form of SD-16 (SERVER_DELTAS.md; empty-authority NODATA variant of
                        the same aa-unused defect); compounded by SD-01/SD-02 (weak spoof rejection)
                        and A011 (unvalidated glue). Delta-analysis workflow 2026-07-09.

                       - **Date**                 2026-07-10
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       N/A

                                                  :381-399 now requires the AA bit before granting
                                                  ground truth: `has_soa = any(... SOA ...)` (:381)
                                                  admits SOA-backed NODATA into the terminal branch,
                                                  and `if not resp["aa"]:` returns `authoritative:
                                                  None, verdict: "inconclusive"` with a "terminal
                                                  response without AA bit" note (:388-393). Only an
                                                  AA-asserted response reaches verdict
                                                  "authoritative" (:394-399). This closes the exact
                                                  gap: a recursive/middlebox answer or an off-path
                                                  txid-race spoof at a delegation level can no longer
                                                  become serverConfirmed ground truth. Matches Fix
                                                  [1] and subsumes SD-16. Criticality Critical
                                                  correct (spoofable ground truth -> forgeable
                                                  client evidence). RESIDUAL (design, not blocking):
                                                  the AA bit itself is spoofable by an on-path
                                                  attacker on the server's outbound UDP/53 who wins
                                                  the txid race — the AA gate raises the bar but does
                                                  not authenticate the source; only DNSSEC validation

                                                  would. Worth a follow-up but distinct from this
                                                  delta. Keep-open until committed.

- **[A018]**            Silent Fetch Truncation Poisons the Warp Clean Baseline → False "tampered"
- **Criticality:**      High (false on-path-injection accusation, cached 300 s and served to every
                        Pro user diffing that URL); analysis 2026-07-09.

                        `max_bytes` with no error or flag. `warp.build_baseline` computes the clean-
                        vantage script/host sets from the truncated page and caches them for
                        WARP_CACHE_TTL. Any page larger than FETCH_MAX_BYTES (5 MB default, smaller
                        if the operator lowers SYXX_FETCH_MAX_BYTES) with a legitimate third-party
                        `<script src>` after the cut point makes the client's full copy classify as
                        injected_hosts → assessment "injected" → `_diff_verdict` "tampered".

                        correctness defect. Related A012 (diff verdict overreach on disjointness).

                                                  defines `class TruncatedError(FetchError)` (:36) and

                                                  truncating: `if len(body) > max_bytes: raise
                                                  TruncatedError(...)` (:117-118), replacing the old

- **[B013]**            HMAC Called "Signature" in Witness — Overclaimed Guarantee
- **Criticality:**      High (misleading cryptographic claim — HMAC ≠ digital signature);
                        user made aware.
- **Location:**         macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/WitnessSigner.swift:1-108; SyxxWitness/
                        SyxxWitness.swift:58-59, 97-100
- **Issue:**            Code uses HMAC-SHA256 (symmetric MAC) but calls it "signature"
                        throughout: "Snapshot signature", "signed!", "Tamper-evident."
                        HMAC proves integrity to two parties sharing the same secret.
                        It does NOT provide non-repudiation — anyone who knows the key
                        can forge a "signed" snapshot. A user could reasonably believe
                        this is asymmetric-crypto evidence for legal/adversarial use.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Rename to "HMAC authentication tag" or "integrity tag."
                        [Fix 2] Migrate to asymmetric signing (Ed25519) for true
                        non-repudiation.
- **Status:**           **[done]** — committed `bedc0c9` (CF-01). Fix 2 taken: WitnessSigner is now
                        Ed25519 (`Curve25519.Signing`), the `signature` field is a genuine digital
                        signature verified with the snapshot's embedded public key (no shared secret),
                        so the non-repudiation overclaim is resolved, not just relabelled. Verified by
                        reading the committed tree 2026-07-09 (`WitnessSigner.swift:39,57,64`).

                       - **Tool Name**            [Opencode]
                       - **Date**                 7-9-2026
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Disagree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       This delta was written before the Ed25519 migration
                                                   (`bedc0c9`). The current codebase uses Ed25519 for
                                                   WitnessSigner on both platforms (macOS
                                                   `WitnessSigner.swift`, Windows `WitnessSigner.cs`).
                                                   The term "Signature" is now correct — Ed25519 is a
                                                   true public-key signature scheme, not HMAC. The
                                                   delta is outdated.
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   Mark as superseded by the Ed25519 migration. No fix
                                                   needed.

                       - **Date**                 2026-07-13

                                                  remediation and remove it from the open ledger

- **[B015]**            VantageComparer: Empty Local + Non-Empty Public = Always Redirection
- **Criticality:**      High (false positive — legitimate NODATA treated as tampering);
                        user made aware.
- **Location:**         macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/VantageComparer.swift:139, 141-142
- **Issue:**            `localEmptyButPublicNot` unconditionally sets `redirection =
                        true`. A local resolver that legitimately returns NODATA for a
                        domain while public resolvers return records is not necessarily
                        tampering — split-horizon DNS or geo-specific records exist.
                        Should be `.inconclusive`, not automatic redirection.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Treat empty-local + non-empty-public as `.inconclusive`
                        unless corroborated by additional evidence (e.g., known block
                        page IP).
- **Status:**           **[done]** — committed 2026-07-08: macOS `b8ba236`, Windows `15e0ecf`.
                        Empty-but-successful local (NODATA/NXDOMAIN) → `.inconclusive`; redirection
                        now requires a blocking IP or a disjoint NON-EMPTY answer. Committed together
                        with the min-2-vantage guard (single usable public baseline → degraded, no
                        redirection verdict) — the two share a hunk in `evaluate` and were reviewed
                        as a unit; the guard also gained its first tests (macOS
                        testEvaluateSingleBaselineIsDegradedNotRedirection, Windows
                        SingleBaselineIsDegradedNotRedirection). Witness-Ed25519 test rework in the
                        same test files was excluded and stays uncommitted with that WIP.
                        WINDOWS WAS NOT ACTUALLY FIXED as of the earlier "FIXED (both platforms)"
                        line above: B017 had been applied only to `Evaluate` — the factored-out
                        logic the unit tests exercise — while the live path
                        (`CompareVantagePointsAsync`, called from AppViewModel.cs:153 and
                        Program.cs:225) duplicated the verdict inline and still counted an empty
                        local answer as redirection (and the min-2 guard had landed only inline).
                        Tests were green while the shipping path kept the bug. `15e0ecf` makes
                        the live path delegate to `Evaluate` (mirroring macOS, whose live path
                        already called `evaluate`), so both semantics live in the one tested path.
                        BlockingAnswerFlaggedAsRedirection gained a second baseline (with the
                        guard, one baseline correctly reads degraded).
                        Verified by real runs on the pre-commit working tree (differs from the
                        committed tree only by the excluded Witness test hunks): macOS 296 tests,
                        1 pre-existing failure (SYN-201 only); Windows 157/157.
- **Lesson:**           A "pure logic, factored out so it can be unit-tested" mirror of live code
                        is a drift trap: the fix landed in the mirror, the tests went green, and
                        the shipping path kept fabricating the verdict. Either the live path calls
                        the tested function, or the tests prove nothing about the product.

                       - **Tool Name**            [Opencode]
                       - **Date**                 7-9-2026

                                                   side before flagging redirection. A domain that
                                                   legitimately has no A records (e.g., MX-only) will
                                                   produce a false positive. Fix: check
                                                   `localRecords.Count == 0 &&
                                                   !result.isRedirectionDetected &&
                                                   IsAuthoritativeNxDomain()` before emitting
                                                   redirection. Needs design.

- **[SYN-201]**         DS Engine Flips interception→contentTampering via Vacuous Clean Support
- **Criticality:**      High (verdict correctness / Honesty §3 calibration). Confirmed by a live
                        test failure (macOS 1/295): SynthesisScenarioTests.swift:70.
- **Location:**         macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/Synthesis/SynthesisEngine.swift:90-99
                        (coveredThreats),
                        :144-146 (clean-baseline emission); Conclusion.swift:182,198-199,205 (weights);
                        Synthesizer.swift:58 (combine: any positive sub-signal makes the section positive).
- **Issue:**            Scenario: dnsUnencrypted + encryptedDnsBlocked + svcbStripped. Raw evidence
                        favors interception 2.4 vs contentTampering 0.6. Mirror & Portal are correctly
                        POSITIVE (they emit the transport-interception evidence) and are excluded from
                        the clean pool. The defect: Prophet & Witness run clean on checks that never
                        probe the DoH/SVCB transport path, yet the static coveredThreats map marks them
                        as covering the whole `interception` atom, so both emit clean support for
                        Θ∖interception. svcbStripped is ambiguous (nested mass on the SET
                        {interception,contentTampering}); Dempster's rule intersects ¬interception ∩
                        {interception,contentTampering} = {contentTampering}, redirecting the vacuous
                        "not interception" mass into committed contentTampering belief → verdict flip.
                        Root cause is SEMANTIC: `interception` is one atom but a multi-mechanism threat,
                        and the coverage map spends vacuous support as informative clean evidence.
- **Fix(es):**          [1 preferred — semantic] Split `interception` by mechanism, or make coverage
                        observation-gated so a section may dampen only the interception subspace it
                        actually probed this run. [2 interim] Section-specific/observation-gated clean
                        weight (does NOT fix the monolithic-atom problem; label interim). [3 last resort]
                        Strong-margin preservation rule (papers over the modeling error).
- **Status:**           Confirmed 2026-07-08, UNFIXED (deliberate). Do NOT tune weights to green the
                        test before the coverage semantics are decided — that would hide the modeling error.

                       - **Tool Name**            [Opencode]
                       - **Date**                 7-9-2026
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       N/A
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   Already fixed by the frame-split implementation
                                                   (committed as part of SYN-201). The old single
                                                   `.interception` hypothesis meant Portal's clean-section
                                                   dampener (-2.0 on `captivePortalActive`) reduced the
                                                   on-path signal from Mirror/Prophet. Frame-split
                                                   isolates Portal→`_transport` and Mirror/Prophet→
                                                   `_onPath`. Verified: SYN-201 build and test both
                                                   platforms (macOS 299/0, Windows 158/0). No further
                                                   action needed.

- **[B025]**            Windows IPClassifier Diverges From macOS: `Invalid` Non-Blocking + Missing
                        Special-Use Ranges → False-Clean Redirection Verdict
- **Criticality:**      Critical (same answers → opposite verdicts across the 1:1 port; false "no
                        redirection" on Windows); analysis 2026-07-09.
- **Location:**         Windows/Syxx.Kit/IPClassifier.cs:48 (`_ => false` catch-all), 52-67
                        (ClassifyIPv4) vs macOS IPClassifier.swift:31-33, 61-64
- **Issue:**            The macOS working tree treats `.invalid` as a blocking answer and classifies
                        192.0.0.0/24 (reserved), 192.88.99.0/24, and 198.18.0.0/15 (benchmarking);
                        the Windows twin still maps `Invalid` to non-blocking through the catch-all
                        and returns PublicRoutable for all three ranges. A censoring resolver
                        returning [real-CDN-IP, 198.18.0.1] keeps localLooksBlocked false and

                        Deserialization)
- **Criticality:**      High ("anyone can verify with the public key alone" broken cross-platform);
                        analysis 2026-07-09.
- **Location:**         Windows/SyxxWitness/Program.cs:101 vs the macOS camelCase witness file
                        format (cf. repo witness.json)
- **Issue:**            `JsonSerializer.Deserialize<WitnessSnapshot>(json)` uses default case-
                        sensitive PascalCase matching, so a macOS-produced witness file (camelCase
                        keys) maps no properties: PublicKey deserializes empty and
                        `WitnessSigner.VerifySnapshot` throws "Snapshot has no public key." before
                        the signature is even checked. The reverse direction (macOS decoding a
                        PascalCase Windows file) fails too.

                        snapshots): this is the snapshot FILE schema layer — fixing E011 alone still
                        leaves cross-platform verify broken.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Standardize the snapshot file on camelCase and deserialize with
                        `PropertyNamingPolicy = CamelCase` (or `PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true`)

- **[D002]**            Offline Clock Regression Undetectable for Trial
- **Criticality:**      High (unlimited offline trial); user made aware.
- **Location:**         macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/LicenseManager.swift:185-193
- **Issue:**            When the server is unreachable and no local state exists,
                        `finalLaunchMillis = now`. On next launch with an earlier clock,
                        no cross-session clock-regression check exists in the offline
                        path. User can set clock back, re-launch, and extend trial
                        indefinitely.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Persist `maxSeenMillis` with Keychain access control.
                        [Fix 2] Reject any timestamp older than the persisted maximum.

                                                   max-seen-timestamp is trivially bypassed by deleting
                                                   the config file. Fix: use biometric or a signed
                                                   hardware anchor (macOS Secure Enclave). Low priority
                                                   — trial bypass doesn't produce false verdicts.

- **[D009]**            macOS Trial Server-Anchor Is Silently Dead (`NSNumber as? Int64` Always
                        nil); Windows Anchors, macOS Does Not
- **Criticality:**      High (a core anti-abuse control — KTRU-03 server anchoring + clock-
                        regression
                        lock — is non-functional on macOS only); analysis 2026-07-09.
- **Location:**         macOS LicenseManager.swift:145-146 vs Windows LicenseManager.cs:247-248;
                        regression lock at LicenseManager.swift:182-184.
- **Issue:**            `JSONSerialization` yields `NSNumber`; `NSNumber as? Int64` returns nil in
                        Swift
                        (fixed-width ints aren't bridged by `as?`, unlike Int/Double/Bool). Both
                        `serverLaunch`/`serverTime` casts fail → guard fails → `syncTrialAnchorWithServer`
                        always returns nil → macOS silently takes the offline branch every time: (a) server
                        never anchors first-launch → clearing Keychain grants a fresh trial; (b) the
                        `serverTime` regression lock can never fire. Windows uses `GetInt64()` and works.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Related D002. Code Claude-verified; nil-cast mechanism is the known Swift
                        gotcha.
- **Fix(es):**          [1] Parse via `(json["firstLaunch"] as? NSNumber)?.int64Value` (both
                        fields), or
                        `JSONDecoder` into a Codable. Add a test feeding a real numeric JSON body.
- **Code Sample:**      [ let serverLaunch = json["firstLaunch"] as? Int64,   // always nil ]
- **Tag:**              INFERRED (code Claude-verified; nil-cast behavior high-confidence, confirm
                        with a parse test).

                       - **Tool Name**            [syxx-researcher]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-10
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Disagree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       False positive. The delta's own Tag asked for a parse
                                                   test; I ran it (Swift 6.x, macOS, today): feeding
                                                   `{"firstLaunch": 1720000000, "serverTime": ...}`
                                                   through JSONSerialization, `json["firstLaunch"] as?
                                                   Int64` returns Optional(1720000000) — NOT nil. Since
                                                   SE-0170 (Swift 4), NSNumber bridges to fixed-width
                                                   ints via `as?` when exactly representable. So the
                                                   guard never always-failed, macOS server anchoring was
                                                   never "silently dead," Keychain-clear did not grant a
                                                   fresh trial via this mechanism, and the serverTime
                                                   regression lock could fire. The core factual claims
                                                   are disproven.
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   Note for the record: the working tree ALREADY applied
                                                   the proposed fix — LicenseManager.swift:145-146 now
                                                   reads `(json["firstLaunch"] as? NSNumber)?.int64Value`
                                                   (uncommitted, on top of f7b01d5). That change is
                                                   equivalent/harmless and fine to keep as defensive
                                                   style, but it fixes nothing. Reject the delta rather
                                                   than mark it fixed, so the ledger does not certify a
                                                   defect that never existed. The still-real weaknesses
                                                   in this path (1.5 s semaphore block on the main
                                                   caller; silent offline fallback) are different deltas
                                                   and partly tracked already (D002 clock-regression
                                                   comment).

                                                  uses NSNumber.int64Value; the original assertion
                                                  that NSNumber cannot bridge to Int64 is false

                        Returns false
- **Criticality:**      Medium (divergence + uncaught-exception DoS: verifying an attacker-supplied
                        /
                        corrupted snapshot crashes the Windows caller where macOS rejects it).

                        `VerifySnapshot` propagates exceptions. macOS returns false on malformed base64. A
                        caller `if (VerifySnapshot(s))` over untrusted input aborts on Windows.

                        `LeakDetector.Verify`, which already does this).

- **[D069]**            Witness Verify shows contradictory verdicts; no-snapshot case misreported as
                        signature mismatch
- **Criticality:**      Critical; user made aware? Yes (user reported with screenshot).
- **Location:**         macOS/Sources/SyxxApp/WitnessView.swift:117-188 (validation report);
                        macOS/Sources/SyxxApp/AppModel.swift:899-903 (witnessVerify())
- **Issue:**            Three defects in the Witness verification flow produce contradictory
                        user-facing output:

                        **(A) Hardcoded "Signature valid" always renders.** WitnessView.swift:178-188
                        shows a green checkmark with "Signature valid with no evidence of tampering"
                        unconditionally inside the `if model.showValidation` block. It is not
                        conditioned on `model.witnessValid`. So even when `witnessValid == false`,
                        the UI simultaneously shows "Testimony invalid" (line 145) AND "Signature
                        valid" (line 184). Three mutually exclusive statements render at once:
                        (1) "Not yet signed" / the signature string, (2) "Testimony invalid —
                        signature mismatch or snapshot altered", (3) "Signature valid with no
                        evidence of tampering." These cannot all be true.

                        **(B) No-snapshot verify misreported as "signature mismatch."**
                        `witnessVerify()` (:899-903) sets `showValidation = true` BEFORE the guard
                        check. If `witnessSnapshot` is nil (user pressed Verify without first
                        pressing Testimony, or Testimony failed), the guard sets `witnessValid =
                        false` and returns. The UI then renders the full validation report with
                        "Testimony invalid — signature mismatch or snapshot altered" (:150). But the
                        issue is not a mismatched signature — there is no signed snapshot to compare
                        against. The error message is factually wrong. It SHOULD say: "No signed
                        snapshot available for comparison — press Witness Testimony first."

                        **(C) Validation report renders with no data.** `showValidation = true` is
                        set at :900 before the guard at :901 checks whether `witnessSnapshot` exists.
                        This means the entire validation report section (domain, timestamp,
                        signature, verdict) renders even when there is nothing to validate. The
                        domain field (:127) falls back to `model.domain`, the timestamp field is
                        hidden (line 129 `if let snap`), and the signature field shows "Not yet
                        signed" — but the contradictory verdict messages still display.

                        Windows `AppViewModel.cs` (:306-311) has the same `ShowValidation = true`
                        before guard pattern, so defect (C) applies there. The XAML view likely
                        has the same hardcoded "valid" block (defect A).

- **Cross-ref. Delta:** C028 (green banner bug — same root cause: hardcoded success UI not gated on
                        actual verdict state). D069 is the Witness-specific instance of the broader
                        pattern.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Gate the "Signature valid" block (:178-188) on `model.witnessValid`.
                        When `witnessValid == false`, show a red X with "Signature could not be
                        verified" instead.

                        [Fix 2] In `witnessVerify()` (:899-903), set `showValidation = true` only
                        AFTER the guard confirms `witnessSnapshot` is non-nil. When the guard
                        fails because snapshot is nil, set a separate state (e.g.,
                        `witnessError: String?`) and show an honest message: "No signed snapshot
                        available for comparison — press Witness Testimony first." Do NOT render
                        the full validation report.

                        [Fix 3] Replace the hardcoded "signature mismatch or snapshot altered" text
                        (:150) with a tri-state:
                        - `witnessValid == true && witnessSnapshot != nil`: "Signature matches;
                          no tampering detected."
                        - `witnessValid == false && witnessSnapshot != nil`: "Signature mismatch
                          — the snapshot was altered after signing."
                        - `witnessSnapshot == nil`: "No signed snapshot available for comparison."

                        [Fix 4] Apply the same fixes to the Windows WitnessView XAML and
                        `AppViewModel.cs` (:306-311).

- **Code Sample:**      [

                        // AppModel.swift:899-903 — showValidation set before guard
                        func witnessVerify() {
                            showValidation = true           // ← renders report immediately
                            guard let snap = witnessSnapshot, WitnessKeyManager.hasKey
                                else { witnessValid = false; return }  // ← report shows "invalid"
                            witnessValid = (try? WitnessSigner.verifySnapshot(snap)) ?? false
                        }

                        // WitnessView.swift:145-150 — "invalid" message
                        + Text(model.witnessValid
                               ? " — signature matches; no tampering detected."
                               : " — signature mismatch or snapshot altered.")

                        // WitnessView.swift:178-188 — hardcoded "valid" block (always shown)
                        HStack(spacing: 8) {
                            Image(systemName: "checkmark.circle.fill")
                                .foregroundColor(.ioSuccessGreen)
                            Text("Signature ")
                            + Text("valid")
                            + Text(" with no evidence of tampering.")
                        }

                        ]

                       - **Tool Name**            [syxx-neural-researcher]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-13
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Pending user review.

                       - **RESOLUTION**           [FIXED 2026-07-16, macOS] Defects (A), (B), (C) all
                         addressed in `WitnessView.swift` + `AppModel.swift`. Added
                         `AppModel.WitnessVerdict { notVerified, noKey, valid, invalid }` and
                         `@Published witnessVerdict`; `witnessVerify()` now sets an honest verdict per
                         branch (no snapshot → `.notVerified`, no key → `.noKey`, else runs the Ed25519
                         verify → `.valid`/`.invalid`). The view renders ONE verdict row from
                         `witnessVerdict`; the hardcoded green "Signature valid…" block (old :178-188)
                         is DELETED. The no-snapshot case now shows "No signed snapshot available for
                         comparison — press Witness Testimony first" and suppresses the domain/timestamp/
                         signature rows (Fix 2). Reset paths (`resetWitness`/`witnessTestify`) clear the
                         verdict. Verified: `swift build` clean, `swift test` 444/444 pass. Windows
                         side already renders a single gated verdict (`WitnessView.xaml.cs:95+`), so no
                         contradiction there — defect (C)'s cosmetic empty-panel on Windows is not a
                         content-rule violation and is left as-is. NOTE: full E021 forensic tri-state
                         (expired/untrusted/forged distinct) on macOS remains owed (owed-list item 11);
                         this fix removes the contradiction at the Bool level. GUI copy above is my
                         wording, close to but not identical to Fix 3 — pending user approval.

- **[E011]**            Windows WitnessSigner JSON Missing Key Sort
- **Criticality:**      High (cross-platform signature mismatch); user made aware.
- **Location:**         Windows/Syxx.Kit/WitnessSigner.cs:40-44, 89 vs macOS WitnessSigner.swift:97
- **Issue:**            macOS sets `encoder.outputFormatting = [.sortedKeys]` for deterministic,
                        alphabetically ordered payload JSON. Windows `PayloadOptions` sets only a
                        CamelCase naming policy — a naming rule, not an ordering guarantee — so
                        System.Text.Json emits properties in declaration order
                        (timestampEpochMillis, targetDomain, comparison) while macOS signs
                        (comparison, targetDomain, timestampEpochMillis). The signed bytes differ,
                        so a snapshot signed on one platform cannot be verified on the other; .NET
                        declaration order is also not a stable cross-version contract.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Formerly E006. Moved to DELTAS-fixed.md 2026-07-09 on a misread `[FIXED -
                        OPENCODE]` numbering-hold tag; verified NOT fixed and returned. Signatures
                        are now Ed25519 (not HMAC as the original entry said); the ordering problem
                        is unchanged.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Serialize the signed payload with sorted keys on Windows (e.g.,
                        build a sorted JsonNode/dictionary or custom converter) so the bytes match
                        macOS `.sortedKeys` output.
- **Status:**           NOT FIXED (Claude-verified 2026-07-09, working tree): the CamelCase policy
                        recorded at move time does not sort keys; payload property order still
                        differs from macOS.

                       - **Tool Name**            [syxx-researcher]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-10
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       N/A (agree the delta is legitimate; the narrow
                                                  titled defect is fixed in the working tree, but
                                                  the entry's stated impact — cross-platform
                                                  signature verification — is still not achieved,
                                                  so the entry should be revised, not closed.)
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   Two-part status. (1) The KEY-SORT defect as titled
                                                  is FIXED in the working tree (uncommitted):
                                                  WitnessSigner.cs:44-56 `SerializePayloadSorted`
                                                  parses the CamelCase JSON into a JsonObject and
                                                  applies :58-75 `SortRecursive` (recursive
                                                  `OrderBy(k => k.Key)`), and BOTH the sign path
                                                  (:118) and verify path (:168) call it — the stale
                                                  `- **Status:** NOT FIXED` line should be updated.
                                                  (2) Do NOT move to DELTAS-fixed yet: byte-level
                                                  parity with macOS `.sortedKeys`
                                                  (WitnessSigner.swift:105) is still NOT guaranteed
                                                  because the two serializers canonicalize strings
                                                  differently — Swift JSONEncoder escapes `/` as
                                                  `\/` and emits non-ASCII as raw UTF-8, while
                                                  System.Text.Json's default JavaScriptEncoder
                                                  leaves `/` unescaped and emits `\uXXXX` for
                                                  non-ASCII and for `+`, `<`, `>`, `&`. Any payload
                                                  string containing those characters (TXT record
                                                  data, `ErrorMessage`, IDN target domain) produces
                                                  different signed bytes → cross-platform verify
                                                  still fails. LIKELY (API semantics, not executed —
                                                  no cross-platform byte-equality harness exists).
                                                  This residual is NOT covered by B026 (legacy
                                                  PascalCase snapshots, DELTAS.md:1328) or B027
                                                  (snapshot FILE case-sensitivity, :1348). Revised
                                                  fix: define one canonical payload encoding (e.g.,
                                                  UnsafeRelaxedJsonEscaping + assert ASCII-only
                                                  fields, or RFC 8785 JCS-style canonicalization on
                                                  both sides) and add a fixture asserting the two
                                                  platforms sign identical bytes for a payload
                                                  containing `/`, `+`, and non-ASCII. Effort M.
                                                  Criticality High stands (forgeable-evidence-
                                                  adjacent: honest snapshots read as "INVALID /
                                                  TAMPERED" cross-platform — a false tampered
                                                  verdict).

- **[B030]**            Windows LeakDetector Has No Throwing Path — All Servers Always "sent" →
                         Any Interception Returns NotDetected (False Negative)
- **Criticality:**      Critical (quick-guide #1 false "no leak" verdict, #2 real interception
                         undetected, #4 platform-divergent verdicts: macOS returns Inconclusive,
                         Windows returns NotDetected; resolution: Critical, not Medium, per
                         [syxx-researcher] 2026-07-10); analysis 2026-07-09, corrected 2026-07-10.
- **Location:**        Windows/Syxx.Kit/LeakDetector.cs:218-240 (TriggerQueriesAsync);
                         DNSResolver.cs:119-122 (QueryUDPAsync — no status check);
                         DNSResolver.cs:191-202 (QueryUDPDetailedAsync — never throws on
                         transport/protocol failure, returns Timeout response at :204)
- **Issue:**            Unlike macOS (which throws via `recordsOrThrow` on timeout/mismatch/truncated/
                         transport failure, DNSResolver.swift:265-266, 1178-1193), Windows
                         `QueryUDPDetailedAsync` (DNSResolver.cs:179-212) catches everything except
                         OperationCanceledException and returns a Timeout DNSResponse at :204.
                         Its caller `QueryUDPAsync` (:119-122) passes `.Records` through with no
                         status check. Therefore `TriggerQueriesAsync` (LeakDetector.cs:218-240) sets
                         `results[server] = true` for EVERY server — including total blackhole /
                         no-response / transport failure. The E007 all-failed guard (:125) is
                         unreachable dead code. Consequence chain: fully intercepted or blackholed
                         DNS → collector verify sees nothing → `leaked=false, observedResolvers=[]`
                         → `ReconcileVerdict` (LeakDetector.cs:206-213) returns NotDetected — a false
                         "no leak detected" where macOS honestly returns Inconclusive. Note: macOS is
                         NOT suspect-parity — it correctly records false via the throwing path.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Related D004 (collector signature verification). macOS LeakDetector verified
                         correct (throws on failure, per [syxx-researcher] 2026-07-10).
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix A — the real fix, S effort] In TriggerQueriesAsync call
                         QueryUDPDetailedAsync and count dispatch success ONLY for answered statuses
                         (Success/NoData/NxDomain/Refused/ServFail), mirroring macOS recordsOrThrow
                         semantics — Timeout / ResponseIdMismatch / Malformed / TransportError /
                         Truncated ⇒ false. This resurrects the E007 guard.
                         [Fix B — honesty, S] Rename the user-facing claim from "sent" to "answered"
                         (or tri-state answered/no-answer/unknown): even a genuine answer only proves
                         a responder exists, not delivery to the configured resolver — against an
                         on-path adversary the collector attestation is the only delivery proof.
                         (User approval needed for wording.)
                         Note: TXID match (proposed as Fix 1 in initial filing) is ALREADY
                         implemented (DNSResolver.cs:445-449) and does not fix this — a mismatch is
                         returned as a status, not thrown, and TXID cannot defeat an on-path
                         responder who reads the query.

                                                `(await QueryUDPDetailedAsync(query)).Records` with
