- **[C007]**            AuthoritativeVantage MajorityConsensus Accepts Single-Responder Data as
                         Unquestioned Ground Truth
- **Criticality:**      Critical (false-"secure" verdict: 2-of-3 bootstrap blockade → single-source
                         delegation accepted → attacker-supplied NS can meet AA quorum → `.matches`
                         rules out tampering); analysis 2026-07-09, upgraded per [syxx-researcher].
- **Location:**        macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/AuthoritativeVantage.swift:213 (majorityConsensus);
                         Windows/Syxx.Kit/AuthoritativeVantage.cs:164 (same)
- **Issue:**            `MajorityConsensus()` requires ≥2 agreeing resolvers. When only 1 resolver
                         responds (the other 2 are blocked by the network, e.g. a corporate firewall
                         blocking 8.8.8.8 and 9.9.9.9 while allowing 1.1.1.1), it returns the single
                        set unconditionally: `if (sets.Count == 1) return sets[0]`. An attacker who
                        can block 2 of 3 bootstrap resolvers can force single-responder fallback and
                        supply arbitrary delegation data through the remaining resolver path. Since
                        authoritative truth anchors the entire comparison chain (Mirror, Witness),
                        this degrades ground truth across all downstream verdicts.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** B012 (single bootstrap resolver, FIXED — this is the MajorityConsensus
                         quorum-degradation residual). C007 on both platforms.
- **Dependency:** B031 (ALL call sites still pass a single-element bootstrap array — ProbePlan.swift:109,
                         SyxxCLI.swift:239). C007 Fix 1 cannot land BEFORE B031, or the authoritative
                         probe goes permanently inconclusive from every current call site (silently
                         disabling the A2 datapoint). Order: B031 first, then C007.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] When `sets.Count == 1`, return an `inconclusive`/`uncertain` ground
                        truth state instead of accepting single-source data.
                        [Fix 2] Mark the authoritative comparison as `Degraded` when ground truth
                        is single-source.
                        [Fix 3] Log which resolver was the sole responder.

                       - **Tool Name**            [syxx-researcher]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-10
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       N/A
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   Confirmed on both platforms, with a location
                                                  correction for macOS. The defect is NOT in
                                                  compare() (:66-119 as cited) — it is in
                                                  majorityConsensus itself:
                                                  AuthoritativeVantage.swift:213 `guard sets.count >=
                                                  2 else { return sets[0] }` (the docstring :209-210
                                                  even says "otherwise returns the (only) set"),
                                                  reached from discoverNameservers at :198. Windows
                                                  cite is exact: AuthoritativeVantage.cs:164 `if
                                                  (sets.Count == 1) return sets[0];`. Not a duplicate:
                                                  B012 added the 3-resolver bootstrap (the ≥2
                                                  consensus exists only because of it) and B011 added
                                                  the AA-answer quorum (.swift:116-122, .cs:81-88);
                                                  C007 is the degradation residual both left open —
                                                  when 2 of 3 bootstraps are blocked, the ENTIRE
                                                  delegation (NS hosts, then NS IPs via the
                                                  union loop .swift:91-99) is single-sourced, and the
                                                  B011 quorum is then satisfiable by ≥2
                                                  attacker-supplied NS IPs agreeing with each other.
                                                  Concretely: an attacker who firewalls 8.8.8.8 +
                                                  9.9.9.9 (cheap — port-53 IP blocks, no on-path
                                                  forgery needed) and controls the remaining resolver
                                                  path can hand the walker fake NS that serve the
                                                  hijacked answer with AA set, producing status
                                                  `.matches` — which per the module header
                                                  (.swift:10-11) "rules out" resolver manipulation.
                                                  That is a false-secure contribution to synthesis,
                                                  and no downstream field records that ground truth
                                                  was single-source. CRITICALITY: recommend
                                                  enhancement High → Critical under the quick guide
                                                  (#1 false "secure"-leaning verdict, #2 real
                                                  tampering undetected, #3 forgeable evidence);
                                                  mitigating context — a fully on-path attacker
                                                  defeats the 3-way plaintext-UDP bootstrap consensus
                                                  regardless (all three legs are unauthenticated udp/53),
                                                  but C007 lowers the required capability from
                                                  on-path forgery to block-two-plus-poison-one.
                                                  Fixes 1-3 are sound and correctly tri-state
                                                  (single-source → `.inconclusive`, never accepted
                                                  ground truth); effort S (~2h both platforms +
                                                  offline QueryFn-injected tests simulating 2-of-3
                                                  bootstrap timeout — validation must assert
                                                  `.inconclusive`, not just non-crash). Adjacent gap
                                                  worth its own delta (speculative, not filed here):
                                                  bootstrap discovery over plaintext udp/53 has no
                                                  transport integrity at all; DoH bootstrap for
                                                  delegation discovery would raise the floor.

- **[B031]**            Refactor Call Sites Pass a SINGLE Bootstrap Resolver — Defeats the B012 Multi-Bootstrap Consensus Fix
- **Criticality:**      Critical (can cause false confidence; regresses a delta already marked
                        FIXED). Authoritative delegation anchors the highest-weight evidence
                        (`authoritativeDiverges` / `authoritativeDivergesConfirmed`).
- **Location:**         ALL FOUR FRONTENDS: macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/ProbePlan.swift:103-110
                        (`bootstrapResolvers: [trustedBootstrap]`); Windows/Syxx.Kit/ProbePlan.cs:105-110
                        (same single-element array); macOS/Sources/SyxxCLI/SyxxCLI.swift:237-240;
                        Windows/Syxx/Program.cs:260-262. GUIs route through ProbePlan: macOS
                        AppModel.swift:259, Windows AppViewModel.cs:135/162/183. Sink:
                        macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/AuthoritativeVantage.swift:211-213 (`guard sets.count >= 2
                        else { return sets[0] }`); Windows/Syxx.Kit/AuthoritativeVantage.cs equivalent.
- **Issue:**            B012's fix defaulted `AuthoritativeVantage.compare` to a 3-resolver bootstrap
                        set with majority consensus (≥2 agreeing) so one poisoned/blocked resolver
                        cannot control the NS delegation set. The new shared `ProbePlan.runMirror`
                        and BOTH CLIs override that default with a ONE-element array
                        (`localResolver == "1.1.1.1" ? "9.9.9.9" : "1.1.1.1"`). With a single
                        bootstrap, `majorityConsensus` degenerates to "return the only set" — consensus
                        can never engage even on a clean network — and NS→IP resolution is single-
                        sourced. An attacker who poisons the one chosen bootstrap steers the
                        "authoritative" ground truth. The macOS GUI now routes through ProbePlan
                        (`AppModel.swift:259`), so it is affected too.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** B012 (FIXED — this is a working-tree regression that silently undoes it at the
                        call site). Distinct from C007: C007 is the FUNCTION accepting single-responder
                        data when the network blocks 2 of 3; this is the CALLERS supplying only 1 by
                        construction, so consensus never engages even on a clean network. Checked
                        DELTAS.md A–F, DELTAS-fixed.md, SERVER_DELTAS.md — not a duplicate.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Pass the full 3-resolver default (or the default set minus the
                        resolver-under-test, still ≥2) from `ProbePlan.runMirror` and both CLIs.
                        [Fix 2] Guard `AuthoritativeVantage.compare` to treat a `<2`-element
                        `bootstrapResolvers` as `.inconclusive`/`.degraded` rather than silently
                        single-sourcing (overlaps C007 Fix 1).
- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED (call sites and consensus fallthrough read directly, both platforms).

- **[B032]**            macOS Infers "Encrypted DNS = yes (DoH/DoT)" From a VPN/Tunnel Interface — False Clean Transport Signal
- **Criticality:**      High (false confidence / missed detection). A hostile VPN/transparent-proxy
                        tunnel — the interception adversary Syxx targets — is turned into a CLEAN
                        transport signal.
- **Location:**         macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/NetworkKeyState.swift:387-393 (tunnel branch →
                        `EncryptedDNSStatus(state: .yes, "…tunneled through VPN interface(s)…")`),
                        :401-402 (`isDNSEncrypted()` now returns `state == .yes`); consumer
                        macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/Synthesis/Synthesizer.swift:360-372 (`.dnsEncrypted`
                        → `.negative` clean sub-signal); macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/Trust/Sentinel.swift:29.
- **Issue:**            Three defects in one change. (a) Mislabel: a resolver merely on a
                        `utun`/`ppp`/`ipsec`/`wg` interface is reported `.yes` with the user-visible
                        string "System DNS is encrypted (DoH/DoT)" — but a tunnel does not imply
                        DoH/DoT; the DNS inside may be plain Do53 and the tunnel endpoint may be the
                        tamperer. (b) False-confidence dampener: `.yes` emits a `.negative` (clean)
                        sub-signal in the DST engine, so a malicious VPN earns a clean transport
                        verdict that structurally suppresses the on-path/interception frame. (c)
                        Conservative-default regression: `isDNSEncrypted()` previously returned a
                        hardcoded `false` ("to prevent false security claims") and now returns `true`
                        off the tunnel heuristic, feeding Sentinel and `resolveSecurely`. The explicit
                        `scutil` Protocol=DoH/DoT branch (:375-385) is sound; only the tunnel inference
                        and the `isDNSEncrypted()` default are the problem.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** E014 (ex-E009) records the macOS-never-yes vs Windows-yes divergence and its
                        Fix explicitly recommends the SAFER direction — report `.unknown` unless DoH is
                        confirmed. This working-tree change moved macOS the OPPOSITE way (yes on a
                        weaker signal than Windows' registry template), so it is a new, distinct defect,
                        not the tracked parity item. Not a duplicate of B009/B021. SCOPE: macOS-only
                        (Windows NetworkKeyState.cs was not modified and has no tunnel heuristic), so
                        this also WIDENS the E014 divergence — macOS now reports `.yes` on two signals
                        (scutil Protocol OR tunnel interface) while Windows reports `.yes` only on a
                        registry DoH template: three different truth conditions for the same claim.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Return `.unknown` (not `.yes`) for the tunnel-interface case, or
                        downgrade its synthesis sub-status to `.inconclusive`; reserve `.yes`/
                        `.dnsEncrypted` for the confirmed `scutil` DoH/DoT branch. [Fix 2] Revert
                        `isDNSEncrypted()` to derive only from the confirmed-protocol path. [Fix 3] Fix
                        the observation wording so it never says "DoH/DoT" for a tunnel (user-visible
                        string — needs User approval before implementation).
- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED (code paths + clean-signal wiring); LIKELY (end-to-end verdict-flip
                        magnitude, not executed).

- **[A019]**            Stripe `pending-mint` Idempotency Burns Webhook Retries After Keygen Outage
- **Criticality:**      Critical (paid customer can be charged but never receive a license after a
                        transient Keygen/mail path failure; retry path collapses to "duplicate" instead
                        of retrying fulfillment); analysis 2026-07-10.
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/fulfillment.py:73-95
- **Issue:**            Checkout fulfillment reserves `stripe_evt:<event_id>` as `"processing"` before
                        minting the Keygen license (`fulfillment.py:78,84`). If `_keygen_create_license`
                        fails or returns no key, the handler records `"pending-mint"` at :93-95 and
                        returns success-ish application state. On Stripe's later retry of the same event,
                        the first branch sees the existing `stripe_evt:` key and returns `"duplicate"`
                        at :78-79, so the mint is not retried. That turns a transient dependency outage
                        into a permanent paid-license delivery failure.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Same failure class as `Server/SERVER_DELTAS.md` SD-11; not previously present
                        as a main `DELTAS.md` entry. Distinct from A013: `kv_insert_once` stops duplicate
                        minting, but here it also prevents retrying a known-unfinished mint.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Treat `"pending-mint"` as retryable: if the idempotency key exists with
                        pending state, retry/reconcile rather than returning duplicate. [Fix 2] Mark a
                        Stripe event final only after a license is minted and customer mapping is stored.
                        [Fix 3] Return a retriable failure to Stripe or enqueue a reconciliation job when
                        Keygen is unavailable.
- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED (source-read; no live Stripe/Keygen run performed).

                                                  failure `key` is falsy, :94 `kv_set(...,"pending-mint")`, :95 returns
                                                  "pending-mint". On Stripe's retry of the SAME event, :78
                                                  `kv_insert_once` fails (key already exists) → `not False` → returns

- **[A020]**            Server DNS Oracle Accepts Wrong-Question and Off-Source UDP Replies as Evidence
- **Criticality:**      Critical (server-side clean-vantage / authoritative ground truth can be poisoned
                        by a packet that only matches TXID+QR, undermining `/api/authoritative`,
                        `/api/diff`, `/api/trace`, and `/api/investigate` evidence); analysis
                        2026-07-10.
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/resolver.py:98-126,146-158,304-321,324-348
- **Issue:**            The server resolver validates transaction ID and QR bit, but never verifies that
                        the echoed question name/type/class matches the query. `_parse_response` skips the
                        question section without comparing it to the requested name/type
                        (`resolver.py:109-112`), and `_parse_sections` does the same for iterative
                        authoritative responses (`resolver.py:313-316`). Both UDP paths ignore the source
                        returned by `recvfrom` (`resolver.py:152-153`, :330-331), so a spoofed/stray UDP
                        reply that guesses the TXID can be parsed as recursive or authoritative evidence
                        even if it answered a different question or came from a different peer.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Distinct from client KDNS-02 fixes: macOS and Windows `DNSResolver` now check
                        response questions (`DNSResolver.swift:289-297,358-363`;
                        `DNSResolver.cs:150-161,296-302`). This is the independent Python server resolver.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Parse and compare response question qname/qtype/qclass against the query
                        before accepting any answer or referral. [Fix 2] Use connected UDP sockets or
                        explicitly validate `recvfrom` peer IP/port against the intended resolver. [Fix 3]
                        On mismatch, return typed DNS error/inconclusive evidence rather than clean or
                        divergent ground truth.
- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED (source-read; no packet-injection run performed).

                       - **Tool Name**            [syxx-researcher]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-10

                       - **Disagree Basis**       Confirmed live. `_parse_response` skips the question section without
                                                  comparing qname/qtype/qclass (resolver.py:110-112); `_parse_sections`
                                                  does the same (:314-316). Both UDP recv paths discard the peer:
                                                  `data, _ = sock.recvfrom(4096)` at :153 (recursive) and :331 (iterative
                                                  walker). Only TXID (:102/:309) and QR bit (:104/:311) are checked, so a
                                                  spoofed/stray reply that guesses the 16-bit TXID and answers a DIFFERENT
                                                  question — or comes from a different peer — is accepted as recursive or
                                                  authoritative evidence. This is the independent Python resolver; the
                                                  clients already fixed the twin (KDNS-02). All cited line ranges verified
                                                  accurate. Fixes 1-3 correct (question-match + connected-UDP/peer-check +
                                                  typed-inconclusive on mismatch).
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   None. Note adversarial reachability: off-path requires TXID guess + race,
                                                  but this is exactly the tamper class Syxx exists to withstand, and it
                                                  feeds /api/authoritative, /api/diff, /api/trace, /api/investigate — the
                                                  server's ground-truth. Critical stands.

- **[A021]**            Server Paid-Route Entitlement Trusts Unsigned Keygen `meta.valid` JSON
- **Criticality:**      High (server-side Pro entitlement is a TLS-only online boolean; a compromised
                        server trust store, pinned-proxy deployment, or Keygen-path hijack can forge paid
                        access to collector/ground-truth routes); analysis 2026-07-10.
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/licensing.py:101-132
- **Issue:**            `_validate_keygen` POSTs the supplied license key to Keygen and returns `"pro"`
                        solely from `meta.valid` in the JSON response (`licensing.py:118-132`). The server
                        does distinguish transient Keygen failures from invalid keys, which is good
                        tri-state behavior, but the accepted entitlement itself is not signed or verified
                        against a Keygen public key/offline license artifact. The paid server routes
                        therefore inherit the network/TLS trust boundary rather than a cryptographic
                        license-verification boundary.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Related to D003's client-side TLS-pinning note for Keygen/collector calls, but
                        distinct: this is the server's authorization decision for paid API routes, not a
                        client display or transport-pinning gap.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Verify a signed Keygen license artifact or signed validation response
                        before granting server-side Pro entitlement. [Fix 2] If Keygen cannot provide a
                        verifiable artifact, pin the Keygen service identity and cache only bounded,
                        auditable positive entitlements. [Fix 3] Treat unverifiable validation as
                        transient/unknown, not as a trustworthy paid-route authorization.
- **Tag:**              FIXED (Opencode 2026-07-11). Implemented Ed25519 response signature verification
                        (A021 Fix 1) — see below for evaluator notes.

- **[A022]**            Ephemeral Collector Signing Key on Restart Silently Orphans All Attestations
- **Criticality:**      Critical (collector Ed25519 attestations become unverifiable after any server
                        restart, and would permanently break D011's client-side pinned collector pubkey;
                        auto-critical — unverifiable/forgeable evidence). Confirmed 2026-07-10.
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/leak.py:44-66 (`_ensure_collector_key`)
- **Issue:**            When `SYXX_COLLECTOR_PRIVATE_KEY` is unset, `_ensure_collector_key()` generates a
                        fresh in-memory Ed25519 key at startup and only logs a warning; the key is never
                        persisted. On every restart a new key is generated, silently invalidating all
                        prior collector attestations and breaking any client that has pinned the collector
                        public key (WS3.1 / D011). Evidence appears valid but is cryptographically
                        orphaned, with no user-visible error.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Hard blocker for D011's collector-pinning half; related to A006 (Ed25519 leak
                        attestation, CF-01). Surfaced as Appendix-B of HANDOFF-OPENCODE.md during WS3.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Fail closed: if `SYXX_COLLECTOR_PRIVATE_KEY` is unset in a non-dev run,
                        refuse to start (exit with a clear error) rather than minting an ephemeral key.
                        [Fix 2] Alternatively persist a generated key to disk (e.g. `/var/lib/syxx/
                        collector_key`) with 0600 perms; fail-closed is preferred for a trust anchor.
                        [Fix 3] Expose a stable key id so clients can detect deliberate rotation.
- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED (source-read, independently verified 2026-07-10; Claude-verified).

                       - **Tool Name**            [syxx-researcher]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-10

                                                  live in leak.py:44-80: with `SYXX_COLLECTOR_PRIVATE_KEY` unset and no
                                                  `SYXX_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL_COLLECTOR_KEY=1` escape, `_ensure_collector_key()`
                                                  raises RuntimeError (:67-77) instead of minting an ephemeral key. The
                                                  ephemeral branch (:57-66) is now a documented dev/test-only escape.
                                                  Fix 3 (stable key id) also present: `_COLLECTOR_KEY_ID` at :80. Fix 2
                                                  (persist-to-disk) intentionally NOT taken — the delta itself preferred
                                                  fail-closed, so this is complete. Caveat: commit note records the Ed25519
                                                  path was not runtime-exercised (`cryptography` absent in that sandbox);
                                                  the fail-closed raise IS the load-bearing behavior and is verifiable by

                       - **Proposed Revisions**   MOVE-TO-FIXED citing f2861b5 (fail-closed, A022 Fix 1). Recommend one

- **[B036]**            AuthoritativeVantage Tests Lock In `Both Empty == Matches` Without Encoding the
                        Required Evidence Premise
- **Criticality:**      High (missing resolver/authority evidence can be treated as a clean consistency
                        signal; tests pass because they assert the softened behavior directly). Static
                        test audit 2026-07-10.
- **Location:**         macOS/Tests/SyxxKitTests/AuthoritativeVantageTests.swift:60-63
                        (`testMatchesWhenBothEmpty`);
                        macOS/Tests/SyxxKitTests/AuthoritativeVantageTests.swift:114-115
                        (`testClassifyDirect` asserts empty resolver/auth sets are `.matches`);
                        Windows/Syxx.Tests/SyxxKitTests.cs:1425-1429
                        (`ClassifyMatchesWhenBothEmpty`).
- **Issue:**            The classifier receives only answer sets, not the recursive resolver's status or
                        the authoritative response status. The tests nevertheless assert `.matches` when
                        both sets are empty. That assertion can only be safe if both sides are known,
                        parsed, validated negative answers; the test does not encode or verify that
                        premise. If a timeout, parse failure, delegation failure, or skipped resolver probe
                        is collapsed upstream to an empty answer set, these tests still pass while the
                        product converts "no evidence" into "consistent with ground truth."
- **Missing Failure
  Case(s):**            [1] Add a production-path test where the resolver side has no usable evidence
                        (timeout/transport error/parse failure) and authoritative no-data exists; expected
                        status must be `.inconclusive`, not `.matches`. [2] If "both authoritative no-data
                        and recursive no-data" is intentionally clean, model that as an explicit typed
                        negative-evidence input rather than a bare empty set, and add a failure case proving
                        empty-from-failure cannot reach `.matches`. [3] Keep the existing positive case
                        only after the required negative-evidence premise is visible in the API and test.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Related to B011/C007/B031's "ground truth before evidence" family, but this is a
                        current test assertion that preserves an empty-evidence clean match.
- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED (static test audit; no network-dependent tests run).

                                                  `.matches` at :114-115; Windows `ClassifyMatchesWhenBothEmpty` at
                                                  SyxxKitTests.cs:1488. The structural concern is real: `classify()`
                                                  receives bare answer SETS (no status), so it cannot distinguish

                                                  locks in `[],[] → .matches`. QUALIFIER on criticality (ground 2): at the

                                                  BEFORE classify is reached — verified by sibling tests

                                                  `testInconclusiveWhenNoNameservers` (:65-71). So there is no CURRENT live

- **[B037]**            WitnessSigner Display-Integrity Guard Omits `resolverQueryOutcomes` — Tampered
                        Per-Resolver Display Verifies as Authentic
- **Criticality:**      Critical (forgeable evidence: a witness snapshot whose displayed per-resolver
                        outcomes were altered can still verify true); user to be made aware.
- **Location:**         macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/WitnessSigner.swift (verifySnapshot display-integrity
                        guard); Windows twin `Windows/Syxx.Kit/WitnessSigner.cs`.
- **Issue:**            The guard re-projects the display fields into a `SignedEvidencePayload` and
                        compares `rebuilt.queryId == evidence.queryId` and `rebuilt.comparisonResult ==
                        evidence.comparisonResult`, but does NOT compare `resolverQueryOutcomes`. The
                        signed evidence includes `resolverQueryOutcomes` (they are in `canonicalBytes()`),
                        so the Ed25519 check protects the SIGNED copy — but a mismatch between the
                        DISPLAYED per-resolver outcomes (`snapshot.comparison`) and the signed evidence
                        is unchecked. An attacker who alters a displayed per-resolver answer while the
                        aggregate verdict/answer-sets stay equal passes both the guard and the signature,
                        so a viewer sees tampered per-resolver evidence marked "authentic".
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Exposed by the missing witness corrupt-signature / display-coverage tests
                        (see B034-B036 audit cluster). E011/D015 landed the canonical DTO + guard.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Add `rebuilt.resolverQueryOutcomes == evidence.resolverQueryOutcomes`
                        to the guard on both platforms. [Fix 2] Add a §3 test: tamper one displayed
                        per-resolver outcome (verdict/sets unchanged) → verifySnapshot must return false.
- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED (source-read both platforms; no forged-snapshot run performed).

- **[B038]**            DualStack Renders `ipv4Suppressed` Censorship Signal on an A-Record TIMEOUT —
                        Failure Rendered as a Verdict (§1 Violation)
- **Criticality:**      Critical (a missing datum — A query timeout/transport failure — is reported as a
                        selective-IPv4-blocking/censorship signal; §1 "a failure must never render as a
                        verdict"); user to be made aware.
- **Location:**         macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/DualStackProbe.swift (`classify`, the
                        `aaaaOk && !aOk → .ipv4Suppressed` branch); Windows twin `DualStackProbe.cs`.
- **Issue:**            `classify` sets `aOk = aStatus == .success && !aAddrs.isEmpty`, then the guard
                        passes when `aaaaOk` is true, and `if aaaaOk && !aOk` returns `.ipv4Suppressed`
                        ("AAAA resolves but A does not — corroborate for selective blocking"). `!aOk`
                        conflates a GENUINE negative (`nxDomain`/`noData`) with a FAILURE
                        (`timeout`/`transportError`/`servFail`). So an A-query that timed out while AAAA
                        works is classified as a censorship-leaning signal instead of inconclusive — a
                        verdict on a missing datum. Only the `aOk && aaaaDenied` path checks for a genuine
                        negative; the suppression path does not.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Exposed by the missing DualStack failure-path test (audit set 1, offender #1).
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Gate `.ipv4Suppressed` on a GENUINE A negative (`aDenied`), i.e.
                        `aaaaOk && aDenied → .ipv4Suppressed`; a non-negative A failure with AAAA ok →
                        `.inconclusive` ("A did not resolve — transport failure, cannot audit"). [Fix 2]
                        Add a §3 test: A `.timeout` + AAAA success → `.inconclusive`, never
                        `.ipv4Suppressed`. Port to Windows.
- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED (source-read `classify`; no live dual-stack run performed).

- **[C009]**            Exfil Analyzer Flags a Benign Domain as `suspicious` — Possible False Positive
- **Criticality:**      High if confirmed (a false 'DNS exfiltration/tunnelling' signal on ordinary
                        traffic erodes trust and could mislead a verdict); UNVERIFIED. Observed
                        2026-07-10.
- **Location:**         macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/Forensics/ExfilAnalyzer.swift (classification →
                        `ExfilSuspicion`); observed via MonitorReportAnalyzerTests fixture.
- **Issue:**            While strengthening `testHighEntropyTunnelDomainIsAssessed`, a benign
                        co-domain in the fixture (from `benignRecords()`) came back with
                        `suspicion == .suspicious`. Either the entropy/label heuristic over-flags an
                        ordinary domain (a real efficacy false positive) OR the fixture contains a
                        domain that legitimately trips the heuristic. Not root-caused (did not
                        rabbit-hole, per instruction).
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Surfaced during the §3 test audit sweep. Related to the exfil/tunnelling
                        datapoint.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Reproduce: dump the flagged benign domain + its entropy/label metrics;
                        confirm whether it's a heuristic over-trigger or a fixture artifact. [Fix 2] If
                        a real FP, tighten the threshold / require corroboration (beacon cadence +
                        entropy + blocklist) before `.suspicious`; add a fixed benign-domain
                        false-positive regression test.
- **Tag:**              OBSERVED (test-fixture; not reproduced against real capture).

                       - **Tool Name**            [syxx-researcher]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-10
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree — STAY-OPEN, and UPGRADE from OBSERVED to CONFIRMED (root-caused).
                       - **Disagree Basis**       REPRODUCED and root-caused by source read (build is currently broken by
                                                  B033, so run-verification was not possible; this is a deterministic code
                                                  trace, not a live capture). Root cause is TWO-fold:
                                                  (1) FIXTURE ARTIFACT: every record in `benignRecords()` is stamped with
                                                    the SAME hardcoded timestamp "2026-07-06 12:00:00.000"
                                                    (MonitorReportAnalyzerTests.swift:18). For the benign domain
                                                    "example.com" the 12 identical timestamps produce 11 inter-arrival
                                                    intervals all equal to 0 → BeaconAnalyzer.score: `mean = 0`,
                                                    `cv = mean == 0 ? 0 : …` = 0 (BeaconAnalyzer.swift:53), and
                                                    `classification(for: 0)` → `cv < 0.05` → `.highlyRegular` (:66). So
                                                    `regular = true` in ExfilAnalyzer.
                                                  (2) REAL DESIGN FALSE-POSITIVE (the substantive part): "example.com" has
                                                    only two labels → `longestSubdomainLabel` returns "" → entropy 0 →
                                                    `highEntropy = false`. Yet ExfilAnalyzer flags
                                                    `else if highEntropy || regular { suspicion = .suspicious }`
                                                    (ExfilAnalyzer.swift:80-81). So `.suspicious` fires on CADENCE ALONE,
                                                    with zero encoded-label signal and no blocklist hit. The module doc
                                                    (:3-6) claims it "fuses three signals into one honest verdict," but the
                                                    code fires on ANY ONE of {highEntropy, regular}. Regular cadence alone
                                                    is ubiquitous in benign traffic (OS/telemetry polling, keepalives, NTP),
                                                    so this is a genuine live FP class, not merely a fixture quirk.
                                                  Secondary defect: BeaconAnalyzer treating identical/zero-mean timestamps
                                                  as the STRONGEST regularity (`.highlyRegular`) is a §6 degenerate-input
                                                  problem — coincident events carry no cadence signal and should be
                                                  `.insufficientData`, not maximal regularity.
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   UPGRADE to CONFIRMED, criticality High (real efficacy FP). Add fixes:
                                                  [Fix A] Do not emit `.suspicious` on `regular` alone — require corroboration
                                                    (regular + high-entropy, or regular + blocklist, or high-entropy alone
                                                    since an encoded label is itself strong). Single-signal `regular` should
                                                    be `.inconclusive`, not `.suspicious`.
                                                  [Fix B] BeaconAnalyzer: map zero-mean / identical-timestamp series to
                                                    `.insufficientData`, not `.highlyRegular` (BeaconAnalyzer.swift:53,65-68).
                                                  [Fix C] Fix the fixture to use distinct, realistic timestamps so
                                                    `benignRecords()` does not manufacture a zero-variance cadence
                                                    (MonitorReportAnalyzerTests.swift:18) — and add a fixed benign-domain
                                                    FP regression test asserting example.com → `.benign`/`.inconclusive`,
                                                    never `.suspicious`.
                                                  Fix A is the load-bearing efficacy fix; Fixes B/C harden the input and lock
                                                  the regression. Note: NX/blocklist `matches` was not exercised (SieveBlocklist
                                                  bundled lists) — the trigger here is purely the cadence path.

- **Location:**         macOS/Sources/SyxxApp/MirrorView.swift; macOS/Sources/SyxxApp/AppModel.swift:254-282
- **Issue:**            When the user runs Mirror, the app prompts for administrator privileges
                        (via AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges or osascript elevation) five
                        separate times, even after the user clicks "Always Allow" in the macOS
                        authorization dialog. This suggests the authorization reference is not being
                        reused, or each sub-probe (vantage comparison, warp, etc.) is independently
                        requesting elevation. The repeated prompts are disruptive and suggest the
                        authorization session is not being cached.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Not covered elsewhere.
- **Fix(es):**          Ensure the AuthorizationRef is created once and reused across all
                        sub-operations in a single Mirror run. If each probe independently calls
                        `sudo` or `osascript` elevation, consolidate to a single authorization
                        request at the start of the Mirror workflow.

- **Issue:**            The Mirror view displays "Tampering Detected" but does not explain what
                        specific evidence (DNS answer mismatch, IP drift, content divergence, etc.)
                        led to that conclusion. The user cannot evaluate the verdict because the

- **[F014]**            App Stays Behind Other Windows — Clicking Dock Icon Does Not Bring Window Forward
- **Criticality:**      Critical; prevents basic app usage.
- **Location:**         macOS/Sources/SyxxApp/SyxxApp.swift; macOS/Sources/SyxxApp/ContentView.swift
- **Issue:**            The Syxx app window stays behind other application windows. Clicking the
                        app's Dock icon does not bring the window to front — the user must manually
                        locate the window in the stack and move other windows behind it. This is
                        likely caused by the custom titlebar configuration (`titlebarAppearsTransparent`,
                        `titleVisibility = .hidden`) or the `NSPanel` used for About/Update/EULA
                        panels interfering with the window's ordering behavior. The app may also
                        lack `NSWindow.activate()` calls in the `applicationDidBecomeActive` delegate.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Not covered elsewhere.
- **Fix(es):**          Add `NSApp.activate(ignoringOtherApps: true)` in the
                        `applicationDidBecomeActive` delegate method. Ensure the main window has
                        `level = .normal` (not `.floating` or `.statusBar`). Check if any NSPanel
                        usage is setting the window level incorrectly. Consider adding
                        `window.makeKeyAndOrderFront(nil)` on Dock icon click.
- **Code Sample:**      [

                        // SyxxAppDelegate.swift — applicationDidFinishLaunching does not
                        // configure window ordering behavior. applicationDidBecomeActive is
                        // not implemented, so clicking the Dock icon doesn't activate the app.

- **[A023]**            Leak Resolver IP Mirrored Into Cross-Readable passive_dns — PII/Deanon Leak
- **Criticality:**      Critical (PII retention and release — auto-enhanced per server-side
                        criticality rule 4; a leak submitter's resolver IP becomes cross-readable to
                        other users).
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/leak.py:119-121; Server/syxx_server/db.py:260-269;
                        Server/syxx_server/app.py:845-852
- **Issue:**            A leak submitter's resolver IP is mirrored into the shared `passive_dns`
                        index, survives the one-time `consume()`, is cross-readable by any caller of
                        `/api/passive-dns` (no ownership check), and is kept 30 days — a
                        PII/deanonymization leak that lets an unrelated user read the resolver IPs
                        of others' leak tests.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Confirms/extends A002 (leak-zone privacy).
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Do not mirror leak-zone observations into the passive index (or
                        namespace them non-queryable).
                        [Fix 2] Delete matching passive rows inside `leak_token_consume`.
                        [Fix 3] Ownership-gate `/api/passive-dns` for leak zones.
- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED

- **[A024]**            Collector Signs leaked:false With Zero Liveness Evidence — Forgeable Signed
                        No-Leak
- **Criticality:**      Critical (forgeable collector-attested evidence — auto-enhanced per server-
                        side criticality rule 3; also client-side forgeable-evidence rule 2).
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/leak.py:140-164 (`"leaked": len(resolvers)>0` at :144)
- **Issue:**            The collector Ed25519-signs `leaked:false` with ZERO collector-liveness
                        evidence — a signed no-leak clean verdict is indistinguishable from
                        collector-never-bound / stalled / path-blocked. An attacker who blocks the
                        collector path obtains a cryptographically signed "no leak" that reads as
                        trustworthy.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Cross-ref B030 (leak-on-timeout reads clean) and D004 (client does not
                        enforce signature).
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Attestation must carry collector-liveness proof (the path was
                        actually exercised).
                        [Fix 2] Absent that proof, render unknown/inconclusive — never a signed
                        `leaked:false`.
- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED

                       - **Tool Name**            [Claude]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-11
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       N/A
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   The structural problem is correct: the server signs
                                                  `leaked:false` on zero collector observations, which
                                                  is indistinguishable from a blocked path. Cross-ref
                                                  to B030 is accurate (B030 is the client-side false
                                                  NotDetected when DNS is blocked; A024 is the server-
                                                  side signed false-no-leak). Fix 1 (carry liveness
                                                  proof in the attestation) is the right direction.
                                                  The practical challenge: liveness proof requires the
                                                  collector to actively confirm it received at least one
                                                  well-formed query from the token — this needs a
                                                  design decision about what constitutes "liveness" for
                                                  a collector that may legitimately see no queries if
                                                  there is no leak. Recommend the attestation carry a
                                                  `collector_pinged: bool` flag (at least one DNS query
                                                  was received for the token during the test window)
                                                  separately from `leaked`. Criticality Critical correct
                                                  (forgeable signed clean evidence — auto-Critical rule
                                                  3).


                       - **Tool Name**            [Codex]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-13
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       verify signs leaked = len(resolvers)>0 even when
                                                  observations are empty at
                                                  Server/syxx_server/leak.py:138-163; collector
                                                  bind/path failure is therefore signed as
                                                  leaked:false without liveness evidence.
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   Represent zero observation as
                                                  inconclusive/collector-unobserved and sign
                                                  liveness/observation-window evidence, never a
                                                  clean Boolean.

                       - **Tool Name**            [Claude]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-13

- **[A038]**            Exposure Check Converts DNS Failure Into Signed-Looking “Closed / Good”
- **Criticality:**      Critical; timeout, transport failure, or malformed response becomes a false-
                        secure open-resolver assessment on a production server route.
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/app.py:813-843
- **Issue:**            `_route_exposure` catches every `resolver.DNSError`, sets `recursive=False`,
                        then returns `assessment: "closed"` and “not an open resolver (good).” A
                        timeout or invalid response is no evidence that the caller's public IP is
                        closed. This violates no-verdict-before-evidence and collapses failure into
                        secure.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** A005/A028 (server timeout/work-budget family); tri-state protocol §1.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Return a typed inconclusive/unknown assessment on every query error.
                        [Fix 2] Reserve `closed` for affirmative negative evidence, if the protocol
                        can obtain it; ordinary silence is filtered/timeout and remains unknown.
- **Mandatory tests:** Happy: a controlled recursive responder → open-resolver. Failure: timeout,
                        refused ICMP/socket error, malformed DNS, wrong ID/source, and empty
                        non-authoritative response → inconclusive, never closed. Real run: exercise
                        production route against a controlled open responder and a filtered public
                        address and capture distinct open vs inconclusive results.

                                                  wrong-source, and empty-response failure cases to
                                                  remain inconclusive; a real controlled run must
                                                  distinguish an open responder from a filtered target.



                       - **Tool Name**            [Codex]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-13
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       _route_exposure catches DNSError and sets
                                                  recursive=False, then emits assessment 'closed'

                       - **Proposed Revisions**   Return an explicit inconclusive/error state on

                        Server/syxx_server/investigate.py:48-63

                        missing `Answer` defaults to `[]`, and missing AD defaults false. The caller
                        then labels the result `status: "ok"`. A resolver/error proxy returning `{}`
                        is therefore treated as a successful empty DNS answer rather than malformed/
                        inconclusive. Answer members are also assumed dictionaries without validating
                        required field types.

                        every answer object's name/type/data before accepting the response.

                        raise `DNSError` and remain inconclusive.

                        Failure: `{}`, null/wrong-type Status, non-array Answer, and non-object/missing-
                        field answers raise `DNSError` and cannot join consensus. Real run: controlled
                        DoH endpoint returns each shape through `/api/investigate`.

- **[B046]**            EDNS DO Bit Never Set — Signed Domains Read .unsigned → False
                        dnssecCanaryStripped
- **Criticality:**      Critical; a decisive false spoofing/interception verdict on real DNS (green
                        on fixtures that inject RRSIGs).
- **Location:**         macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/DNSResolver.swift:419-423;
                        macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/DNSSECVerifier.swift:78-79
- **Issue:**            The EDNS DO bit is never set (OPT TTL `00 00 00 00`), so real resolvers
                        return no RRSIG/NSEC → signed domains read `.unsigned` →
                        `dnssecCanaryStripped` fires at weight 3.0 (a decisive false
                        spoofing/interception verdict). Fixtures pass because they inject RRSIGs;
                        real DNS is wrong. Same systemic bug as the server path A030.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Systemic twin of A030 (server /api/investigate DO=0) — file both, cross-
                        referenced.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Set the DO bit on DNSSEC-bearing queries.
                        [Fix 2] Add a real-resolver integration assert that a known-signed zone
                        reads signed.
- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED (code) / INFERRED (live frequency) — systemic with A030

                       - **Tool Name**            [Claude]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-11
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       N/A
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   SOURCE VERIFIED. DNSResolver.swift:418-423 explicitly
                                                  documents "no DO bit" and sets the OPT TTL flags to
                                                  all zeros (`[0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00]`). The impact is
                                                  severe: `dnssecCanaryStripped` carries weight 3.0 and
                                                  will fire on EVERY signed domain queried from a real
                                                  resolver. This is the highest-weight evidence item
                                                  in the rubric and it will be false on all real runs.
                                                  Fix 1 is correct — set the DO bit by changing the
                                                  fourth byte of the OPT TTL field from `0x00` to
                                                  `0x80` (the DO flag occupies the high bit of the
                                                  Flags-MSB of the Extended-RCODE+Flags field in the
                                                  OPT RR per RFC 4035 §3.2.1). Platform parity: both
                                                  macOS and Windows need this fix; the EDNS OPT
                                                  construction should be verified on Windows
                                                  DNSResolver.cs as well. Fix 2 (real-resolver
                                                  integration test) is mandatory per AGENTS.md §2.
                       - **Tool Name**            [Syxx-Researcher]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-11
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Disagree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       `checkStatus` explicitly queries QTYPE=DNSKEY and
                                                  QTYPE=RRSIG (`DNSSECVerifier.swift:78-79`) and does
                                                  not pass `edns0UDPSize`, so the cited OPT builder at
                                                  `DNSResolver.swift:417-435` is not emitted in this
                                                  path. Source proves the generic builder cannot set
                                                  DO; it does not prove explicit RRSIG queries always
                                                  return unsigned. The prior byte edit is also wrong:
                                                  in `[ext-rcode, version, flags-MSB, flags-LSB]`, DO
                                                  0x8000 sets the third byte to 0x80, not the fourth.
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   Downgrade B046 to INFERRED pending the mandatory real
                                                  run, or archive if known-signed zones return explicit
                                                  RRSIG normally. CF-08 needs an explicit EDNS/DO
                                                  parameter, packet-byte fixtures on both platforms,
                                                  and real valid/bogus/unsigned verification.

                       - **Tool Name**            [Codex]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-13
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree with revisions
                       - **Disagree Basis**       macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/DNSResolver.swift:419-423;
                                                  macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/DNSSECVerifier.swift:78-79 —
                                                  Live-source inspection confirms the cited concern
                                                  only in narrowed/current form: The EDNS DO bit is
                                                  never set (OPT TTL `00 00 00 00`), so real
                                                  resolvers return no RRSIG/NSEC → signed domains
                                                  read `.unsigned` → `dnssecCanaryStripped` fires at
                                                  weight 3.0 (a decisive false spoofing/interception
                                                  verdict). Fixtures pass because they inject
                                                  RRSIGs; real DNS is wrong. Same systemic bug as
                                                  the server path A030.
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   Revalidate current query builder because EDNS/DO
                                                  code has changed; retain only a live packet-byte
                                                  proof, not historical lines.

                       - **Tool Name**            [Claude]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-13
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       Traced the full live chain: dnssecControl(control=
                                                  "cloudflare.com", DNSCanaries.swift:86) ->
                                                  checkStatus (DNSSECVerifier.swift:77-102) calls
                                                  queryUDPDetailed with DNSQuery default
                                                  edns0UDPSize=nil, so makeQueryPacketWithID emits
                                                  ZERO additional RRs (DNSResolver.swift:400) — no
                                                  OPT, hence no DO — on both the DNSKEY(48) and
                                                  RRSIG(46) queries. Without DO a validating resolver
                                                  strips RRSIG (RFC 4035 §3.2.1) -> rrsigRecords
                                                  empty -> .unsigned (DNSSECVerifier.swift:88-89) ->
                                                  dnssecCanaryStripped POSITIVE (DNSCanaries.swift:97-
                                                  104) at weight 3.0 toward interception/spoofing
                                                  (Conclusion.swift:229-230). A near-always-false
                                                  decisive verdict on a signed control. Rebut Codex
                                                  "code changed": lines 419-423 still carry no DO and
                                                  this path emits no OPT at all. Rebut earlier byte
                                                  edit: DO is the high bit of flags-MSB = the THIRD
                                                  TTL byte, so [0x00,0x00,0x80,0x00], not the fourth
                                                  (Syxx-Researcher was right, earlier Claude wrong).
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   Add an explicit DO flag to DNSQuery/
                                                  makeQueryPacketWithID (set edns0UDPSize e.g. 1232
                                                  AND the DO bit) OR query the covering type with DO
                                                  and read RRSIG from the answer. Mandatory
                                                  real-resolver assert that cloudflare.com reads
                                                  signed. Platform parity: Windows DNSResolver.cs OPT
                                                  builder needs the same. Fix jointly with A030.
                                                  Priority: highest — highest-weight false verdict in
                                                  this shard.

                        `probe` runs a cleartext Do53 control when DoH does not clearly succeed.
                        timeout/transportError → `.blocked` only if control succeeds, else

- **[A046]**            Stripe Product GET Sends Expansion Parameters in a Request Body
- **Criticality:**      Critical (payments); checkout can fail because a GET body is not a reliable
                        query-parameter transport.
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/stripe_checkout.py:29-42, 64-68
- **Issue:**            `_request` URL-encodes `params` into `data` for every method. The product GET
                        therefore sends `expand[]=default_price` in a body rather than the URL;
                        intermediaries or Stripe may ignore it, leaving `default_price` as an ID and
                        causing the server to reject a valid product.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Distinct from A035 checkout abuse.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Put GET parameters in the query string; reserve bodies for POST.
- **Code Sample:**      [

                        data = urllib.parse.urlencode(params, doseq=True).encode()
                        req = urllib.request.Request(_API + path, data=data, method=method)

                        ]

                       - **Date**                 2026-07-13
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree

                                                  data for all methods and product retrieval calls
                                                  GET with expand params at
                                                  Server/syxx_server/stripe_checkout.py:29-42,64.
                                                  HTTP/Stripe intermediaries can ignore a GET body.
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   Append GET parameters to the URL and send no body.
                                                  Official Stripe docs describe GET as idempotent
                                                  and parameters in the query.

                       - **Tool Name**            [Claude]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-13
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       Confirmed at stripe_checkout.py:32-33 — params are
                                                  urlencoded into `data` for every method, then
                                                  Request(url, data=data, method=method) sends them
                                                  as a body. create_checkout_session (line 64) calls
                                                  _request(..., "GET", {"expand[]":"default_price"}),
                                                  so the expand travels in a GET body. If an
                                                  intermediary or Stripe ignores it, default_price
                                                  stays an ID (not a dict), and line 66-67 raises
                                                  "no default price", rejecting a valid product.
                                                  Payments-critical, not a DNS verdict.
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   Agree. Priority high (revenue). For GET, append
                                                  params to the query string and send no body;
                                                  reserve bodies for POST.

                                                  instead of requiring exactly `ANCOUNT` records. If

- **[D040]**            Licensing A021 signature check fails open when KEYGEN_PUBLIC_KEY unset
- **Criticality:**      Critical; forgeable Pro entitlement by default on an unset key.
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/licensing.py:129-130; Server/syxx_server/config.py:130.
- **Issue:**            [CONFIRMED] _verify_validate_key_response() returns True (skip verification)
                         whenever config.KEYGEN_PUBLIC_KEY is empty (licensing.py:129-130), and
                         config.py:130 defaults it to "" ("Leave empty to skip signature
                         verification"). The A021 control - Ed25519 verification of Keygen's
                         validate-key response before trusting meta.valid - is therefore FAIL-OPEN in
                         any deployment that does not explicitly set SYXX_KEYGEN_PUBLIC_KEY. A MITM,
                         compromised TLS trust store, or Keygen-path hijack can then return a forged
                         body with meta.valid: true and be granted Pro entitlement. The comment frames
                         this as "dev/test compat," but it is the production default, so the security
                         control is inert unless an operator opts in.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Clarifies WS1-03 / A021 (which added the verify path) - the verify path
                         exists but is bypassed by default.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Fail CLOSED: when KEYGEN_PUBLIC_KEY is unset in a production profile,
                         deny entitlement (or require an explicit SYXX_KEYGEN_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED=1
                         opt-out that logs a loud warning), rather than return True.
                         [Fix 2] Make the production config set a pinned Keygen public key, and treat
                         missing/invalid signature as denial (None), never "pro."

- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED

- **[A052]**            Server `kv` Table Has No TTL/Purge — Unbounded Disk Growth
- **Criticality:**      Medium (operational — unbounded disk growth; distinct from A013 which is about idempotency race conditions, not cleanup).
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/db.py:18-24 (schema), db.py:421-456 (purge_expired), fulfillment.py:82-121 (kv_set callers)
- **Issue:**            [CONFIRMED] The `kv` table (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS kv (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL)`) has no TTL or expiry mechanism. The `purge_expired()` function (db.py:421-456) cleans `leak_observations`, `leak_tokens`, `audit`, `passive_dns`, `trial_anchors`, and `warp_cache` — but NOT `kv`. Every `stripe_evt:<event_id>` key written by fulfillment.py:88,103,121 is永久 stored. Every `stripe_cust:<customer_id>` key (fulfillment.py:98) is永久 stored. High-volume payment processing creates thousands of orphaned keys that are never cleaned, causing unbounded SQLite database growth. The only other kv consumers (`session_secret` at db.py:198, `beta_digest_last_sent` at app.py:986/992/1004) are singleton keys and do not contribute to growth.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Distinct from A013 (Stripe webhook TOCTOU race). A013 is about the idempotency check being check-then-act; A052 is about the kv entries never being cleaned up after processing is complete.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Add a `kv` purge to `purge_expired()`: delete `stripe_evt:*` keys older than N days (configurable, e.g. 90) and `stripe_cust:*` keys for suspended/expired licenses. Keep `session_secret` and `beta_digest_last_sent` as permanent singleton keys.
                          [Fix 2] Alternatively, add an `expires_at` column to the `kv` schema and set TTLs at write time; the purge job already handles TTL-based expiry for other tables.
- **Code Sample:**      [
                         # Server/syxx_server/purge_expired() — the purge covers every table EXCEPT kv
                         conn.execute("DELETE FROM leak_observations WHERE token IN ...", (now,))
                         conn.execute("DELETE FROM leak_tokens WHERE expires_at < ?", (now,))
                         conn.execute("DELETE FROM audit WHERE ts < ?", ...)
                         conn.execute("DELETE FROM passive_dns WHERE last_seen < ?", ...)
                         conn.execute("DELETE FROM trial_anchors WHERE first_launch < ?", ...)
                         conn.execute("DELETE FROM warp_cache WHERE created_at < ?", ...)
                         # ^^^ no kv cleanup — stripe_evt:*and stripe_cust:* grow forever
                         ]

                         # Server/syxx_server/fulfillment.py:88 — every webhook event writes a permanent kv entry
                         db.kv_set("stripe_evt:" + event_id, "processing")
                         ]



                       - **Tool Name**            [Codex]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-13
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       The kv schema has no timestamp at
                                                  Server/syxx_server/db.py:21-24 and purge_expired
                                                  omits kv at :421-456, while per-event and customer
                                                  keys are continuously written in
                                                  fulfillment.py:81-121.
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   Use purpose-specific tables with
                                                  timestamps/foreign keys and retention; preserve
                                                  singleton secrets separately.

                       - **Tool Name**            [Claude]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-13
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree
                       - **Disagree Basis**       Verified: kv schema (db.py:21-24) has no
                                                  timestamp; purge_expired (db.py:421-456) covers
                                                  six tables but never kv; fulfillment.py:88,103,121
                                                  write stripe_evt:* and :98 writes stripe_cust:*

- **[A054]**            Server Rate Limiter Indefinite Lockout and Fractional Token Truncation on Blocked Requests
- **Criticality:**      Non-critical (High); a client sending requests rapidly can be permanently locked out because their last-request timestamp is reset on blocked requests, preventing token accumulation.
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/ratelimit.py:28-44
- **Issue:**            [CONFIRMED] `allow()` resets the bucket's `last` timestamp to `now` even when returning `False` (line 41). Under fast-polling or low-refill-rate configs, `elapsed * refill_ms // 1000` truncates to 0, resetting the token generation timer. This causes a permanent lockout for clients sending requests faster than the refill rate.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** SD-12 covers `_prune` not being called (partially fixed under A001), but does not cover this rate-limiter logic lockout defect.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Do not update the bucket's `last` timestamp to `now` when returning `False`. This allows `elapsed` time to continue accumulating from the last successful token consumption.
- **Code Sample:**      [

                        // Server/syxx_server/ratelimit.py:37-44
                        tokens_ms, last = _buckets.get(key, (capacity * 1000, now))
                        elapsed = now - last
                        tokens_ms = min(capacity * 1000, tokens_ms + elapsed * refill_ms // 1000)
                        if tokens_ms < 1000:
                            _buckets[key] = (tokens_ms, now) # <-- Resets 'last' to 'now' even on block!
                            return False
                        _buckets[key] = (tokens_ms - 1000, now)
                        return True

                        ]
- **Tag:**              CONFIRMED

                       - **Tool Name**            [Codex]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-13
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree with revisions
                       - **Disagree Basis**       Blocked requests store (tokens_ms, now) at
                                                  Server/syxx_server/ratelimit.py:37-43, losing
                                                  fractional elapsed time and enabling rapid polling
                                                  to prevent refill. The proposed 'do not update
                                                  last' fix would double-count elapsed already added
                                                  to tokens_ms on repeated checks.
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   Carry fractional remainder or compute tokens from
                                                  a monotonic last-refill anchor exactly once; add
                                                  rapid-block polling tests. Do not use the filed
                                                  simplistic fix.

                       - **Tool Name**            [Claude]
                       - **Date**                 2026-07-13
                       - **Agree / Disagree**     Agree with revisions
                       - **Disagree Basis**       Verified ratelimit.py:37-43 stores (tokens_ms,
                                                  now) on a blocked request; small elapsed makes
                                                  elapsed*refill//1000 truncate to 0, so a client
                                                  polling faster than the refill threshold never
                                                  accrues — effective lockout. Codex is right: the
                                                  filed "don't update last" fix double-counts, since
                                                  the (truncated) refill is already folded into the
                                                  stored tokens_ms.
                       - **Proposed Revisions**   Agree w/ revisions: recompute tokens from a single
                                                  monotonic last-refill anchor (don't pre-add into
                                                  stored tokens) or carry the fractional remainder;
                                                  add rapid-block polling tests. Reject the filed
                                                  simplistic fix. Priority Low.
