- **[A147]**           `do_HEAD` Delegates to `do_GET`, So a HEAD Request Executes Every
                        Side Effect and Every Expensive Probe — Including Creating a Real Stripe
                        Checkout Session
- **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Restricted HEAD to static files and assets only; all other routes return 405 Method Not Allowed.
- **Criticality:**      Medium (unbilled side effects and full-cost work from a request whose
                        response body is discarded; free amplification for crawlers and scanners)
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/app.py:632-633 (`do_HEAD`), :525-526 (`_send` skips only
                        the body), :904-933 (`_route_checkout`), :1603-1670 (`/api/benchmark`),
                        :1689-1773 (`/api/propagation`)
- **Issue:**            `do_HEAD` is `return self.do_GET()`. `_send` suppresses only the final
                        `wfile.write` (`if self.command != "HEAD"`, app.py:525-526); every line of
                        the route above it has already run.
                        The clearest case is `/api/checkout` (app.py:904-933): a HEAD request calls
                        `stripe_checkout.create_checkout_session(sku)` (:926), creating a real
                        Stripe Checkout Session, incrementing `logging_util.incr("checkouts")`
                        (:932), and returning a 303 whose `Location` the caller never sees. HEAD is
                        defined as safe; this route is not. Any crawler, link-preview bot, or
                        uptime monitor that HEADs `https://syxx.app/api/checkout?sku=…` manufactures
                        Stripe sessions and corrupts the `checkouts` metric that the conversion
                        story depends on.
                        The cost side is worse in aggregate: HEAD `/api/benchmark?rounds=10`
                        performs the full ~50 seconds of DNS work (S1-05); HEAD `/api/propagation`
                        spawns the full 12-thread fan-out (S1-06); HEAD `/api/exposure` sends a real
                        outbound probe. All are free-tier. An attacker gains nothing over GET, but a
                        *benign* crawler now costs the same as an attack, and HEAD is what crawlers
                        send by default.
                        `_route_activate` and the other mutating routes are POST-only and therefore
                        unaffected — the exposure is confined to GET routes with side effects, of
                        which `/api/checkout` is the significant one.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** No delta. `grep -n "do_HEAD" DELTAS.md DELTAS-fixed.md DELTAS-rejected.md
                        Server/SERVER_DELTAS.md` → no matches. NEW.
- **Fix(es):**          [1] Restrict HEAD to the routes for which it is meaningful — the static /
                        asset handlers — and return `405 Method Not Allowed` with `Allow: GET,
                        POST, OPTIONS` for everything else. A cheap allowlist check at the top of
                        `do_HEAD` is enough.
                        [2] At minimum, refuse HEAD on `/api/checkout` explicitly: it is the only
                        GET route in the file that creates external, billable state.
                        [3] Do not increment success counters (`logging_util.incr("checkouts")`,
                        :932) on a request whose response was never delivered — that is a fabricated
                        measurement in the metrics snapshot.
                        [4] Make `/api/checkout` a POST (with the GET kept only for the shipped
                        app builds that cannot be recalled, as :909-913 already documents for the
                        legacy `?product=` parameter).
- **Code Sample:**

```python
# app.py:632-633
    def do_HEAD(self):
        self.do_GET()

# app.py:525-526 — only the body is suppressed; the route already ran
        self.end_headers()
        if self.command != "HEAD":
            self.wfile.write(body)

# app.py:925-933 — a real Stripe session, created by a HEAD request
        try:
            url, _sid = stripe_checkout.create_checkout_session(sku)
        except stripe_checkout.StripeError as e:
            ...
        logging_util.incr("checkouts")
        self._send(303, b"", "text/plain", {"Location": url})
```

- **[A148]**           Unauthenticated, Un-Rate-Limited Routes Perform Database Work and 1 MiB HMAC
                        Computations — `/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/api/stats`, and Both Webhooks
- **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Added rate limiting to /readyz and /api/stats; wrapped keygen webhook compare_digest in try/except TypeError.
- **Criticality:**      Medium (free unauthenticated DB and CPU load; the rate limiter is applied
                        per-route and these five routes were missed)
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/app.py:723-730 (`/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/api/stats`),
                        :1046-1064 (`_route_readyz`), :935-952 (`_route_stripe_webhook`),
                        :954-994 (`_route_keygen_webhook`)
- **Issue:**            Rate limiting in this file is opt-in per route (`self._rate_ok(...)` as the
                        first statement — e.g. :800, :829, :857, :871, :895, :914, :1086). Five
                        public routes omit it.
                        `/api/stats` (app.py:729-730) calls `passivedns.total_records()` →
                        `db.passive_count()` → an unindexed `COUNT(*)` over the passive-DNS table,
                        which grows for 30 days (config.py:298). One line, no auth, no limit, no
                        cost to the caller.
                        `/readyz` (app.py:1046-1064) opens and closes a SQLite connection
                        (`db.connect().close()`, :1052) on every request. Under a flood this
                        contends with the write path (leak observations, passive-DNS inserts) —
                        i.e. hammering the *readiness* endpoint is a way to make the service less
                        ready, and `/readyz` is what the operator and any orchestrator poll.
                        `/healthz` (:723-724) is a constant and is fine on cost; it is listed only
                        because it shares the gap.
                        Both webhooks read up to 1 MiB (`_body`, app.py:591) and then compute an
                        HMAC over the whole buffer *before* any authentication — `verify_webhook`
                        at :943 and `hmac.new(...).hexdigest()` at :968-971. Signature verification
                        must precede trust, which it correctly does; but it means an unauthenticated
                        caller can compel a 1 MiB read plus a SHA-256 pass per request, unlimited.
                        `/api/webhooks/keygen` has a second flaw: `hmac.compare_digest(expected,
                        sig_header)` at :972 raises `TypeError` when `sig_header` contains non-ASCII
                        (compare_digest requires both `str` operands to be ASCII-only). A header of
                        `Keygen-Signature: é` produces a 500 rather than a 400 — an unauthenticated
                        caller choosing the server's error class.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** No delta. `grep -n "healthz\|readyz\|api/stats" Server/SERVER_DELTAS.md`
                        returns only **SD-48** (:115), which concerns `_route_readyz` leaking
                        `str(e)` — FIXED at app.py:1053-1057. The missing rate limit is
                        unrecorded. NEW.
- **Fix(es):**          [1] Apply the limiter at the dispatcher rather than per route, with an
                        explicit exemption list, so "forgot to call `_rate_ok`" stops being a
                        reachable state. That also closes the unrouted-404 gap in S1-08.
                        [2] Give `/api/stats` a cached value (recompute at most once a minute) —
                        `passiveRecords` does not need to be exact per request.
                        [3] Give `/readyz` a short-TTL cached result (2-5s) so polling cannot
                        multiply DB connections.
                        [4] Rate-limit the webhook routes by source IP before reading the body, and
                        lower their body cap well below 1 MiB (a Stripe/Keygen event is a few KiB).
                        [5] Wrap the `compare_digest` at :972 in try/except `TypeError` → 400, or
                        pre-validate `sig_header` as `[0-9a-f]{64}` before comparing.
- **Code Sample:**

```python
# app.py:723-730 — three public routes, no _rate_ok
        if path == "/healthz":
            return self._send(200, {"ok": True})
        if path == "/readyz":
            return self._route_readyz()
        if path == "/metrics":
            return self._route_metrics()
        if path == "/api/stats":
            return self._send(200, {"passiveRecords": passivedns.total_records()})

# app.py:939-943 — 1 MiB read + HMAC, unauthenticated, unlimited
        raw = self._body()
        if self._body_error(raw):
            return
        try:
            event = stripe_checkout.verify_webhook(raw or b"", self.headers.get("Stripe-Signature", ""))

# app.py:972 — TypeError on a non-ASCII signature header
        if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, sig_header):
```

- **[A149]**           `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` Omits DELETE Though Two DELETE Routes Ship,
                        and `Vary: Origin` Is Sent Only on the Allowed Branch
- **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Added DELETE to Access-Control-Allow-Methods; Vary: Origin was already moved outside the if block.
- **Criticality:**      Medium (the documented DELETE API is unreachable from any browser;
                        preflight and cache correctness are both wrong)
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/app.py:468-477 (`_cors`), :625-630 (`do_OPTIONS`),
                        :688-703 (`do_DELETE`), :1863-1877 (`DELETE /api/keys/<id>`),
                        :1943-1953 (`DELETE /api/monitors/<id>`)
- **Issue:**            (a) `_cors` advertises `Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST, OPTIONS`
                        (app.py:475). `do_DELETE` (:688-703) routes two real endpoints —
                        `DELETE /api/keys/<id>` and `DELETE /api/monitors/<id>` — and both are
                        published in `Server/docs/openapi.yaml`. A browser preflight for DELETE
                        receives an `Allow-Methods` list that does not contain DELETE and blocks the
                        request. The dashboard cannot revoke an API key or delete a monitor
                        cross-origin. This is a shipped API that cannot be called from the shipped
                        website.
                        (b) `Vary: Origin` (app.py:474) is inside the allowlist branch only. A
                        response to a non-allowlisted (or absent) Origin differs — it has no
                        `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` — yet carries no `Vary`, so a shared cache may
                        key it on URL alone and reuse it for an allowlisted origin (and vice-versa).
                        Combined with S1-10 (no `Vary: Accept-Encoding`) and the
                        `Cache-Control: public` routes at :1043/:1021/:849, the cache key is wrong
                        along two axes at once.
                        (c) `do_OPTIONS` (:625-630) answers `204` for **every** path, routed or not,
                        with no rate limit and no `Access-Control-Max-Age` — so every cross-origin
                        request pays a preflight round trip, and OPTIONS is a free unlimited
                        endpoint (feeding S1-08's counter growth via `handle_one_request`).
                        (d) `do_OPTIONS` does not reflect the actual methods for the requested path,
                        so the response is a static claim rather than a measured one.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** **SD-42** (`Server/SERVER_DELTAS.md:99`) — CORS wildcard — is FIXED at
                        app.py:468-474 (origin echo + allowlist). The method-list and `Vary`-branch
                        defects were introduced/left by that fix and have no delta. NEW.
- **Fix(es):**          [1] Add `DELETE` to `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` (app.py:475). Better:
                        derive the list from the routes that actually exist for the requested path.
                        [2] Move `self.send_header("Vary", "Origin")` outside the `if` in `_cors`
                        so it is sent whenever an `Origin` header was present, allowlisted or not —
                        and merge with `Accept-Encoding` per S1-10 fix [1].
                        [3] Add `Access-Control-Max-Age: 600` to `do_OPTIONS` to stop preflighting
                        every request.
                        [4] Return 404 from `do_OPTIONS` for unrouted paths, and apply the
                        dispatcher-level rate limit from S1-18 fix [1].
- **Code Sample:**

```python
# app.py:468-477
    def _cors(self):
        origin = self.headers.get("Origin", "")
        if origin and origin in config.CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS:
            self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", origin)
            self.send_header("Vary", "Origin")        # <-- allowed branch only
        self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Methods", "GET, POST, OPTIONS")   # <-- no DELETE
        self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Headers",
                         "Authorization, Content-Type, X-Syxx-License")

# app.py:696-699 — the DELETE routes that exist
            if path.startswith("/api/keys/"):
                return self._route_revoke_api_key(path)
            if path.startswith("/api/monitors/"):
                return self._route_delete_monitor(path)
```

- **[A150]**           Host-Header Routing Discards the Path Entirely and Matches `leaktest.` by
                        Prefix — Any Host Beginning `leaktest.` Serves the Leak-Test Page
- **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** MOTD hosts now serve What's-New only at root paths; leaktest uses exact match against config.LEAKTEST_HOST.
- **Criticality:**      Low (content confusion and a dead operational surface on four hostnames; no
                        privilege crossed)
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/app.py:706-718 (`_dispatch_get` Host block);
                        config.py:66-70 (MOTD hosts)
- **Issue:**            The first four checks in `_dispatch_get` compare the `Host` header and
                        return immediately, **without consulting `path` at all** (app.py:709-715).
                        On `macmotd.syxx.app`, `winmotd.syxx.app` and `debmotd.syxx.app` every URL
                        — `/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/metrics`, `/api/investigate`, `/assets/logo.svg`,
                        `/robots.txt` — returns the What's-New HTML with 200. The operational
                        endpoints are unreachable on those names even though nginx proxies them to
                        the same backend (deploy.sh:396 lists all four in one `server_name`), and a
                        health check pointed at the wrong hostname reports a healthy 200 for a
                        server that could be failing.
                        The `leaktest.` check at :717 uses `host.startswith("leaktest.")`, a prefix
                        match on an attacker-controlled header, not equality against a configured
                        host (contrast :710-715, which compare against `config.MOTD_*_HOST`). Any
                        `Host: leaktest.attacker.tld` — including a hostname the attacker controls
                        and points at this IP — serves the leak-test page. There is no
                        `config.LEAKTEST_HOST` constant; the string is inline.
                        Because the Host header is unvalidated, `_serve_whats_new` is also reachable
                        on the marketing origin by anyone who can set the header directly against
                        `0.0.0.0:8080` (config.py:261).
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** No delta. The Host-routing design is documented at app.py:707-708 and
                        config.py:63-70 and in deploy.sh:384-393 (which records the 2026-07-16
                        outage caused by a MISSING `server_name`), but the path-discarding and
                        prefix-match behaviours are unrecorded. NEW.
- **Fix(es):**          [1] Gate the Host override on the path as well: only `path in ("/",
                        "/index.html", "")` should serve MOTD content — matching what the
                        `leaktest.` branch at :717 already does correctly. Everything else on those
                        hosts should fall through to normal routing.
                        [2] Replace `startswith("leaktest.")` with equality against a new
                        `config.LEAKTEST_HOST` (default `leaktest.syxx.app`), consistent with
                        `MOTD_MAC_HOST` et al.
                        [3] Validate the `Host` header against a configured allowlist at the top of
                        the dispatcher and 421 (Misdirected Request) otherwise.
- **Code Sample:**

```python
# app.py:706-718
    def _dispatch_get(self, path, query):
        host = (self.headers.get("Host", "").split(":")[0]).strip().lower()
        if host == config.MOTD_MAC_HOST:
            return self._serve_whats_new("mac")      # <-- path ignored entirely
        if host == config.MOTD_WIN_HOST:
            return self._serve_whats_new("win")
        if host == config.MOTD_DEB_HOST:
            return self._serve_whats_new("deb")
        if host and host.startswith("leaktest.") and path in ("/", "/index.html", ""):
            return self._serve_static("/leaktest")   # <-- prefix match on an attacker header
```

- **[A151]**           `extra_headers` Duplicates Headers Already Emitted by `_security_headers` —
                        Two `Content-Security-Policy` and Two `X-Content-Type-Options` on
                        `/api/whats-new`
- **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Made extra_headers REPLACE rather than append by stripping overridden headers from the buffer before emitting.
- **Criticality:**      Low (works today because CSP duplicates are intersected, but the mechanism
                        silently ignores any attempt to RELAX a security header per-route)
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/app.py:502-524 (`_send` header ordering),
                        :479-500 (`_security_headers`), :847-851 (`_serve_whats_new` extras)
- **Issue:**            `_send` emits `_cors()` then `_security_headers()` and only then the
                        caller's `extra_headers` (app.py:519-523), appending rather than replacing.
                        `_serve_whats_new` passes `Content-Security-Policy` and
                        `X-Content-Type-Options` (app.py:848, :850), both of which
                        `_security_headers` has already sent (:485, :480). The response carries two
                        of each.
                        For CSP the browser enforces the **intersection** of all policies, so the
                        result is `default-src 'none'` AND the site policy — stricter than either,
                        which is the intended direction here and why nothing has broken. But the
                        mechanism is a trap: the next route that passes an `extra_headers` CSP
                        meaning to *permit* something will find its policy silently intersected
                        away, with no error and no log. The route author's intent and the wire
                        behaviour diverge, and there is no way to tell from the call site.
                        `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, nosniff` is harmless but noisy.
                        Same class, different header: `_send` also lets `extra_headers` set
                        `Cache-Control` (:1022, :1043, :849) where `_security_headers` sets none, so
                        the inconsistency is invisible in the common case.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** No delta. The strict What's-New CSP is documented in DELTAS.md:14518,
                        :14540 and :21294 (A112 lineage) as the intended policy; the duplication
                        against `_security_headers` is not recorded. NEW.
- **Fix(es):**          [1] Make `extra_headers` REPLACE rather than append: collect all headers
                        into a dict inside `_send`, let `extra_headers` overwrite by name, then emit
                        once. This is a five-line change and removes the whole class.
                        [2] Drop the now-redundant `X-Content-Type-Options` from
                        `_serve_whats_new` (app.py:850).
                        [3] Keep the What's-New CSP explicit after [1] — it is the correct policy
                        for that content and should be visible at the call site, just not duplicated
                        on the wire.
- **Code Sample:**

```python
# app.py:519-524 — appends; never replaces
        self._cors()
        self._security_headers()
        if extra_headers:
            for k, v in extra_headers.items():
                self.send_header(k, v)
        self.end_headers()

# app.py:847-851 — both headers already sent by _security_headers
        self._send(200, html, "text/html; charset=utf-8", {
            "Content-Security-Policy": "default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'",
            "Cache-Control": "public, max-age=300",
            "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff",
        })
```

- **[A152]**           `/api/trace` Calls `resolve_authoritative` Unwrapped — a Resolution Failure
                        Becomes `500 internal error` Instead of an Honest 502
- **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Wrapped resolve_authoritative in try/except; returns 200 with result "unreachable" and brokenAt on DNSError; uses .get for delegation.
- **Criticality:**      Low (an inconclusive result is reported as a server fault; inconsistent with
                        both sibling routes)
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/app.py:1380-1397 (`_route_trace`), specifically
                        :1393-1394; contrast :1289-1292 (`_route_authoritative`) and :1326-1329
                        (`_route_diff`)
- **Issue:**            `_route_authoritative` wraps the call and returns `502 "resolution
                        failed: …"` (app.py:1289-1292). `_route_diff` wraps it and degrades to
                        `{"verdict": "unreachable"}` (:1326-1329, the SD-41 fix). `_route_trace`
                        does neither: `result = resolver.resolve_authoritative(domain,
                        qtypes[qtype_str])` at :1393 is bare, so a `resolver.DNSError` propagates to
                        `do_GET`'s catch-all (:647-649) and the caller receives `500 internal
                        error`.
                        That is dishonest in the specific sense this codebase cares about: the
                        server did not fail, the *resolution* did — which for a DNS-tampering tool
                        is itself a finding worth surfacing (a trace that cannot complete is a
                        signal, not an error). A 500 tells the user "our bug"; the truth is "the
                        delegation chain did not answer". The route's own docstring (:1381-1382)
                        says its purpose is to show "where resolution breaks" — the one case it
                        exists to report is the case it swallows.
                        Line :1394 compounds it: `result["delegation"]` is indexed directly with no
                        `.get`, so any partial result lacking that key raises `KeyError` → also 500.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** **SD-41** (`Server/SERVER_DELTAS.md:97`) — "[M] Correct · `app.py:633` —
                        `/api/diff` calls `resolve_authoritative` without the try/except every
                        sibling route uses, so a `DNSError` becomes a generic 500. **Fix:** wrap it
                        and return `502 'resolution failed'` like the others." SD-41 was applied to
                        `/api/diff` only (app.py:1326-1329); `/api/trace` has the identical defect
                        and was not covered. Same delta, unfixed instance.
- **Fix(es):**          [1] Apply SD-41's fix to `_route_trace`: wrap :1393 in
                        `try/except resolver.DNSError` and return `502 "resolution failed: %s"`,
                        matching `_route_authoritative` at :1291-1292.
                        [2] Better for this route specifically: return `200` with
                        `verdict: "unreachable"` and `brokenAt` naming the zone that failed — a
                        trace that stops partway is the diagnostic, not an error. That is what the
                        docstring promises.
                        [3] Use `result.get("delegation", [])` at :1394.
                        [4] Grep for every other unwrapped `resolve_authoritative` call site when
                        fixing, so SD-41 closes for the whole file rather than one route at a time.
- **Code Sample:**

```python
# app.py:1289-1292 — the sibling does it correctly
        try:
            result = resolver.resolve_authoritative(domain, qtypes[qtype_str])
        except resolver.DNSError as e:
            return self._json_error(502, "resolution failed: %s" % e)

# app.py:1393-1394 — unwrapped, and an unguarded key access
        result = resolver.resolve_authoritative(domain, qtypes[qtype_str])
        broken = next((d.get("zone") for d in result["delegation"] if d.get("error")), None)
```

- **[A153]**           Unguarded `int()` on Caller-Supplied JSON Fields Returns 500, and Neither
                        `ttlDays` Nor `maxPermutations` Has a Lower Bound
- **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Added try/except and max(1, ...) bounds for ttlDays and maxPermutations; returns 400 on invalid input.
- **Criticality:**      Low (400-class input yields a 500; a zero/negative TTL mints an
                        already-expired API key and reports it as created)
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/app.py:1848 (`ttlDays`), :1927 (`maxPermutations`);
                        response claim at :1851-1852
- **Issue:**            `ttl = min(int(payload.get("ttlDays", 90)), 365)` (app.py:1848) and
                        `max_perm = min(int(payload.get("maxPermutations", 200)), 500)` (:1927) both
                        call `int()` on an arbitrary JSON value with no try/except and no floor.
                        `{"ttlDays": "abc"}` → `ValueError`; `{"ttlDays": {}}` → `TypeError`;
                        `{"ttlDays": 1e400}` → `OverflowError`. All three escape to `do_POST`'s
                        catch-all (:684-686) and return `500 internal error` for what is plainly a
                        `400 invalid field`.
                        The missing floor is the substantive half. `{"ttlDays": 0}` or `-1` passes
                        `min(…, 365)` untouched, `db.api_key_create(..., ttl_days=0)` mints a key
                        that is expired at creation, and the response at :1851-1852 nonetheless
                        returns `201` with `{"key": …, "expiresInDays": 0, "warning": "store this
                        key now; it will not be shown again"}`. The server tells the caller it
                        created a usable credential it did not create — a claim ahead of the
                        evidence, and the daily creation quota at :1836 (5/day) is consumed for it.
                        `maxPermutations: -1` reaches `lookalike.scan(domain,
                        max_permutations=-1)`, which will produce an empty scan reported as a
                        completed one.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** **SD-88** (`Server/SERVER_DELTAS.md:228`) — "[M] Sec · `app.py:1702` — API
                        key TTL accepts zero and negative values (`ttlDays:0` creates a key that
                        expires immediately). **Fix:** `ttl = max(1, min(int(...), 365))`."
                        **SD-89** (:230) — "[M] Correct · `app.py:1702,1739` — Unhandled `ValueError`
                        on non-numeric integer fields returns 500 instead of 400." **Both OPEN**;
                        still present at the current app.py:1848 and :1927 (line numbers moved from
                        1702/1739). Adding here: SD-88 does not note that the 201 response
                        *asserts* a successful creation, which is the honesty half.
- **Fix(es):**          [1] Apply SD-88: `ttl = max(1, min(int(...), 365))`; likewise
                        `max_perm = max(1, min(int(...), 500))`.
                        [2] Apply SD-89: wrap both in `try/except (ValueError, TypeError,
                        OverflowError)` → `400 "ttlDays must be an integer"`.
                        [3] Introduce one `_int_field(payload, name, default, lo, hi)` helper and
                        route both call sites (and any future one) through it — two independent
                        fixes of the same bug is how SD-88/89 came to be two deltas.
                        [4] Do not consume the 5/day creation quota (:1836) on a request that fails
                        validation: move the quota check after field validation.
- **Code Sample:**

```python
# app.py:1848-1852
        ttl = min(int(payload.get("ttlDays", 90)), 365)          # no floor, no guard
        key = db.api_key_create(ent.subject, label=label, ttl_days=ttl)
        logging_util.incr("api_keys_created")
        self._send(201, {"key": key, "label": label, "expiresInDays": ttl,
                         "warning": "store this key now; it will not be shown again"})

# app.py:1927
        max_perm = min(int(payload.get("maxPermutations", 200)), 500)
```

- **[A154]**           `_i()` / `_env_int()` Silently Substitute the Default for Any Malformed
                        Numeric Configuration Value
- **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Added logging when malformed int config values are coerced to defaults in config.py, app.py, and investigate.py.
- **Criticality:**      Low (a mistyped limit reverts to the default with no signal; same doctrine
                        failure as S1-01, lower blast radius because the defaults are safe)
- **Location:**         Server/syxx_server/config.py:18-22 (`_i`), used at :49, :262-266, :277-279,
                        :292, :297-301, :316, :321-325, :327, :364-366, :378-379, :394, :401, :405,
                        :418, :442-443, :446-447; Server/syxx_server/app.py:135-139 (`_env_int`),
                        used at :145, :151, :154
- **Issue:**            `_i` returns the default whenever `int()` raises. There is no third state
                        and no diagnostic, so `SYXX_LEAK_TOKEN_TTL=15m` silently becomes 900,
                        `SYXX_SESSION_TTL=1h` silently becomes 3600, `SYXX_RATE_CAPACITY=thirty`
                        silently becomes 30, and `SYXX_HTTP_MAX_WORKERS=64` (with a trailing
                        comment) silently becomes 64. In each case the operator believes they
                        changed a limit and did not. Nothing is logged; `/readyz` does not report
                        effective configuration; `/metrics` is unreadable (S1-02).
                        This is the same shape as S1-01 and rated lower only because the fallbacks
                        are the shipped defaults rather than a permissive value — a mistyped
                        `_i` cannot *open* anything, it can only fail to close it further. The one
                        place it bites harder is `SYXX_KEYGEN_TIMEOUT` (:277) and
                        `SYXX_DOH_UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT` (:378): an operator lengthening a timeout to
                        cope with a slow upstream gets the short default and sees the failures
                        continue with no explanation.
                        There is also no range validation anywhere: `SYXX_RATE_CAPACITY=-5` parses
                        fine and yields a bucket that denies every request (ratelimit.py:51,
                        `tokens_ms < 1000` always true) — fail-closed, but as a silent global
                        outage rather than a startup error. `SYXX_HTTP_MAX_WORKERS=100000` parses
                        fine and defeats the S1-06/SD-51 bound.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** No delta on `_i` coercion. The failure mode is described in prose in
                        config.py:205-210 ("an env var nothing references is silently dead, which
                        is precisely what happened to SYXX_KEYGEN_POLICY_{MAC,WIN}_TRIAL on the
                        2026-07 production host") — the same lesson, one layer over. See also
                        S1-15, where a *referenced* variable is dead for a different reason. NEW.
- **Fix(es):**          [1] Log the coercion: `logging_util.warn("config_invalid_int", name=name,
                        value=v, using=default)` before returning the default. A silent fallback is
                        the defect; the fallback itself is defensible.
                        [2] For values with a meaningful domain, accept a `lo`/`hi` and refuse (or
                        clamp with a warning) outside it — `RATE_CAPACITY`, `HTTP_MAX_WORKERS`,
                        `SESSION_TTL`, `LEAK_TOKEN_TTL` all have obvious floors.
                        [3] Emit the full effective configuration at startup (secrets redacted) so
                        an operator can diff intent against reality — this is the single change
                        that would have surfaced S1-01, S1-15 and S1-24 together.
                        [4] Consider failing startup on an unparseable value for anything
                        security-relevant, consistent with S1-01 fix [1].
- **Code Sample:**

```python
# config.py:18-22
def _i(name, default):
    try:
        return int(os.environ.get(name, "").strip())
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return default            # silent; operator is never told their value was discarded

# app.py:135-139 — same shape, duplicated
def _env_int(name, default):
    try:
        return int(os.environ.get(name, "").strip())
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return default
```

- **[A155]**               Investigate RCODE Mapping Compares Integers to Strings — Every Vantage Crashes, No Vantage Can Ever Be `ok`
- **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code), already resolved.** RCODE comparisons now use integers (0, 3) with resolver.rcode_name() for labels; broad exception handler added.
- **Criticality:**      Critical; `/api/investigate` (paid) and every scheduled `investigate`
                        monitor raise `AttributeError` on the first vantage that answers. The
                        A044/A045 remediation in the tree is non-functional: even with the crash
                        removed, `status == "ok"` is unreachable, so `_consensus_one` can never
                        return `consistent` — and the `rcodes` join at :119 would then raise
                        `TypeError` on the all-failure path too.
- **Location:**         investigate.py:82-93, 117-119, 125-126
- **Issue:**            `resolver` returns `rcode` as an **integer** in all three transports —
                        `_parse_response` (`resolver.py:162,200`) returns `flags & 0x000F`,
                        `_parse_doh_json` (`resolver.py:461,477`) returns the numeric `Status`,
                        and `query_system` (`resolver.py:421`) hardcodes `0`. `_resolve_all`
                        compares that integer against the **strings** `"NOERROR"`, `"SERVFAIL"`,
                        `"REFUSED"`, `"NXDOMAIN"`. All four comparisons are permanently False, so
                        control always falls into the `else` branch and evaluates `rcode.lower()`
                        on an `int`. Only `resolver.DNSError` is caught (:97), so the
                        `AttributeError` escapes `_resolve_all` → `investigate()` →
                        `app.py:1269` (no try/except) → HTTP 500. The same type confusion
                        poisons :117 (`if d.get("rcode")` drops NOERROR because `0` is falsy)
                        and :119 (`", ".join(sorted(rcodes))` over ints → `TypeError`), and
                        :125-126 (`d.get("rcode") == "NXDOMAIN"` never matches, so A044's
                        selective-censorship detector is dead code).
                        Not covered by tests: `tests/test_routes.py:414-416` only asserts the
                        402 paywall, so the suite is green over a route that cannot succeed.
                        **[reproduced]** with three stubbed vantages returning `{"rcode": 0, ...}`:
                        `EXC AttributeError 'int' object has no attribute 'lower'`.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** DELTAS.md:11518 **A044** (consensus drops reachable empty vantages) and
                        DELTAS.md:11571 **A045** (SERVFAIL/REFUSED marked `ok`) — both still open;
                        this is the *broken fix* for both. Neither appears in DELTAS-fixed.md.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Compare numerically (`rcode == 0` / `in (2, 5)` / `== 3`) and keep a
                        single `_RCODE_NAMES` map for the user-visible label, or normalize to a name
                        once inside `resolver` and change all consumers (`firewall_test.py:69-75`,
                        `lookalike.py:123`, `subdomain_enum.py:186`, `app.py:1446,1568`) together.
                        [Fix 2] Broaden the `except` in `_resolve_all` to record an honest
                        `status:"error"` for *any* exception, so a bug in the mapping degrades to
                        inconclusive instead of a 500 that hides the outcome (honesty spine #2).
                        [Fix 3] Add a route test that stubs the resolver and asserts a real
                        `consistent`/`divergent` body — the current 402-only test cannot catch this.
- **Code Sample:**      [
                        investigate.py:82-90
                            rcode = res["rcode"]                      # int, e.g. 0
                            if rcode == "NOERROR":                    # never True
                                status = "ok"
                            elif rcode in ("SERVFAIL", "REFUSED"):    # never True
                                status = "rcode_%s" % rcode.lower()
                            elif rcode == "NXDOMAIN":                 # never True
                                status = "nxdomain"
                            else:
                                status = "rcode_%s" % rcode.lower()   # AttributeError on int
                        ]

- **[A156]**               DNSSEC Denial-of-Existence Path Raises `UnboundLocalError` — `/api/dnssec` 502s and the NSEC Code Is Unreachable
- **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code), already resolved.** The `signed` variable is now computed before the answer-RRSIG block that uses it.
- **Criticality:**      Critical; `signed` is read at :363 but only bound at :381. Any domain whose
                        answer query returns no `qtype` records or no RRSIG — which includes every
                        NODATA/NXDOMAIN answer and every case where the zone walk broke early and
                        `pv_s` is still a root/parent server returning a referral — hits an
                        `UnboundLocalError`, caught by `app.py:1966` and returned as
                        `502 "DNSSEC validation failed"`. SD-73's remediation therefore never runs.
- **Location:**         dnssec_validator.py:361-378 (read at :363), assignment at :381
- **Issue:**            `validate_chain` assigns `signed` only at :381, after the answer-RRSIG
                        block. The `else:` branch at :361 ("No answer records — check for
                        authenticated denial of existence") tests `if signed:` at :363 — a load of
                        a local that is not yet bound. Python resolves `signed` as function-local
                        because of the :381 store, so this is a hard `UnboundLocalError`, not a
                        fallback to a global. AST check: loads at lines 387,387,**363**,384,385;
                        store at line 381 only.
                        Reachability is not exotic: `pv_s` is initialised to the root server IP at
                        :300 and stays truthy after any `break` in the zone loop, so the block at
                        :346 runs even when the chain aborted at, e.g., `"no DS in parent"` (:313).
                        **[reproduced]** with stubbed `_find`/`_sq`:
                        `EXC: UnboundLocalError cannot access local variable 'signed'`.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Server/SERVER_DELTAS.md:198 **SD-73** (accepts denial of existence without
                        verifying NSEC/NSEC3) — the code added to close SD-73 is unreachable.
                        Not otherwise tracked.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Compute `signed` from the chain *before* the answer block
                        (`signed = any(s["step"] == "ds-match" and s["status"] == "valid" for s in ch)`
                        immediately after the zone loop) and reuse it at both :363 and :381.
                        [Fix 2] Add a unit test that drives `validate_chain` through the
                        no-answer-records branch with stubbed `_find`/`_sq`; the current suite has
                        no coverage of this branch at all.
- **Code Sample:**      [
                        dnssec_validator.py:361-364
                            else:
                                # No answer records — check for authenticated denial of existence
                                if signed:                      # UnboundLocalError
                                    denial = verify_denial_of_existence(domain, qtype, ar["ans"])
                        dnssec_validator.py:381
                            signed = any(s["step"] == "ds-match" and s["status"] == "valid" for s in ch)
                        ]

- **[A157]**               `verify_denial_of_existence` Would Report an *Unsigned* NSEC as "Authenticated Denial of Existence"
- **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** _verify_nsec_denial now returns inconclusive until proper RRSIG verification is implemented; caller passes ar["auth"] instead of ar["ans"].
- **Criticality:**      High; the function performs **no signature verification whatsoever**, yet
                        its return value is rendered as `status:"valid"` /
                        `"authenticated denial of existence (NSEC/NSEC3)"` (:366-367) and feeds the
                        `all(s["status"] == "valid")` gate at :384 that produces the overall
                        `valid` verdict. A verdict from unauthenticated evidence — honesty spine
                        #1. Presently masked by the `UnboundLocalError` above; fixing that finding
                        alone would activate this one.
- **Location:**         dnssec_validator.py:415-452, 475-499; caller at :361-375
- **Issue:**            Four independent defects in the same proof:
                        1. **No RRSIG check.** `_verify_nsec_denial` never verifies that the NSEC
                           RRset is signed by the zone's validated DNSKEY. Any on-path attacker or
                           rogue authoritative can inject a bare NSEC RR and obtain "valid".
                        2. **Wrong section.** The caller passes `ar["ans"]` (:364) — the ANSWER
                           section. NSEC/NSEC3 denial records live in the AUTHORITY section
                           (`ar["auth"]`), which is parsed at :74 and never consulted.
                        3. **str vs bytes.** `rr["ow"]` is a decoded dotted `str` from `_read_name`
                           (:51); `target` at :426 is `bytes` (`...encode("idna") + b"\x00"`).
                           `rr["ow"] == target` is always False, and the ordering test at :449
                           raises. **[reproduced]**:
                           `TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'bytes'`
                           — an uncaught exception on the denial path, i.e. another 502.
                        4. **Wrong ordering.** Even with matching types, `<` is Python string
                           ordering, not RFC 4034 §6.1 canonical DNS name order (label-reversed,
                           length-then-octet), so covering-range proofs are unsound in both
                           directions. `_read_name(rd, 0)` at :434 also cannot follow a compression
                           pointer, since it is handed the isolated rdata slice rather than the
                           full message (`rr["pk"]`/`rr["ro"]` are available and unused).
                        `_verify_nsec3_denial` (:455-472) is honest — it returns `inconclusive`
                        unconditionally and says so.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Server/SERVER_DELTAS.md:198 **SD-73**. Related: SERVER_DELTAS.md:286
                        (SD-65 rejection note listing SD-73 as still valid).
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Require the NSEC/NSEC3 RRset to pass `_vsig` against the zone's
                        DS-validated DNSKEY before any `"valid"` is returned; without that, return
                        `inconclusive`.
                        [Fix 2] Pass `ar["auth"]` (authority section), and pass `rr["pk"]/rr["ro"]`
                        to `_read_name` so the next-owner name can be decompressed.
                        [Fix 3] Compare canonical wire names on both sides (`_nw(rr["ow"])` vs
                        `_nw(name)`) using RFC 4034 §6.1 label-reversed ordering, not `str.__lt__`.
                        [Fix 4] Until closest-encloser + next-hashed NSEC3 proof exists, keep
                        NSEC3 at `inconclusive` (already correct) and never let NSEC alone upgrade
                        a chain to `valid`.
- **Code Sample:**      [
                        dnssec_validator.py:426, 442-451
                            target = name.rstrip(".").lower().encode("idna") + b"\x00"   # bytes
                            ...
                            if rr["ow"] == target:          # str == bytes -> always False
                                if qtype in bitmap_types:
                                    return "valid"          # no RRSIG was ever checked
                                return "inconclusive"
                            else:
                                if rr["ow"] < target < next_owner:   # TypeError (str < bytes)
                                    return "valid"
                        ]

- **[A158]**               **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Answer-path RRSIG now verified at the DS-validated apex with signer-name check; answer-time DNSKEY RRset re-verified against DS-validated key before use.
                        Answer-Path RRSIG Verified Against a DNSKEY RRset That Is Never DS-Matched, RRSIG-Checked, or Signer-Name Bound
- **Criticality:**      High; the chain-of-trust link between the DS-validated key and the key that
                        actually verifies the answer is missing. `_chk_ans` re-queries DNSKEY, uses
                        **whatever keys come back**, and calls `_vsig` **without** `zone=`, so the
                        SD-94 signer-name check applies only on the DNSKEY path. A hostile or
                        on-path authoritative can serve a second, unsigned DNSKEY RRset containing
                        its own key and have the forged answer RRSIG accepted → `verdict: "valid"`.
- **Location:**         dnssec_validator.py:246-256 (`_chk_ans`), 352-354 (call site),
                        174-190 (`_vsig` `zone` parameter), 335 (DNSKEY path, correct)
- **Issue:**            In the zone loop the code does the right thing: it DS-matches a key
                        (`mkp`, :321-330) and verifies the DNSKEY RRSIG with `zone=zone` (:335).
                        The answer path throws all of that away:
                        `tdk = _sq(tz, TYPE_DNSKEY, pv_s, timeout)` (:352) is a **fresh, unverified
                        query**; `tks` is every DNSKEY in the reply (:353); `_chk_ans` accepts a
                        signature from **any** of them (:252-255); and `_vsig(sigs, arecs, dp, dr, now)`
                        (:253) omits `zone=`, so `sg["sg"]` (the RRSIG signer field) is never
                        compared to the zone apex. Neither `mk`/`mkp` from the DS match nor the
                        RRSIG over the second DNSKEY RRset is consulted. The only remaining binding
                        is the 16-bit key tag (`sg["kt"] != dkt`, :181), which is not a security
                        property.
                        Secondary: `tz = zones[-1]` (:345) is the full queried name, not the zone
                        apex, so for any non-apex name (`www.example.com`) the DNSKEY query returns
                        NODATA, `tks` is empty, and `_chk_ans` returns `None` → permanent
                        `inconclusive` on the answer step for subdomains.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Server/SERVER_DELTAS.md:242 **SD-94** (RRSIG signer name not verified) —
                        fixed on the DNSKEY path only; the answer path is untouched.
                        SERVER_DELTAS.md:286 lists SD-94 among the still-valid DNSSEC deltas.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Verify answer RRSIGs with the DS-validated key material carried out
                        of the zone loop (`mk`/`mkp`), or re-verify the answer-time DNSKEY RRset
                        against the DS digest and its own RRSIG before use.
                        [Fix 2] Pass `zone=<apex>` on the answer call so SD-94's signer check
                        applies: `_vsig(sigs, arecs, dp, dr, now, zone=apex)`.
                        [Fix 3] Derive the apex from the deepest zone that produced a valid
                        `ds-match` step, not from `zones[-1]`.
- **Code Sample:**      [
                        dnssec_validator.py:249-255
                            keys = [(r,_pdk(r["rd"])) for r in dkrs if _pdk(r["rd"]) and_pdk[r["rd"]](1) == 3]
                            if not keys: return None
                            unsup = False
                            for dr, dp in keys:
                                r = _vsig(sigs, arecs, dp, dr, now)      # no zone= -> SD-94 not applied
                        dnssec_validator.py:352-353
                            tdk = _sq(tz, TYPE_DNSKEY, pv_s, timeout)    # unverified re-query
                            tks = [r for r in tdk["ans"] if r["rt"] == TYPE_DNSKEY] if tdk else []
                        ]

- **[A159]**               **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Added `nodata` as first-class status (NOERROR+no A = filtering signal); `"open"` now requires `inconclusive_count <= tested * 0.2`.
                        Firewall Test Reports `"open"` (Not Filtering) From Measurements That Were All Inconclusive
- **Criticality:**      High; the assessment branch at :187 requires only `filtered_count == 0`,
                        never consulting `inconclusive_count`. The two most common real-world
                        blocking modes — empty-NOERROR (Pi-hole/AdGuard NODATA mode) and silent
                        drop (timeout) — both land in `"error"`, so the endpoint returns
                        `assessment: "open"` on precisely the filtered network it exists to detect.
                        Missing data rendered as clean data (honesty spine #2).
- **Location:**         firewall_test.py:76-80, 157-164, 180-190
- **Issue:**            `_query_resolver` collapses two distinct outcomes into `"error"`:
                        (a) NOERROR with no A records (`if not addrs: return "error", []`, :78-79)
                        and (b) any exception, including a timeout (:65-67). `_is_filtered` returns
                        False for `"error"` (no branch matches, :106), so `filtered_count` stays 0.
                        The tally then routes `"error"` to `inconclusive_count` (:161-162), and
                        `clean_domains_ok` only tracks the three `expected == "resolve"` controls
                        (:167-168) — which a filtering resolver answers normally. Result:
                        7 inconclusive + 3 clean → `"open"`.
                        The `clean_reference_count == 0` guard at :183-186 (correctly added for the
                        all-vantages-blocked case) does not help here, because the *clean* vantages
                        answered fine; it is the *user* resolver's measurements that are missing.
                        **[reproduced]** with a stub where the user resolver returns
                        `{"rcode": 0, "records": []}` for the 7 blocked-category domains:
                        `assessment: open  summary: {'tested': 10, 'filtered': 0, 'clean': 3, 'inconclusive': 7}`.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Server/SERVER_DELTAS.md:248 **SD-97** (`_query_resolver` flattens all
                        exceptions to "error") — related but narrower; SD-97 is about error
                        taxonomy, this is about the verdict computed from it. No delta covers the
                        `"open"`-from-inconclusive branch.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Add `nodata` as a first-class status (NOERROR + no A records) and
                        treat it as a filtering signal in `_is_filtered` when the clean vantage
                        resolved — empty-NOERROR *is* a block when the reference has answers.
                        [Fix 2] Require an evidence floor for `"open"`:
                        `elif clean_domains_ok and filtered_count == 0 and inconclusive_count <= tested * 0.2`,
                        else `"inconclusive"`, and surface `inconclusive` in the response so the UI
                        cannot render "open" over mostly-unmeasured domains.
                        [Fix 3] Separate `timeout` from `error` (SD-97) so a systematically
                        dropping resolver is visibly distinct from a transport fault.
- **Code Sample:**      [
                        firewall_test.py:76-80
                            addrs = [r["value"] for r in resp.get("records", []) ...]
                            if not addrs:
                                return "error", []        # empty NOERROR == a block, not an error
                        firewall_test.py:187-190
                            elif clean_domains_ok and filtered_count == 0:
                                assessment = "open"       # inconclusive_count never consulted
                            else:
                                assessment = "inconclusive"
                        ]

- **[A160]**               **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Enforced RFC 1035 limits in `_read_name` (255-octet name, 128 labels, monotonic pointers); capped parsed records per section at 256.
                        Name-Decompression Amplification in the Server DNS Parser — 64 KB Hostile Response → 2.2 s CPU / 67 MB RAM
- **Criticality:**      High; measured 1000× memory amplification and multi-second CPU per response
                        on a handler thread, reachable from any hostile authoritative in the
                        delegation walk (`/api/trace` is not even wrapped in a try/except) and from
                        any upstream in the DoH forwarder. Server twin of the macOS delta D020.
- **Location:**         resolver.py:117-149 (`_read_name`), 534-559 (`_read_records`),
                        562-591 (`_parse_sections`), 302-315 / 610-622 / 368-379 (TCP fallbacks)
- **Issue:**            `_read_name` bounds pointer *loops* (`seen > 128`, :136-137) but not the
                        total work: each of the up-to-128 hops may traverse an arbitrarily long
                        label run, and the decoded labels accumulate in `labels` without a
                        253-octet name cap. `_read_records` then calls `_read_name` once per RR,
                        with the record count taken from the attacker-controlled header (`an`/`ns`/`ar`,
                        up to 65535 each), and stores every expanded owner string in `recs`.
                        Nothing caps the record count, the expanded name length, or the total bytes
                        materialised. The TCP fallbacks trust the peer's 2-byte length prefix with
                        no ceiling — note `dnssec_validator._q` **does** cap it
                        (`if ln > 16384`, dnssec_validator.py:95-96, SD-72) but the three copies in
                        `resolver.py` (:311-312, :617-618, :376) do not.
                        Reached by setting the TC bit in a UDP reply, which forces the TCP retry.
                        **[reproduced]** — a wire-legal 65 217-byte response (question name = a
                        16 KB label run, `an=4100`, every RR owner a 2-byte pointer to offset 12):
                        `parse=2.22s peak=66.6MB answers=4100 owner_len=15999`
                        (control: 28 017 B / an=1000 → `parse=0.55s peak=16.3MB`).
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** DELTAS.md:9646 **D020** — *Name-Decompression O(n^2) on a Hostile TCP
                        Response*, filed against `macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/DNSResolver.swift:737-772`
                        and tagged LIKELY/Agree. The Python server twin is not tracked (platform
                        parity, honesty spine #6). Server/SERVER_DELTAS.md:196 **SD-72** fixed the
                        TCP-length ceiling in `dnssec_validator.py` only.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Enforce RFC 1035 limits in `_read_name`: total decoded name ≤ 255
                        octets and ≤ 128 labels; raise `DNSError` beyond that.
                        [Fix 2] Require every compression pointer to target a strictly *lower*
                        offset than the pointer itself (the standard monotonic rule) — this makes
                        pointer chains linear and removes the loop counter's dependence on 128.
                        [Fix 3] Cap parsed records per section (e.g. 256) and per message, and cap
                        the peer-declared TCP length in all three `resolver.py` sites the way
                        SD-72 did in `dnssec_validator.py:95`.
- **Code Sample:**      [
                        resolver.py:133-149
                            offset = pointer
                            jumped = True
                            seen += 1
                            if seen > 128:                      # loop bound only; no work bound
                                raise DNSError("compression loop")
                            ...
                            labels.append(data[offset:offset + length].decode("utf-8", "ignore"))
                        resolver.py:311-312 (no ceiling, cf. dnssec_validator.py:95)
                            (length,) = struct.unpack(">H", length_bytes)
                            data = _recv_exact(sock, length)
                        ]

- **[A161]**               **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Every RDAP hop (including first) now uses `_PinnedHTTPSConnection` with `_resolve_public`; replaced `is_global` with `netutil.ip_is_public`; non-HTTPS base URLs refused.
                        RDAP Redirect Guard Is Check-Then-Connect — DNS-Rebinding SSRF, and the First Hop Is Never Checked
- **Criticality:**      High; `_redirect_target_is_safe` resolves the hostname, approves it, and
                        then **throws the vetted IP away** — the next loop iteration builds
                        `HTTPSConnection(parsed.hostname)`, which re-runs `getaddrinfo` inside
                        `connect()`. A DNS record with a 0-second TTL answers public on the check
                        and `169.254.169.254` on the connect. `fetcher.py` and `resolver.py` both
                        solved exactly this with `_PinnedHTTPSConnection`; `whois_lookup.py` does not
                        import it.
- **Location:**         whois_lookup.py:93-128 (`_redirect_target_is_safe`),
                        139-172 (`_rdap_query`; re-resolve at :141-146, hand-off at :164)
- **Issue:**            Three gaps in one path:
                        1. **TOCTOU/rebinding.** :162 validates `location`; :164 stores the *URL*;
                           :141-146 re-parses and re-resolves it on the next pass. No pinning.
                           Contrast `fetcher.py:63-67` and `resolver.py:441-445`, whose comments
                           (A067/A088/A090/A100) describe this exact hazard.
                        2. **First hop unvalidated.** The initial `url` (:138) is built from the
                           IANA bootstrap and dialled at :144 with **no** IP check at all. A
                           poisoned/stale bootstrap entry (fetched over HTTPS but cached for 24 h,
                           :24-51, and silently reused on any failure at :44/:51) dials whatever it
                           names.
                        3. **Divergent gate.** :112/:124 use `ipaddress.is_global` instead of the
                           canonical `netutil.ip_is_public`. `is_global` does not exclude the NAT64
                           well-known prefix `64:ff9b::/96`, which `netutil.py:14,36-37` was
                           specifically written to block; CGNAT/IPv4-mapped coverage also depends on
                           interpreter version rather than on the project's own gate.
                        Also unmitigated: SD-80 (`parsed.scheme != "https"` still falls through to a
                        cleartext `HTTPConnection` at :145-146) is only defended for *redirects*
                        (:158), not for the bootstrap-supplied base URL.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Server/SERVER_DELTAS.md:184 **SD-67** (redirect target not validated) —
                        partially fixed: the check exists but is not connect-bound.
                        Server/SERVER_DELTAS.md:212 **SD-80** (cleartext HTTPConnection) — open.
                        Compare the closed A067/A088/A090/A100 pattern in `fetcher.py:46-67`.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Route every RDAP hop (including the first) through
                        `fetcher._resolve_public` + `fetcher._PinnedHTTPSConnection`, so the socket
                        dials the numeric IP that was validated and SNI/cert still use the hostname.
                        [Fix 2] Replace `addr.is_global` with `netutil.ip_is_public` so one gate
                        governs all outbound paths.
                        [Fix 3] Refuse any non-`https` RDAP base URL outright (SD-80).
- **Code Sample:**      [

- **[A162]**               **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Threaded monotonic deadline through `_q`/`_sq`/`_find` (clamping per-socket timeout); added aggregate deadline to `firewall_test.test()`.
                        Aggregate Deadlines Not Threaded Into the Queries Beneath Them (`dnssec_validator`, `resolve_authoritative`, `firewall_test`)
- **Criticality:**      High; the declared budgets are advisory checkpoints between phases, not
                        bounds on the work inside them. Free-tier `/api/dnssec` and `/api/firewall-test`
                        and rate-limited `/api/trace` can each pin a handler thread far beyond the
                        stated cap.
- **Location:**         dnssec_validator.py:274, 281-282, 303-304 (deadline) vs 192-229 (`_find`),
                        101-103 (`_sq`), 79-99 (`_q`); resolver.py:688-776 (`resolve_authoritative`,
                        no budget at all; recursion at :762); firewall_test.py:109-118, 141-157
- **Issue:**            `dnssec_validator`: `deadline = now + min(timeout*4, 30.0)` (:274) is checked
                        only at :281 and at the top of each zone iteration (:303). Inside an
                        iteration, `_find` (:305) may try `_MAXD=16` levels × `_MAXS=4` servers ×
                        `timeout=5 s` = 320 s, plus per-level `resolve_authoritative(nn, 1, to, 4)`
                        sub-walks (:222) — and `_find` is called once per zone, plus four more `_sq`
                        calls per zone. Neither `_find`, `_sq`, nor `_q` accepts a deadline; only the
                        per-socket `timeout` is passed down. The 30 s cap can be exceeded by more
                        than an order of magnitude.
                        `resolve_authoritative` has **no** aggregate budget: 16 depths × 4 servers ×
                        `timeout`, and at each depth up to two recursive NS-resolution sub-walks
                        (:757-769) that themselves fan out (depth ≤ 3, 4 servers per level).
                        `firewall_test.test` runs 10 domains × up to 3 sequential queries × 5 s =
                        150 s with no deadline parameter at all.
                        This is the same defect class the codebase already fixed once for
                        `investigate` (A096, `investigate.py:29-35`) — the pattern was not carried
                        to the other three entry points.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Server/SERVER_DELTAS.md:194 **SD-71** (no aggregate time budget in
                        dnssec_validator) — partially fixed: the deadline exists but "pass remaining
                        time to each query", the explicit second half of the SD-71 fix, was not done.
                        Server/SERVER_DELTAS.md:208 **SD-78** (firewall_test 30 sequential queries) —
                        open. DELTAS.md:18546 **A096** is the already-fixed sibling for `investigate`.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Thread a monotonic `deadline` through `_find`/`_sq`/`_q` and derive
                        each socket timeout as `min(timeout, deadline - now)`; abort with an
                        `inconclusive` step when the remainder is ≤ 0.
                        [Fix 2] Give `resolve_authoritative` a `deadline` parameter (default from
                        config), check it at every depth and before every sub-walk, and record
                        `error: "deadline exceeded"` in the delegation chain so the honest
                        `inconclusive` verdict carries its reason.
                        [Fix 3] Give `firewall_test.test` a deadline and mark unqueried domains
                        `inconclusive` rather than letting them fall through to the `"open"` branch
                        (compounds the firewall finding above).
- **Code Sample:**      [
                        dnssec_validator.py:274, 303-305
                            deadline = now + min(timeout * 4, 30.0)  # SD-71: aggregate wall-clock cap
                            ...
                            if time.time() > deadline: ... break     # only between zones
                            zv,_ = _find(zone.rstrip("."), timeout) # up to 320s inside, unbounded
                        ]

- **[A163]**               **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Changed `except socket.timeout` to `except OSError` in all three UDP socket paths (`query`, `_query_sections`, `forward_wire`).
                        Non-Timeout Socket Errors Escape `resolver.query` / `_query_sections` as `OSError` — 500 Instead of Inconclusive
- **Criticality:**      Medium-High; only `socket.timeout` is converted to `DNSError`. A connected
                        UDP socket raises `ConnectionRefusedError` on an ICMP port-unreachable and
                        `OSError(ENETUNREACH/EHOSTUNREACH)` on connect — routine conditions for a
                        walker that dials arbitrary authoritative servers. Callers that catch only
                        `resolver.DNSError` therefore surface an HTTP 500, hiding a result that
                        should be an honest `inconclusive`.
- **Location:**         resolver.py:282-299 (`query`), 594-608 / 610-622 (`_query_sections` and its
                        TCP fallback), 302-315 (`_query_tcp`), 343-390 (`forward_wire`);
                        consumers: resolve_authoritative:698-702, investigate.py:97,
                        app.py:1290-1292 (`/api/authoritative`), app.py:1391 (`/api/trace`, no
                        try/except at all)
- **Issue:**            `except socket.timeout: raise DNSError("timeout")` (:292-293, :605-606)
                        is the only translation. Everything else — `connect`, `send`, `recv`,
                        `sendall`, and `_recv_exact`'s `sock.recv` — propagates the raw `OSError`.
                        In `resolve_authoritative` the per-server retry loop catches only `DNSError`
                        (:701), so **one** refusing server aborts the entire walk instead of moving
                        to the next root/NS. `/api/trace` (app.py:1391) calls
                        `resolve_authoritative` with no exception handling whatsoever.
                        **[reproduced]**: `R.query("example.com", TYPE_A, "127.0.0.1", timeout=2)`
                        → `UNCAUGHT ConnectionRefusedError escapes resolver.query: [Errno 61]`.
                        This is the same class as the already-fixed A078/A098 (`struct.error` on a
                        truncated question section, resolver.py:168-172, 576-579) — that fix
                        addressed the parse path but not the socket path.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** A078/A098 (cited in resolver.py:168-172 and :576-579) are the parse-path
                        siblings. DELTAS.md:16561 references A045 for investigate failure handling.
                        The socket-path leak is not tracked.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Wrap every socket op in `except OSError as e: raise DNSError(str(e))`
                        (a `socket.timeout` *is* an `OSError`, so one handler covers both).
                        [Fix 2] Broaden the walker's per-server retry to `except (DNSError, OSError)`
                        so one dead server does not end the walk.
                        [Fix 3] Wrap `/api/trace`'s `resolve_authoritative` call the way
                        `/api/diff` already does (app.py:1325-1328, A038) so the route returns an
                        `inconclusive` verdict rather than a 500.
- **Code Sample:**      [
                        resolver.py:288-295
                            try:
                                sock.connect((server, 53))
                                sock.send(packet)
                                data = sock.recv(4096)
                            except socket.timeout:            # ConnectionRefusedError escapes
                                raise DNSError("timeout")
                            finally:
                                sock.close()
                        ]

- **[A164]**               **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Added aggregate deadline in `fetch()`, chunked body reads with deadline checking, per-hop timeout clamped to remaining budget.
                        Outbound Fetch Has No Byte-Rate or Aggregate Deadline — Slow-Drip Thread Pinning (5 MB × 5 s per recv)
- **Criticality:**      Medium-High; `config.FETCH_MAX_BYTES = 5 MiB` and `FETCH_TIMEOUT = 5 s`, and
                        `settimeout` is per-recv, not per-request. A target that emits one byte
                        every 4 s holds a handler thread for months. `warp.build_baseline` then
                        repeats this for up to `FETCH_MAX_SCRIPTS = 40` scripts sequentially, and
                        `fetch()` allows `FETCH_MAX_REDIRECTS + 1` full requests per call.
- **Location:**         fetcher.py:137-153 (`resp.read(max_bytes + 1)` at :148), 156-174 (`fetch`);
                        warp.py:112-118; resolver.py:318-325 (`_recv_exact`, same shape)
- **Issue:**            No deadline is computed anywhere in `fetcher.py`; `timeout` is handed to the
                        connection constructor and thereafter governs each individual socket
                        operation only. `resp.read(n)` blocks until `n` bytes or EOF, resetting the
                        clock on every chunk. The redirect loop (:166-173) re-enters `_one_request`
                        with the same full `timeout` for each hop rather than a shrinking remainder.
                        `resolver._recv_exact` (:318-325) has the identical shape — bounded only by
                        the 16-bit length field, i.e. 65535 × `timeout`.
                        This is the outbound twin of A102, whose vetting notes explicitly reframed
                        the defect as "no aggregate per-request deadline for slow-drip".
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** DELTAS-fixed.md:2026 **SRV-017** (`fetcher.py:~101` — `read()` called
                        without explicit speed bounds; "Vetting: Agree") is listed as vetted, but
                        the current code contains no rate or deadline guard.
                        DELTAS-fixed.md:12814 **A102** (server *inbound* slow-loris) is the
                        already-analysed sibling — same residual, opposite direction.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Compute `deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout` in `fetch()`, pass
                        the remaining budget to each hop, and read the body in bounded chunks that
                        check the deadline between reads.
                        [Fix 2] Enforce a minimum throughput (abort if `bytes_read / elapsed` falls
                        below a floor), which is what actually defeats a drip.
                        [Fix 3] Apply the same chunked-with-deadline loop to
                        `resolver._recv_exact`.
- **Code Sample:**      [
                        fetcher.py:144-150
                            resp = conn.getresponse()
                            ...
                            body = resp.read(max_bytes + 1)   # up to 5 MiB, timeout resets per chunk
                            if len(body) > max_bytes:
                                raise TruncatedError("baseline truncated; diff is inconclusive")
                        ]

- **[A165]**               **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Body now read before `conn.close()` inside the `try` block, with explicit 10 MiB byte cap.
                        `_query_crtsh` Reads the Response Body After Closing the Connection — Subdomain Enumeration Always Returns Zero
- **Criticality:**      Medium; on any HTTP/1.1 keep-alive server (crt.sh is one) `conn.close()`
                        closes the `HTTPResponse` too, so the subsequent `resp.read()` returns
                        `b""`, `json.loads` raises, and every call raises `_CrtshError`. The route
                        then returns `total: 0, subdomains: [], truncated: true` with HTTP 200 —
                        "no subdomains found" is indistinguishable from "the CT log was never read".
- **Location:**         subdomain_enum.py:85-111 (close at :95-96, body read at :106),
                        51-55 (error swallowed into `truncated`), 78-82 (response shape)
- **Issue:**            The `try/finally` at :90-96 closes the connection immediately after
                        `getresponse()`, before the body is read at :106.
                        `HTTPConnection.close()` closes `self.__response`, which nulls the
                        response's `fp`; `HTTPResponse.read()` then returns `b""`.
                        **[reproduced]** against a local `protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"` server:
                        `status 200 will_close False` / `body after close: b''` /
                        `JSON FAIL -> JSONDecodeError`. (The same test against an HTTP/1.0 server
                        succeeds, because `will_close` makes `getresponse()` detach the response —
                        which is why this can look fine in a naive local test.)
                        Compounding it, `enumerate` maps the failure onto `truncated = True` (:53-54)
                        and emits no `error` field, so the caller cannot distinguish an unreachable
                        CT log from a domain with no certificates. Missing data presented as an
                        empty measured result.
- **Cross-ref. Delta:** Server/SERVER_DELTAS.md:294 **SD-109** (subdomain_enum thread pinning) is
                        the only tracked issue for this file and its fix (deadline + pool) is in
                        the tree. The read-after-close defect is not tracked.
- **Fix(es):**          [Fix 1] Read the body inside the `try`, before `close()`:
                        `body = resp.read(<cap>)` then close in `finally`.
                        [Fix 2] Cap the read explicitly — crt.sh replies for a busy domain are
                        multi-megabyte and are currently read unbounded (`resp.read()`, :106).
                        [Fix 3] Return an explicit `{"source": "crt.sh", "error": ...,
                        "subdomains": null}` shape when the log could not be read, so zero results
                        cannot be rendered as a completed enumeration.
- **Code Sample:**      [
                        subdomain_enum.py:90-106
                            try:
                                conn.request("GET", path, headers={...})
                                resp = conn.getresponse()
                            except Exception as exc:
                                raise_CrtshError("connection failed: %s" % exc)
                            finally:
                                conn.close()          # closes resp too
                            ...
                            entries = json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))   # b"" on HTTP/1.1
                        ]
