**[D111]** **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** SetServers validates every server address with IPAddress.TryParse before PowerShell interpolation, preventing command injection.
**Criticality:** MEDIUM
**Location:** `Windows/dotNET/Syxx.Kit/UnboundManager.cs:53-58` (and `34`, `43-44`)
**Issue:** The PowerShell command line is assembled by string interpolation and then re-wrapped in
an outer `-Command "…"` quote. A server address containing `"` terminates the outer quote and the
remainder executes as PowerShell — with whatever token the process holds, and this code path is
explicitly intended to run elevated. The values come from `Restore(prior)`, where `prior` is the
result of splitting *earlier* PowerShell stdout (line 46), so the trust boundary is "whatever the
previous command printed", and `SetServers` is public on `ISystemResolverSwitching` so any caller
can supply arbitrary strings.
**Cross-ref. Delta:** none — new.
**Fix(es):** validate every element with `IPAddress.TryParse` before interpolation and refuse the
whole operation on any element that fails. Prefer `ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList` with
`-EncodedCommand` (base64 UTF-16LE) so no quoting is involved, or call the
`Set-DnsClientServerAddress` WMI/CIM equivalent (`MSFT_DNSClientServerAddress`) directly instead of
shelling out.
**Code Sample:**

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx.Kit/UnboundManager.cs:53-56
string cmd = servers.Count == 0
    ? $"Set-DnsClientServerAddress -InterfaceIndex {idx} -ResetServerAddresses"
    : $"Set-DnsClientServerAddress -InterfaceIndex {idx} -ServerAddresses {string.Join(",", servers)}";
var (outp, code) = Run("powershell", $"-NoProfile -Command \"{cmd}\"");
```

**[D112]** **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** SigningIdentifier returns SignatureTrust verdict via X509Chain.Build; subject reported only with trust state.
**Criticality:** MEDIUM
**Location:** `Windows/dotNET/Syxx.Kit/DNSCapture.cs:676-690`
**Issue:** `SigningIdentifier` calls `X509Certificate.CreateFromSignedFile` and returns
`cert.Subject` as the record's `"signing ID"` (serialised at DNSCapture.cs:22-23 and shown in the
forensic report). That API **extracts** the embedded certificate; it performs no Authenticode
verification — no `WinVerifyTrust`, no chain build, no revocation check, no hash comparison against
the file. A binary with a stripped, expired, revoked or outright forged signature block still
yields a confident-looking `CN=Microsoft Windows, O=Microsoft Corporation, …` in the evidence
report. A tampered binary is the exact scenario a forensic capture exists to expose.

Secondary: `CreateFromSignedFile` is `[SupportedOSPlatform("windows")]`; on Linux it throws and the
`catch` at 686-689 returns `null`, which the doc comment at 677-678 describes as meaning "the binary
is unsigned" — conflating "unsigned" with "cannot be checked here".
**Cross-ref. Delta:** W29 is cited at line 677 for replacing a fabricated identifier with the real
certificate subject; verification was not part of it.
**Fix(es):** add a trust verdict alongside the subject — `SignatureTrust { Valid, Invalid,
Unsigned, Unverifiable }` from `WinVerifyTrust` (or `X509Chain.Build` on the extracted cert plus a
file-hash check) — and render the subject only together with its trust state. Map the non-Windows
and exception cases to `Unverifiable`, never to `Unsigned`.
**Code Sample:**

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx.Kit/DNSCapture.cs:679-690
private static string? SigningIdentifier(string executablePath)
{
    try
    {
        using var cert = X509Certificate.CreateFromSignedFile(executablePath);
        return cert.Subject;      // extracted, never verified
    }
    catch
    {
        return null;              // "unsigned" and "couldn't check" collapse here
    }
}
```

**[D113]** **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** DhcpPushedDNS returns null for unreadable registry (broadened catch); DetectGatewayAsync distinguishes "no DHCP DNS" from "could not determine".
**Criticality:** MEDIUM
**Location:** `Windows/dotNET/Syxx.Kit/NetworkKeyState.cs:664-678`, consumed at `630, 649`
**Issue:** `DhcpPushedDNS` catches **only** `System.Security.SecurityException`. `OpenSubKey` and
`GetValue` can also raise `UnauthorizedAccessException`, `IOException` (key marked for deletion) and
`ObjectDisposedException`; those escape into `DetectGatewayAsync`, which has no `try` around the
call at line 630 — so a transient registry condition turns the whole gateway audit into an
unhandled exception rather than a degraded result.

When it *does* return empty, that is rendered as a definite absence: line 649 simply omits the
"DHCP pushed DNS" clause from the detail string, so "the router pushed no DNS" and "we could not
read the registry" produce byte-identical output. Same class as W4-03, lower blast radius.
**Cross-ref. Delta:** none — new (C1 is the workstream, per the comment at line 600).
**Fix(es):** return `List<string>?` (null = unreadable) and have `DetectGatewayAsync` append
"DHCP-pushed DNS: could not be determined" in that case. Broaden the catch to
`catch (Exception ex) when (ex is SecurityException or UnauthorizedAccessException or IOException)`.
**Code Sample:**

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx.Kit/NetworkKeyState.cs:664-678
public static List<string> DhcpPushedDNS(string interfaceId)
{
    var servers = new List<string>();
    if (!OperatingSystem.IsWindows() || string.IsNullOrEmpty(interfaceId)) return servers;
    try
    {
        using var key = Microsoft.Win32.Registry.LocalMachine.OpenSubKey(
            $@"SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters\Interfaces\{interfaceId}");
        var raw = key?.GetValue("DhcpNameServer") as string;
        ...
    }
    catch (System.Security.SecurityException) { /* unreadable — honest empty, not a guess */ }
    return servers;      // empty means BOTH "none pushed" and "unreadable"
}
```

**[D114]**
**FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Added `dotnet publish` of `Syxx.csproj` into the same `$PublishDir` and a `Test-Path` assertion before zipping. Fixed signtool instructions to sign PE files (`SyxxUI.exe`, `Syxx.exe`) not the archive. Guarded WiX hint on `installer.wxs` existence.
**Criticality:** MEDIUM
**Location:** `build-installer.ps1:46-56, 64, 74, 78-83`; consumed by
`Windows/dotNET/SyxxUI/Views/CageView.xaml.cs:93-97`
**Issue:** The distributable package publishes **only** `SyxxUI.csproj` (line 46). The `syxx` CLI
(`Syxx.csproj`, `AssemblyName=Syxx`) is never published into `$PublishDir`, and it is the CLI that
performs the privileged packet capture. `CageView.LocateCageBinary` looks for `syxx.exe`/`Syxx.exe`
next to the GUI exe (lines 93-97) and will not find it, so **Cage is structurally non-functional in
every shipped zip** — the user gets "Live capture is unavailable: the syxx capture binary isn't
installed alongside the app" (CageView.xaml.cs:126) from a correctly installed product.

Two further defects in the same script: line 74 tells the operator to `signtool sign … $ZipPath` —
`signtool` cannot sign a `.zip`, so the printed remedy fails; and line 81 references
`installer.wxs`, which does not exist anywhere in the repository.
**Cross-ref. Delta:** none — new.
**Fix(es):** add a second `dotnet publish` of `Windows\dotNET\Syxx\Syxx.csproj` into the same
`$PublishDir` before zipping, and assert `Test-Path "$PublishDir\Syxx.exe"` before `Compress-Archive`
so the omission cannot recur silently. Sign `SyxxUI.exe` and `Syxx.exe` (the PE files) rather than
the archive. Either commit `installer.wxs` or drop the WiX branch.
**Code Sample:**

```powershell
# build-installer.ps1:46-52 — GUI only; the capture binary is never packaged
dotnet publish Windows\dotNET\SyxxUI\SyxxUI.csproj `
    -c $Configuration `
    -p:Platform=$Platform `
    -r win-${Platform} `
    --self-contained true `
    -o $PublishDir
```

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/SyxxUI/Views/CageView.xaml.cs:93-97 — what it looks for, and never finds
foreach (var name in new[] { "syxx.exe", "Syxx.exe" })
{
    var local = Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, name);
    if (File.Exists(local)) return local;
}
```

**[D115]**
**FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Replaced the stale duplicate script with a one-line delegation to the canonical `build.ps1` at the repo root, eliminating wrong paths, `$args` shadowing, and the transposed output path.
**Criticality:** MEDIUM
**Location:** `scripts/win-build.ps1:16-19, 27-29, 48`
**Issue:** A stale duplicate of the repo-root `build.ps1` that cannot run. Every project path is

instead of `Windows\dotNET\SyxxUI\SyxxUI.csproj` — so the first `dotnet build` fails with
MSB1009 and the script exits 1 (line 32-33). It also names its parameter `$args` (line 27),

**[E056]**
**FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Added home plug to snapcraft.yaml; CageCommand now detects snap confinement and emits explicit inconclusive result with snap connect remedy.
**Criticality:** CRITICAL
**Location:** `Linux/snap/snapcraft.yaml:16-19` vs `Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/CageCommand.cs:69-70,251-256`
and `Windows/dotNET/Syxx.Kit/Trust/Trust.cs:105,241,312`
**Issue:** Two confinement gaps that both fail as *silent degradation*, not as an error the
user can read:

1. **Raw sockets.** `CageCommand` opens `SocketType.Raw` sockets for capture. Under
   `confinement: strict` the only interface that can permit that is `network-observe`, which is
   listed — but `network-observe` is **not auto-connected**. On a fresh `snap install syxx` it
   is disconnected until the user runs `snap connect syxx:network-observe`, so Cage's capture
   path fails on every first run. `OpenRawSocket` returns `Socket?` (nullable), i.e. the code
   is built to keep going on failure — so a confinement denial surfaces as "0 queries captured"
   rather than "capture is not permitted", the exact class the honesty spine forbids.
2. **No `home` plug.** Witness key (`~/.syxx/witness.key`), the answer ledger, sentinel
   snapshot and home baseline are all written under `SpecialFolder.UserProfile`. Strict
   confinement remaps `$HOME` into `~/snap/syxx/<rev>/`, so the user's evidence and the Witness
   *signing key* live inside a directory that `snap remove` deletes, and cannot be read from a
   normal path.
**Cross-ref. Delta:** none — new.
**Fix(es):** add `home` (and `personal-files`/`removable-media` if report export is a
requirement); either request a store auto-connect assertion for `network-observe` or make Cage
detect `EPERM`/`EACCES` on socket creation and emit an explicit *inconclusive — capture not
permitted by confinement* rather than an empty-but-successful capture. Add a `snap connect`
line to the install docs regardless.
**Code Sample:**

```yaml
# Linux/snap/snapcraft.yaml:16-19
    plugs:
      - network
      - network-bind
      - network-observe   # not auto-connect; no `home` plug at all
```

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/CageCommand.cs:251-256
private static Socket? OpenRawSocket(AddressFamily family, ProtocolType protocol)
{
    ...
        socket = new Socket(family, SocketType.Raw, protocol);
```

**[E057]**
**FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Fixed ROOT to resolve to repo root; grep now matches const (not static); version extraction fails closed; icon miss is fatal; Depends changed from libicu-dev to libicu74.
**Criticality:** CRITICAL
**Location:** `Ubuntu/build_deb.sh:6,9,13,29-31,67-69,78`
**Issue:** The .deb builder cannot produce a package. Four independent defects:

1. `cd "$(dirname "$0")"` puts `ROOT` at `Ubuntu/`, then line 29 does `cd Ubuntu/SyxxUI.Avalonia`
   → `Ubuntu/Ubuntu/SyxxUI.Avalonia`, which does not exist. Under `set -e` the script dies here.
2. Line 13 greps for `public static string Version`; the actual declaration in
   `Windows/dotNET/Syxx.Kit/SyxxConfig.cs:13` is `public const string Version = "2.0.0"`.
   The grep matches nothing, so `SYXX_VERSION` is **empty** — `DEB_NAME` becomes
   `syxx__amd64.deb` and the control file gets `Version: -1234`, which `dpkg-deb` rejects.
3. Line 67 tests `Design/logos/syxx-logo-source.png` relative to `Ubuntu/`; the file is at the
   repo root. The `if` guard makes the miss **silent**, so the package ships a `.desktop` with
   `Icon=syxx` and no icon file — a broken launcher entry with no warning.
4. Line 78 declares `Depends: libc6, libicu-dev`. `libicu-dev` is the *build* package; the
   runtime dependency is `libicu74`. On a clean Ubuntu 24.04 desktop this either pulls dev
   headers onto an end-user machine or fails to resolve.
**Cross-ref. Delta:** none — new.
**Fix(es):** `ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"`; grep `public const string Version`
and `exit 1` if the capture is empty (never build an unversioned package); resolve the icon
from repo root and **fail** rather than skip when it is missing; depend on `libicu74`.
**Code Sample:**

```bash
# Ubuntu/build_deb.sh:13
SYXX_VERSION=$(grep 'public static string Version' ../Windows/dotNET/Syxx.Kit/SyxxConfig.cs | sed 's/.*"\(.*\)".*/\1/')
# Ubuntu/build_deb.sh:29
cd Ubuntu/SyxxUI.Avalonia      # ROOT is already Ubuntu/ -> Ubuntu/Ubuntu/...
# Ubuntu/build_deb.sh:67-69
if [ -f "Design/logos/syxx-logo-source.png" ]; then   # wrong cwd; miss is silent
```

**[E059]**
**FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Removed || true from useradd/adduser; script now aborts (exit 1) if the syxx service user cannot be created, instead of silently falling back to root.
**Criticality:** CRITICAL
**Location:** `scripts/deploy.sh:191-204,319`
**Issue:** Silent fallback to **root**. Every user-creation branch ends in `|| true`, so a
failure is swallowed; the script then tests `id -u syxx` and, when absent, sets `SVC_USER=root`
and writes `User=root` into the unit. The only signal is one `echo "WARNING: ..."` at line 202,
buried ~180 lines above the final `🎉 Deployed.` banner — and the deploy still reports
`✅ Daemon running.` and exits 0. The network-facing DNS packet parser then runs as root with
`AmbientCapabilities=CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE`, which is exactly the state A110 was raised to
remove. A security control that degrades itself and still reports success is the deploy-script
analogue of a fabricated verdict.
**Cross-ref. Delta:** A110 (`DELTAS.md:19086`) — regressed / incompletely closed.
**Fix(es):** drop `|| true`; if the `syxx` account cannot be created, **abort** (`exit 1`) with
the useradd stderr shown. If a root fallback must exist, gate it behind an explicit
`SYXX_ALLOW_ROOT_SERVICE=1` opt-in and print it again in the final banner.
**Code Sample:**

```bash
# scripts/deploy.sh:193-204
    useradd --system --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin syxx || true
...
if id -u syxx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  SVC_USER=syxx
else
  echo "WARNING: could not create the 'syxx' service user; the unit will fall back to root. ..."
  SVC_USER=root
fi
```

**[E060]**
**FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code), already resolved.** The || echo was already removed (A120 fix); dependency install failure now propagates via set -euo pipefail.
**Criticality:** CRITICAL

**Issue:** The inner dependency-check block is written carefully to **fail closed** — it
`exit 1`s with "❌ cryptography is NOT importable. /api/pubkey WILL 500 and every leak
attestation is unverifiable." That hard exit is then thrown away by the outer
`|| echo "⚠️  dependency install reported a problem — see above."` on line 137. The deploy
continues through systemd install, nginx, backups and Sentry, and terminates with

(lines 124-135) describes this precise two-day silent outage as the thing it exists to prevent.

capture the status and re-print a hard `❌ DEPLOY INCOMPLETE` line in the final banner and

```bash
# scripts/deploy.sh:137
remote "bash -s" <<'PIPEOF' || echo "⚠️  dependency install reported a problem — see above."
...
# scripts/deploy.sh:151-153  (this exit 1 never reaches the operator's shell)
  echo "❌ cryptography is NOT importable. /api/pubkey WILL 500 ..."
```

**[E062]**
**FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Hoisted SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN and SENTRY_URL to workflow-level env: so step if: conditions can evaluate them before the step env: block is applied.
**Criticality:** HIGH
**Location:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:148-149,156-157,168-169,180-181`
**Issue:** Every Sentry step is gated on `if: env.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN != ''`, but
`SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` is only defined in each step's own `env:` block. GitHub Actions evaluates a
step `if:` **before** applying that step's `env:`, and there is no workflow- or job-level `env:`
in this file. `env.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` is therefore always the empty string and **all four steps
are permanently skipped** — including `Create Sentry release (server)` on the linux-x64 leg.
The comment on line 145 says the steps "no-op if SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN is not configured"; in fact
they no-op even when it *is* configured. Crash reports from the first-ship platform arrive
unsymbolicated forever, and CI shows green skips that read as "not configured".
**Cross-ref. Delta:** none — new.
**Fix(es):** hoist to a workflow-level `env: SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}`,
or change the guard to `if: secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN != ''` at job level via an output.
**Code Sample:**

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml:180-181
      - name: Create Sentry release (server)
        if: matrix.kind == 'dotnet' && runner.os == 'Linux' && matrix.rid == 'linux-x64' && env.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN != ''
        env:
          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}   # applied AFTER `if:` is evaluated
```

**[E063]**
**FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Added post-restart verification: sleep 3 + systemctl is-active check + curl /api/pubkey probe; deploy now aborts if the daemon is not actually serving.
**Criticality:** HIGH
**Location:** `scripts/deploy.sh:365-368`
**Issue:** "Reports success without verifying the thing it claims to have done." The unit is
`Type=simple`, so `systemctl restart` returns 0 as soon as systemd has forked the process —
before Python has parsed a single import. A daemon that dies one second later (bad env file,
missing module, port 53 already bound) still yields `✅ Daemon running.` and the run proceeds to
the `🎉 Deployed.` banner. There is no `systemctl is-active`, no `journalctl` tail, and no HTTP
probe of `:8080` anywhere in the script.
**Cross-ref. Delta:** none — new.
**Fix(es):** either `Type=notify` with `sd_notify` in `server.py`, or after restart:
`sleep 3; systemctl is-active --quiet syxx-server || { journalctl -u syxx-server -n 50 --no-pager; exit 1; }`
plus `curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/pubkey` as the real bar.
**Code Sample:**

```bash
# scripts/deploy.sh:365-368
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable syxx-server.service
systemctl restart syxx-server.service
echo "✅ Daemon running."
```

**[E064]**
**FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Added `User=${SVC_USER}`, `NoNewPrivileges`, `ProtectSystem=strict`, `ReadWritePaths`, `PrivateTmp`, `ProtectHome`, `CapabilityBoundingSet=` to `syxx-backup.service`; moved script to `/usr/local/libexec/syxx-backup.sh` (root-owned 0755) outside the syxx-writable tree. Success-message gating was already fixed (A120).
**Criticality:** HIGH
**Location:** `scripts/deploy.sh:493-520`
**Issue:** Two problems in the backup provisioning block.

1. **False claim of a taken backup.** Line 517 runs the initial backup with
   `|| echo "⚠️  initial backup run failed"`, and line 518 then *unconditionally* prints
   `✅ DB backup timer installed (daily). First backup taken now.` When the run fails, the
   operator is told a restore point exists when none does. Directly violates honesty rule 4.
2. **`syxx-backup.service` has zero hardening and no `User=`.** It runs as **root**, whereas
   `syxx-server.service` runs as `syxx`. It has none of `NoNewPrivileges`, `ProtectSystem`,
   `PrivateTmp`, `ProtectHome`, `CapabilityBoundingSet`. Its `ExecStart` is
   `/bin/sh ${REMOTE_DIR}/scripts/syxx-backup.sh` — a script inside a directory that line 310
   `chown -R`s to the unprivileged `syxx` account. Any compromise of the daemon user rewrites
   that script and gets root at the next timer fire (a straightforward privilege-escalation
   path created by the combination of these two lines).
Additionally the block claims "the online backup" is safe (`syxx-backup.sh` comments), but
**no restore path exists** anywhere: `grep 'def restore'` in `Server/syxx_server/db.py` returns
nothing. A backup never proven restorable is claimed safety that is not provided.
**Cross-ref. Delta:** SD-56 (`Server/SERVER_DELTAS.md:135`) — backup leg implemented, but the
verification, hardening and StartLimit legs are not.
**Fix(es):** print the ✅ line only on success and `exit 1` otherwise; add `User=syxx`,
`NoNewPrivileges=true`, `ProtectSystem=strict`, `ReadWritePaths=${REMOTE_DIR}/backups`,
`PrivateTmp=true`, `CapabilityBoundingSet=` to `syxx-backup.service`; move the script out of
the `syxx`-writable tree (e.g. `/usr/local/libexec/syxx-backup.sh`, root-owned 0755); add and
CI-test a restore path.
**Code Sample:**

```bash
# scripts/deploy.sh:495-503 — no User=, no hardening at all
cat > /etc/systemd/system/syxx-backup.service <<UNIT
[Unit]
Description=Syxx DB online backup (rotating)
After=syxx-server.service
[Service]
Type=oneshot
Environment=SYXX_SERVER_DIR=${REMOTE_DIR}
ExecStart=/bin/sh ${REMOTE_DIR}/scripts/syxx-backup.sh
UNIT
# scripts/deploy.sh:517-518
systemctl start syxx-backup.service || echo "⚠️  initial backup run failed — check: journalctl -u syxx-backup"
echo "✅ DB backup timer installed (daily). First backup taken now."   # printed either way
```

**[E065]**
**FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Added all missing hardening directives: `RestrictAddressFamilies`, `SystemCallFilter`, `SystemCallArchitectures`, `MemoryDenyWriteExecute`, `ProtectKernelTunables/Modules/Logs`, `ProtectControlGroups`, `ProtectClock`, `ProtectProc`, `RestrictNamespaces/SUIDSGID/Realtime`, `LockPersonality`, `PrivateUsers`, `UMask=0077`, `StartLimitIntervalSec=300`, `StartLimitBurst=5`.

no fail2ban and no `unattended-upgrades` anywhere in the script (`grep -i 'ufw|fail2ban|

**[E067]**
**FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Token now created with `ApiToken.get_default_scopes()` instead of `scopes=0`. Project-creation curl now captures HTTP status to distinguish 409 (exists) from auth/other errors, replacing the misleading `|| echo "(may already exist)"`.
**Criticality:** HIGH
**Location:** `scripts/deploy-sentry.sh:191-201,232-236,244-250`
**Issue:** Step 6 cannot work, and reports its failure as something else. The API token is
created with **`scopes=0`** and the inline comment `# will be updated below` — nothing below
updates it. A zero-scope token is rejected (403) by every subsequent call. Those calls are
`curl -sf ... >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "  (may already exist)"`, so an authorization failure is
reported to the operator as *the project already exists* — an error message about entirely the
wrong thing. The DSN loop then prints `NOT FOUND` / `ERROR` per project, which is the only
honest output in the block, but by then the "API token created. Creating projects..." banner
(line 214) has already claimed success.

**[E069]**
**FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Certbot failure now exits 1 with a clear error message instead of printing a warning and continuing to the "✅ Reverse proxy configured." banner. `X-Forwarded-Proto` was already present in the nginx config (line 421).
**Criticality:** MEDIUM
**Location:** `scripts/deploy.sh:412-416,483-485`
**Issue:** Certbot failure is downgraded to a warning (line 416 `|| echo "⚠️  certbot
failed..."`), and because the whole TLS heredoc is wrapped in `if remote ...; then echo
"✅ Reverse proxy configured."`, the block still reports success — the `set -e` inside the
heredoc is neutralised by the `||`. The nginx config written at 393-405 has `listen 80` only;
the 443 server block is added *by certbot*. So a certbot failure leaves the entire site,
including the licensing and leak-attestation API, on **plaintext HTTP** while the deploy prints
`✅ Reverse proxy configured.` The block also sets no `X-Forwarded-Proto` header, so the
application cannot tell it is being served over TLS even when certbot succeeds.
**Cross-ref. Delta:** SD-57 (`Server/SERVER_DELTAS.md:137`) — the renewal-verification leg was
implemented (lines 428-459, good), the issuance-failure leg was not.
**Fix(es):** make certbot failure fatal when `SETUP_TLS=1`; verify with
`curl -fsS https://${DOMAIN}/` from the deploy host before printing ✅; add
`proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;`.
**Code Sample:**

```bash
# scripts/deploy.sh:415-416
    --non-interactive --agree-tos -m "\${EMAIL}" --redirect \
    || echo "⚠️  certbot failed (every name must resolve here first). HTTP proxy is live; re-run certbot later."
# scripts/deploy.sh:483
  then echo "✅ Reverse proxy configured."
```

**[E070]**
**FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** `syxx-backup.sh` now uses `grep`/`cut` to extract only the three variables it needs (`SYXX_DB_PATH`, `SYXX_DB_BACKUP_DIR`, `SYXX_DB_BACKUP_KEEP`) instead of shell-sourcing the systemd-format env file. Shell metacharacters in unrelated values (Stripe keys, mail-from) can no longer corrupt or execute during backup.
**Criticality:** MEDIUM
**Location:** `scripts/deploy.sh:214-306` vs `Server/scripts/syxx-backup.sh:17-21`
**Issue:** Format mismatch between the two consumers of `/etc/syxx/syxx.env`. systemd's
`EnvironmentFile=` uses its own parser; `syxx-backup.sh` **shell-sources** the same file with
`set -a; . /etc/syxx/syxx.env`. Values that are perfectly legal for systemd — anything
containing a space, `$`, backtick, `<`, `>`, `;` or `|` — either break the backup script or are
executed by it. `SYXX_MAIL_FROM=Syxx <noreply@syxx.app>` is exactly that shape and is already
the default at `deploy.sh:43`; the file's own header comment (line 215) documents only "no
'export', no spaces around '='", which does not cover value content. The file is 0600 root-only,
so this is a robustness/edge-case bug rather than an injection vector from an unprivileged
user — but a Stripe or Keygen secret containing a shell metacharacter silently corrupts every
backup run.
**Cross-ref. Delta:** A109 (`DELTAS.md:19045`) — related; the 0600 EnvironmentFile design is
correct, the second shell-sourcing consumer is the gap.
**Fix(es):** have `syxx-backup.sh` read the values it needs with a `grep`/`cut` parser matching
systemd semantics, or run the backup via `systemd-run --property=EnvironmentFile=...` so only
one parser exists.
**Code Sample:**

```sh
# Server/scripts/syxx-backup.sh:17-21
if [ -r /etc/syxx/syxx.env ]; then
    set -a
    . /etc/syxx/syxx.env     # shell-sources a systemd-format file
    set +a
fi
```

(3) `SENTRY_DOMAIN` now applied to `sentry.conf.py` via `system.url-prefix` instead of a no-op grep. **[E072]**
**FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code), already resolved.** `GetTracerouteCommand` method exists at `TracerouteRunner.cs:88-100` with correct platform switch: Windows uses `tracert -d -h {maxHops} -w {waitMs}`, Linux/macOS uses `traceroute -n -m {maxHops} -w {waitSeconds}` with proper ms→s conversion (floor of 1). Build confirmed: no CS0103 for this method.
**Criticality:** CRITICAL — ship blocker (empirically reproduced, not read)
**Location:** `Windows/dotNET/Syxx.Kit/TracerouteRunner.cs:32`; consumers
`Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/RouteCommand.cs:33`, `Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Program.cs:664`
**Issue:** **The Linux CLI does not compile.** `TracerouteRunner.TraceAsync` calls
`GetTracerouteCommand(target, maxHops, waitMs)`, and that method **does not exist anywhere in the
repository** — a full-tree grep for the identifier returns exactly one hit, the call site itself.
The XML doc above it (`TracerouteRunner.cs:10-12`) describes the method that was supposed to
choose `tracert` on Windows and `traceroute` on Linux/macOS; the method was never written (or was
deleted). I ran the real build rather than reasoning about it:

```
$ dotnet build -c Release -r linux-x64 --self-contained   # Windows/dotNET/Syxx
Syxx.Kit/TracerouteRunner.cs(32,40): error CS0103: The name 'GetTracerouteCommand' does not exist in the current context
Syxx.Kit/TracerouteRunner.cs(32,22): error CS8130: Cannot infer the type of implicitly-typed deconstruction variable 'fileName'.
Syxx.Kit/TracerouteRunner.cs(32,32): error CS8130: Cannot infer the type of implicitly-typed deconstruction variable 'args'.
    57 Warning(s)
    3 Error(s)
```

`Syxx.Kit` is a `ProjectReference` of the CLI (`Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Syxx.csproj:20`), so the CLI
project cannot produce an artifact for `linux-x64` or `linux-arm64` at all. This subsumes the
snap's `command:`-name defect a sibling filed (`Linux/snap/snapcraft.yaml:13`): even with the
right binary name there is no binary to name, because the `dotnet` part fails at compile. Nothing
in CI catches it — see [L4-14].
**The committed/indexed state is not better, only quieter.** `git diff` on this file shows the
working tree is a half-finished edit; the **staged** version hardcodes:

```csharp
FileName = "tracert",
// -d skips reverse-name lookups; -h caps hops; -w bounds each probe's wait.
Arguments = $"-h {maxHops} -w {waitMs} -d {target}",
```

`tracert` does not exist on Linux, so `Process.Start` throws `Win32Exception` on every invocation,
which `catch { return lines; }` (`TracerouteRunner.cs:63-66`) swallows into an **empty list**. So
in the indexed state `syxx route <anything>` on Linux always prints "Traceroute failed, timed out,
or produced no output." (`RouteCommand.cs:36`) and the guided Portal always prints "(No hops
returned — the trace could not run or timed out.)" (`Program.cs:667`) — an entire discipline that
can never produce evidence on the ship-first platform, reported as a transient timeout rather than
"not implemented on this platform". Pick either state and Linux Portal/route is dead.
**Cross-ref. Delta:** none — new. (Supersedes/precedes the snap `command:` finding.)
**Fix(es):** implement the platform switch that the doc comment already promises, e.g.
`OperatingSystem.IsWindows() ? ("tracert", $"-h {maxHops} -w {waitMs} {target}") : ("traceroute", $"-m {maxHops} -w {waitMs/1000} {target}")` — note Linux `traceroute -w` takes **seconds**, not
milliseconds, so a straight port of the Windows argument string produces a 1000-second per-probe
wait. Then add a `dotnet build -r linux-x64` leg to CI so a missing method can never again be
discovered by a user instead of a compiler.
**Code Sample:**

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx.Kit/TracerouteRunner.cs:30-33
try
{
    var (fileName, args) = GetTracerouteCommand(target, maxHops, waitMs);  // CS0103 — no such method
```

**[E073]**
**FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** `Main` now seeds `Environment.ExitCode = 2` (inconclusive) at entry, matching the macOS contract default. `--version` and `--help` explicitly set exit 0. Interactive/guided mode sets exit 0 on normal completion. Mirror command now sets exit 1 on redirection/censorship detection, exit 0 on clean, exit 2 on inconclusive/degraded. Unknown commands already set exit 3 (B253).
**Criticality:** CRITICAL — honesty violation (doctrine #2, #3)
**Location:** `Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Program.cs:15` (`static async Task Main`), and the entire
dispatcher `Program.cs:56-86`; the only `Environment.ExitCode` writes in the whole CLI are
`Program.cs:84`, `Commands/WitnessCommand.cs:63`, `Commands/LeakCommand.cs:80,100,126,166,171`.
Compare `macOS/Sources/SyxxCLI/SyxxCLI.swift:7-8,196-202`.
**Issue:** **Every scripted invocation on Linux returns exit 0 regardless of verdict**, except
`syxx leak` and two usage errors. `Main` returns `Task` (not `Task<int>`) and no subcommand
returns a status to the dispatcher — `RunAsync` is `Task` for all fifteen commands, so a
subcommand *structurally cannot* influence the exit code except by reaching out and mutating the
global `Environment.ExitCode`, which twelve of the fifteen never do. Concretely, all of these
exit **0**:

- `syxx cage` when the raw socket could not be opened and **nothing was captured**
  (`Commands/CageCommand.cs:71-77` — bare `return`)
- `syxx witness verify forged.json` printing `❌ INVALID SIGNATURE`
  (`Commands/WitnessCommand.cs:288-311` — no `ExitCode` write on any branch)
- `syxx route` printing "Traceroute failed, timed out, or produced no output."
  (`Commands/RouteCommand.cs:34-38`)
- `syxx mirror` printing `🚨 MALICIOUSLY REDIRECTED` (`Program.cs:565`)
- `syxx firstrun`, `syxx forensics`, `syxx sentinel`, `syxx filter`, `syxx warp`, `syxx speed`,
  `syxx nslook`, `syxx lan`, `syxx key`, `syxx unbound` — every branch of every one.

macOS documents and implements `0=clean, 1=threat, 2=inconclusive, 3=error` and, critically,
**defaults to `2` (inconclusive)** so an unreached verdict cannot read as clean
(`SyxxCLI.swift:8`). The C# CLI defaults to `0` (clean). A CI job, a cron wrapper, or an `&&`
chain on Ubuntu therefore reads "clean" from a Cage run that captured zero packets and from a
Witness verification that failed. This is doctrine #2 ("missing data is not clean data") realised
at the process-contract level, on the ship-first platform.
**Cross-ref. Delta:** parallel to the macOS `run(args:) -> Void` finding a sibling filed; this is
the C# twin and it is worse (macOS at least defaults to 2).
**Fix(es):** change `Main` to `static async Task<int> Main` and every `RunAsync` to
`Task<int>`, returning the macOS mapping; seed the default to `2`. Where a command has no verdict
concept (`--help`, `--version`) return 0 explicitly. Add a CI leg that asserts the code for a
known-forged witness file is 1 and for an unrunnable cage is 2.
**Code Sample:**

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Program.cs:15  — no int, no default
static async Task Main(string[] args)
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/CageCommand.cs:71-77 — nothing captured, exits 0
if (socketV4 == null && socketV6 == null)
{
    Console.WriteLine("\n🚨 ERROR: Could not open raw socket for DNS packet capture.");
    ...
    return;              // <-- Environment.ExitCode untouched => 0 => "clean"
}
```

```swift
// macOS/Sources/SyxxCLI/SyxxCLI.swift:7-8  — the contract Linux does not honour
// 9.4: standardized exit codes — 0=clean, 1=threat, 2=inconclusive, 3=error
nonisolated(unsafe) static var exitCode: Int32 = 2  // default inconclusive
```

**[E074]**
**FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** `Confirmed` now sets exit 1 (threat), `NotDetected` sets exit 0 (clean), usage error (missing token) sets exit 3 (error), and "all probes FAILED" sets exit 3 (error) instead of the previous inverted exit 1 (which read as "threat" under the shared contract).
**Criticality:** CRITICAL — honesty violation + inverted contract
**Location:** `Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/LeakCommand.cs:116-128` and `:163-172`
**Issue:** `syxx leak` is the *only* subcommand that sets exit codes, and it sets them wrong in
both directions:

1. **A confirmed DNS leak exits 0.** `case LeakVerdict.Confirmed:` (`:118-120`) prints the
   observed resolvers and falls out of the switch without touching `Environment.ExitCode` — so a
   collector-attested, signed *positive detection of a DNS leak* returns the same status as a
   clean run. Under the macOS mapping a threat is 1.
2. **An error is reported as a threat.** The "all probe dispatches FAILED, the leak test did not
   run and nothing was measured" branch (`:170-171`) sets `ExitCode = 1`. Under the documented
   macOS mapping (`SyxxCLI.swift:7`) `1` means **THREAT DETECTED**. So on Linux the *only* way to
   get exit 1 out of `syxx leak` is for the test to have failed to run, and a script following the
   published contract will read "threat" from "nothing was measured" — the exact inversion
   doctrine #2 forbids, with the sign flipped as well.
   `ExitCode = 1` is also used at `:100` for a pure usage error (missing token/key), which macOS
   maps to `3`.
**Cross-ref. Delta:** none — new.
**Fix(es):** `Confirmed => 1`, `NotDetected => 0`, `Inconclusive/Untested => 2`, usage/transport
error `=> 3`. Then delete the divergent local convention and drive it from one shared mapping the
Kit owns, so macOS and Linux cannot drift again.
**Code Sample:**

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/LeakCommand.cs:116-128
switch (result.Verdict)
{
    case LeakVerdict.Confirmed:
        Console.WriteLine($"\n{result.ObservedResolvers.Count} resolver(s) observed");
        break;                       // <-- leak CONFIRMED, exit code stays 0
    case LeakVerdict.NotDetected:
        Console.WriteLine("\n1 resolver observed — verify it matches your provider");
        break;                       // also 0 — indistinguishable from the line above
    default:
        Console.WriteLine("\nINCONCLUSIVE");
        Environment.ExitCode = 2;
        break;
}
```

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/LeakCommand.cs:168-171 — "nothing measured" => 1 => "THREAT"
Console.WriteLine("\nINCONCLUSIVE — all probe dispatches FAILED, so the leak test did not run ...");
Environment.ExitCode = 1;
```

**[E075]**
**FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** `OpenRawSocket` now guards the Windows-only `SIO_RCVALL` ioctl behind `OperatingSystem.IsWindows()`. On Linux/macOS, `SOCK_RAW + IPPROTO_UDP` already receives all UDP packets (including DNS) with root/CAP_NET_RAW — no ioctl needed. Error message now platform-aware: Linux says "requires root or CAP_NET_RAW. Run: sudo syxx cage" instead of the unexecutable "Open Command Prompt/PowerShell as Administrator".
**Criticality:** CRITICAL — capability impossible on Linux, reported as a privilege problem
**Location:** `Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/CageCommand.cs:251-285` (`OpenRawSocket`), consumed at
`:69-77`; snap plugs `Linux/snap/snapcraft.yaml:14-18`
**Issue:** **`syxx cage` can never capture a single packet on Linux, at any privilege level**, and
the only explanation it gives the user is a Windows one. `OpenRawSocket` ends with
`socket.IOControl(IOControlCode.ReceiveAll, byIn, byOut)` — SIO_RCVALL, a Windows-only ioctl. I ran
it on .NET 10/Unix (same `SocketPal.Unix` used on Linux):

```
raw v4 socket (non-root)         : SocketException: Permission denied
  SetSocketOption(IP, HeaderIncluded): SocketException: Protocol not available
  IOControl(ReceiveAll)          : PlatformNotSupportedException:
      Socket.IOControl handles Windows-specific control codes and is not supported on this platform.
```

So there are two independent dead ends: unprivileged → `SocketException` at construction; **root or
`CAP_NET_RAW` → `PlatformNotSupportedException` at the `IOControl` line**, which the same
`catch (Exception)` at `:277-284` converts to `return null`. Both sockets null ⇒ `:71-77` fires:

> 🚨 ERROR: Could not open raw socket for DNS packet capture.
> This usually requires Administrator privileges. **Open Command Prompt/PowerShell as Administrator** and run: syxx cage

That instruction is unexecutable on Ubuntu, and it is worse than useless: it tells the user the
capability exists and they merely lack rights, when in fact the code path cannot work on their OS
even as root. (There is no `AF_PACKET`/`SOCK_RAW`+`ETH_P_ALL` path anywhere in the file, and
`ProtocolType.IP` = 0 is not a receiving protocol on Linux — the promiscuous behaviour comes
*entirely* from the Windows-only SIO_RCVALL.) The snap makes it structurally worse still: it plugs
`network-observe` only (`snapcraft.yaml:14-18`), and an AppArmor `capability net_raw` allowance
does not *grant* a capability to an unprivileged user process — it only permits one already held.
Compounding: the command then `return`s with exit code 0 ([L4-02]).
**Cross-ref. Delta:** none — new. Related to the sibling's snap `command:` finding only in that
both make the shipped artifact non-functional.
**Fix(es):** (a) short term, gate on `OperatingSystem.IsWindows()` and emit an explicit
`UNTESTED — live DNS capture is not implemented on Linux in this build` with exit 2, never the
Administrator text; (b) real fix, implement the Linux capture path (`AF_PACKET`/`SOCK_RAW`
`ETH_P_ALL` with a BPF filter, or an `nflog`/`eBPF` reader), declare the needed interface in the
snap, and make the privilege check `geteuid()==0 || CAP_NET_RAW` rather than a Windows token check
([L4-05]); (c) a CI leg that runs `syxx cage --duration 1` on ubuntu-latest and asserts the output
does not contain "Command Prompt" and the exit code is not 0.
**Code Sample:**

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/CageCommand.cs:270-275
socket.SetSocketOption(SocketOptionLevel.IP, SocketOptionName.HeaderIncluded, family == AddressFamily.InterNetwork);
byte[] byIn = new byte[] { 1, 0, 0, 0 };
byte[] byOut = new byte[] { 1, 0, 0, 0 };
socket.IOControl(IOControlCode.ReceiveAll, byIn, byOut);   // PlatformNotSupportedException on Linux, always
return socket;
```

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/CageCommand.cs:73-76 — the Linux user's only guidance
Console.WriteLine("\n🚨 ERROR: Could not open raw socket for DNS packet capture.");
Console.WriteLine("    This usually requires Administrator privileges. Open Command Prompt/PowerShell as Administrator and run: syxx cage");
```

**[E076]** **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** IsElevated() platform-switched (geteuid on Linux/macOS); RunCageCaptureAsync uses platform-appropriate elevation; raw Win32Exception numbers replaced with actionable guidance.
**Criticality:** HIGH — guided Cage is unreachable on Linux and fails with a Windows error number
**Location:** `Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Program.cs:896-906` (`IsElevated`), `:801-825`
(`RunCageCaptureAsync`), user-facing string `:807`
**Issue:** The privilege check the guided flow uses is `WindowsIdentity.GetCurrent()` /
`WindowsPrincipal.IsInRole(WindowsBuiltInRole.Administrator)`, wrapped in `catch { return false; }`.
Measured on .NET 10/Unix:

```
WindowsIdentity.GetCurrent(): PlatformNotSupportedException: Windows Principal functionality is not supported on this platform.
```

So `IsElevated()` returns **false on Linux unconditionally — including under `sudo`**. The guided
Cage therefore always takes the elevation branch and prints a promise it cannot keep
(`Program.cs:807`): "Live packet capture needs Administrator rights — accept the elevation prompt
to continue (the capture opens in an elevated window)". It then sets `UseShellExecute = true` and
`Verb = "runas"` (`:808-809`). Measured on Unix:

```
Process.Start(UseShellExecute=true, Verb="runas"): Win32Exception: Unknown error: 1155
```

which `catch (Exception ex)` at `:821` renders to the user as
`⚠️ Live capture could not start: Unknown error: 1155.` — a bare Windows `ERROR_NO_ASSOCIATION`
code shown to an Ubuntu user. Menu option `[5] Cage` is thus 100% non-functional on the ship-first
platform, and the one line of the message that is honest ("Cage stays UNTESTED (this is NOT a
clean result)") is buried behind a meaningless number. Note the failure is *never* the real cause
([L4-04]); even a working `pkexec`/`sudo` re-exec would still hit the SIO_RCVALL wall.
**Cross-ref. Delta:** none — new.
**Fix(es):** replace `IsElevated()` with a platform switch — `OperatingSystem.IsWindows()` →
current logic; Linux/macOS → `geteuid() == 0` (or read `/proc/self/status` `CapEff` for
CAP_NET_RAW). Replace the `runas` re-exec on Linux with `pkexec`/`sudo -n` (or, better, tell the
user to run `sudo syxx cage` and do not attempt to self-elevate). Never surface a raw
`Win32Exception` number as the user-facing reason.
**Code Sample:**

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Program.cs:896-906 — always false on Linux, even as root
static bool IsElevated()
{
    try
    {
        using var id = System.Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity.GetCurrent();   // throws PNSE on Linux
        var principal = new System.Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal(id);
        return principal.IsInRole(System.Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole.Administrator);
    }
    catch { return false; }
}
```

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Program.cs:806-810
Console.WriteLine("• Live packet capture needs Administrator rights — accept the elevation prompt to continue (the capture opens in an elevated window).");
psi.UseShellExecute = true;
psi.Verb = "runas"; // UAC elevation   -> Win32Exception 1155 on Linux
```

**[E077]** **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** CageCommand captures directory restricted to 0700/0600 via SyxxPaths.EnsurePrivateDir/RestrictToOwner on Linux; applies to all four output files.
**Criticality:** HIGH — privacy guarantee stated in the code is false on Linux
**Location:** `Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/CageCommand.cs:49-57` (comment + `Directory.CreateDirectory`),
`:83` (`new FileStream(...)`), `:211` (`File.WriteAllText(queriesFilePath, ...)`)
**Issue:** The comment at `:49-51` states the design intent: *"Write captures under the per-user
LocalApplicationData profile (**ACL'd to this user**) … identity-bearing data that must not be left
world-readable wherever the tool ran."* On Linux that ACL does not happen. `Directory.CreateDirectory`
and the default `FileStream`/`File.WriteAllText` modes are umask-derived, and I measured the actual
values on .NET 10/Unix with a default umask:

```
dir mode  = UserRead|UserWrite|UserExecute|GroupRead|GroupExecute|OtherRead|OtherExecute   (0755)
file mode = UserRead|UserWrite|GroupRead|OtherRead                                          (0644)
```

There is **no `File.SetUnixFileMode` call anywhere in `CageCommand.cs`** (the CLI has exactly one,
in `WitnessCommand.cs:420`). So on Ubuntu the raw NDJSON capture — which by the file's own
description embeds full process paths and *every DNS query the user made during the capture window* —
lands **world-readable** at `~/.local/share/Syxx/captures/`, as does the always-retained
`Syxx Cage Queries <stamp>.json`. On a shared/managed Ubuntu box (a lab, a work laptop with a
second account, a container with a shared home) any local user can read the target's full browsing
history. The same applies to the `--keep` path and to `Program.cs:792-793`, which reads the same
directory.
**Cross-ref. Delta:** none — new. Adjacent to C037/C039 (already-fixed honesty deltas on this file),
which fixed *claims about* the files but not their permissions.
**Fix(es):** on non-Windows, `File.SetUnixFileMode(capturesDir, UserRead|UserWrite|UserExecute)`
(0700) immediately after `Directory.CreateDirectory`, and 0600 on each of the three files right
after creation — before the first byte is written, not after. On Windows keep/add the explicit ACL
the comment already claims. Add a test that creates a capture dir on Linux and asserts the mode.
**Code Sample:**

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/CageCommand.cs:49-54
// Write captures under the per-user LocalApplicationData profile (ACL'd to this user),   <-- not on Linux
// not the working directory. Records embed process paths like C:\Users\<name>\… —
// identity-bearing data that must not be left world-readable wherever the tool ran.
string capturesDir = Path.Combine(
    Environment.GetFolderPath(Environment.SpecialFolder.LocalApplicationData), "Syxx", "captures");
Directory.CreateDirectory(capturesDir);      // 0755 on Linux; no SetUnixFileMode anywhere in this file
```

**[E078]** **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Key file created atomically with 0600 via FileStreamOptions.UnixCreateMode; ~/.syxx dir restricted to 0700; chmod failure split into separate try with honest "key written but permissions failed" message.
**Criticality:** HIGH — private key briefly world-readable; a *successful* write reported as failure
**Location:** `Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/WitnessCommand.cs:39-56`, `:405-422`
**Issue:** Two defects in the same eight lines of `syxx witness --gen-keypair`, both Linux-only.

1. **Write-then-chmod race.** `File.WriteAllTextAsync(keyFile, priv + "\n")` (`:47`) creates the
   Ed25519 **private key** at the umask-derived default — measured **0644, world-readable** — and
   only then does `RestrictKeyFileToCurrentUser` (`:48`) call `File.SetUnixFileMode(..., 0600)`
   (`:420`). Every other local user can read the key in the window between. The enclosing
   `Directory.CreateDirectory(dir)` (`:46`) creates `~/.syxx` at **0755** and is *never* chmod'd at
   all, so the directory holding every Syxx secret and baseline stays world-traversable for good.
   The doc comment at `:397-403` explicitly claims this is "the Windows/Linux equivalent of macOS's
   chmod 0600" — it is not, because macOS's Swift twin creates the file with the mode, and this
   creates it and then narrows it.
2. **A false failure message.** `RestrictKeyFileToCurrentUser` is inside the same `try` as the
   write (`:43-56`). If `SetUnixFileMode` throws (it can: `UnauthorizedAccessException`/`IOException`
   on a mount that does not support `chmod`, e.g. an exFAT/NTFS or some overlay `$HOME`), the
   handler prints `[ERROR] Could not write private key to {keyFile}` and `[ERROR] Refusing to print
   the private key to stdout` — while **the private key is in fact already on disk, at 0644**. The
   user is told nothing was written and no key exists; a world-readable signing key exists. That is
   doctrine #4 inverted: a real artifact reported as absent.
**Cross-ref. Delta:** D086 — the fix that introduced this code. D086 closed "private key printed to
stdout"; it did not close "private key written world-readable then narrowed", and it introduced
the false-failure branch.
**Fix(es):** create the file with the mode atomically —
`new FileStream(keyFile, new FileStreamOptions { Mode = CreateNew, Access = Write, UnixCreateMode = UserRead|UserWrite })`
— and `SetUnixFileMode(dir, 0700)` on `~/.syxx`. Split the try blocks so a chmod failure reports
"key WAS written to {path} but its permissions could not be restricted — treat it as compromised
and regenerate", never "could not write".
**Code Sample:**

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/WitnessCommand.cs:43-56
try
{
    string? dir = Path.GetDirectoryName(keyFile);
    if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(dir)) Directory.CreateDirectory(dir);   // ~/.syxx at 0755, never narrowed
    await File.WriteAllTextAsync(keyFile, priv + "\n");               // private key at 0644
    RestrictKeyFileToCurrentUser(keyFile);                            // 0600 — one syscall too late
    ...
}
catch (Exception ex)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"[ERROR] Could not write private key to {keyFile}: {ex.Message}");  // false if the throw was the chmod
    Console.WriteLine("[ERROR] Refusing to print the private key to stdout — use --key-file <path> to choose a location.");
}
```

**[E079]** **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** All three 8.8.8.8 fallbacks removed (Prophet, Mirror, witness create); replaced with INCONCLUSIVE refusal matching LeakCommand pattern; witness create refuses to sign when resolver is undetectable.
**Criticality:** CRITICAL — measures a resolver the user does not use and reports it as theirs
**Location:** `Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Program.cs:397-403` (Prophet), `:493-499` (Mirror),
`Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/WitnessCommand.cs:106-111` (`witness create`)
**Issue:** When resolver discovery returns nothing, three CLI paths **silently substitute Google
Public DNS and then run the whole discipline against it**, presenting the result as a measurement
of the user's network:

```csharp
var servers = NetworkKeyState.GetSystemDNSServers();
string localResolver = servers.FirstOrDefault();
if (localResolver == null)
{
    Console.WriteLine("⚠️ System resolver undetectable — falling back to 8.8.8.8");
    localResolver = "8.8.8.8";
}
...
Console.WriteLine($"• Current local DNS server: {localResolver}");
```

Everything downstream — the A/AAAA queries, DNSSEC status, the NXDOMAIN and DNSSEC canaries,
latency, stability, wildcard synthesis, denial-of-existence, dual-stack, EDNS0, `version.bind`
(`Program.cs:413-479`), and in Mirror the entire vantage comparison and its
`✅ SECURE — no answer tampering, censorship, or redirection detected for {domain}` verdict
(`Program.cs:570`) — then describes **8.8.8.8**, labelled as "Current local DNS server". A user on
a hijacked network, which is precisely the condition that breaks resolver discovery, is told their
resolver is clean when Google's was measured. `syxx witness create` is the worst case
(`WitnessCommand.cs:106-117`): it takes that substituted vantage and produces an **Ed25519-signed,
tamper-evident evidence snapshot** attesting to a resolver the subject never queried.

The codebase already knows this is wrong and does it correctly two screens away —
`LeakCommand.cs:77-82` and `Program.cs:696-702` both print
`INCONCLUSIVE: No system DNS resolvers detected. Refusing to fall back to public resolvers` and
stop. The three paths above are the un-migrated remainder. This matters more on Linux than on
Windows because Linux resolver discovery is the fragile path (`NetworkKeyState.cs:131-192` shells
to `resolvectl status` with a 3s timeout and falls back to `NetworkInterface` enumeration), and
under snap strict confinement `resolvectl` is not staged at all
(`Linux/snap/snapcraft.yaml:30-31` stages only `libicu74`).
**Cross-ref. Delta:** none — new. Same class as the already-fixed leak-test refusal.
**Fix(es):** delete all three fallbacks. Print the `LeakCommand` wording, mark the section
UNTESTED, exit 2. `witness create` must **refuse to sign** when the vantage is a substitute — a
signature over an unrepresentative measurement is worse than no signature.
**Code Sample:**

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/WitnessCommand.cs:106-117 — signs a snapshot of 8.8.8.8
string systemResolver = NetworkKeyState.GetSystemDNSServers().Count > 0 ? NetworkKeyState.GetSystemDNSServers()[0] : null;
if (systemResolver == null)
{
    Console.WriteLine("⚠️ System resolver undetectable — falling back to 8.8.8.8");
    systemResolver = "8.8.8.8";
}
...
var comparison = await VantageComparer.CompareVantagePointsAsync(domain, localServer: systemResolver);
var snapshot = WitnessSigner.CreateSignedSnapshot(domain, comparison, key);   // signed, attributed to the user
```

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/LeakCommand.cs:77-82 — the correct behaviour, already shipped
if (servers.Count == 0)
{
    Console.WriteLine("INCONCLUSIVE: No system DNS resolvers were detected. Refusing to fall back to public resolvers for a leak test.");
    Environment.ExitCode = 2;
    return;
}
```

**[E080]** **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Console.ReadLine() null now exits with code 3 and actionable message instead of falling to "Invalid choice" infinite loop; fixes /dev/null, snap desktop, CI/cron invocations.
**Criticality:** HIGH — non-interactive `syxx` spins forever
**Location:** `Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Program.cs:50-53`, `:170-263` (menu loop), `:189`
**Issue:** `syxx` with **no arguments** enters the interactive guided menu — and that is exactly how
the snap launches (`Linux/snap/snapcraft.yaml:12-15` defines `command:` with no default
subcommand, so a `.desktop` launcher, `snap run syxx`, a systemd unit, or a cron entry all reach
it). The loop reads:

```csharp
string choice = Console.ReadLine()?.Trim().ToUpper() ?? "";
```

`Console.ReadLine()` returns `null` at **EOF**, which the `?? ""` converts into an empty string,
which falls to `default: Console.WriteLine("Invalid choice. Enter 1-6, C, L, or Q.");` (`:260-262`)
and loops. `running` is only cleared by an explicit `Q`/`QUIT`/`EXIT` (`:254-258`), so there is no
EOF exit path at all. `syxx < /dev/null`, `echo | syxx`, a snap launched from a desktop file with
no attached tty, or any CI/cron invocation therefore **loops forever at full CPU**, printing the
72-line ASCII-art banner's menu block repeatedly and filling the journal. I confirmed
`Console.IsOutputRedirected == True` is already observable in this runtime, so the guard is
available; nothing consults it.
**Cross-ref. Delta:** none — new.
**Fix(es):** capture the raw `Console.ReadLine()` and treat `null` as an immediate, honest exit:
`if (raw is null) { Console.Error.WriteLine("syxx: no terminal attached — run a subcommand, e.g.`syxx firstrun`."); Environment.ExitCode = 3; return; }`. Additionally, when
`Console.IsInputRedirected` is true, skip the guided menu entirely and print the usage block.
**Code Sample:**

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Program.cs:189 — EOF becomes "" becomes "invalid choice" becomes an infinite loop
string choice = Console.ReadLine()?.Trim().ToUpper() ?? "";
...
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Program.cs:260-262
default:
    Console.WriteLine("Invalid choice. Enter 1-6, C, L, or Q.");
    break;                       // <-- `running` still true; no null/EOF case anywhere in the loop
```

**[E081]** **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code), already resolved.** LicenseManager now uses ISecretStore abstraction (DpapiSecretStore on Windows, LinuxSecretStore with libsecret/AES-GCM on Linux); Protect/Unprotect no longer throw DllNotFoundException.
**Criticality:** HIGH — every Pro-gated CLI path throws `DllNotFoundException` on Linux
**Location:** `Windows/dotNET/Syxx.Kit/LicenseManager.cs:22-42` (`DpapiNative`, `DllImport("crypt32.dll")`),
`:182-188` (`Protect`), `:517-599` (`IsFeatureUnlockedAsync`, unguarded `Protect` at `:532` and
`:580`); CLI call sites `Program.cs:526`, `:573`, `:684`, `:933`
**Issue:** Licence storage is Windows DPAPI via a raw `DllImport("crypt32.dll")`. `Unprotect` swallows
everything (`:199-202`) so `GetStoredLicenseKey()` merely returns `null` forever on Linux — but
**`Protect` has no `try`/`catch` at all**, and `IsFeatureUnlockedAsync` calls it unconditionally on
the ordinary path:

```csharp
// LicenseManager.cs:578-582
if (nowMillis > maxSeenMillis)
{
    dict["trialMaxTime"] = Protect(nowMillis.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture));   // <-- throws on Linux
    SaveConfig(dict);
}
```

`nowMillis > maxSeenMillis` is true on essentially every run (`maxSeenMillis` starts at 0 and can
never be persisted). Measured on .NET 10/Unix:

```
System.DllNotFoundException: Unable to load shared library 'crypt32.dll' or one of its dependencies.
```

None of the four CLI call sites wraps the call in a `try`: `Program.cs:526` (Mirror Pro
corroboration), `:573` (Mirror content-warp gate), `:684` (Glutton entry), `:933` (Witness banner).
So on Ubuntu, guided **Mirror**, **Glutton** and **Witness** terminate with an unhandled
`DllNotFoundException` stack trace the moment they check entitlement — and, because
`SentrySdk.Init` is live (`Program.cs:18-27`), the crash is reported as a product exception rather
than as an unimplemented platform. The build already tells us this: `dotnet build -r linux-x64`
emits eight `CA1416` warnings — *"This call site is reachable on all platforms.
'LicenseManager.Protect(string)' is only supported on: 'windows'"* — at `LicenseManager.cs:212,
221, 291, 336, 356, 370, 532, 547, 570, 580`. Warnings, not errors, so CI is green.
**Cross-ref. Delta:** none — new. Overlaps the sibling's shared-Kit Linux-crash lane; filed here
because the reachable paths are four CLI commands and the user-visible consequence is CLI-only.
**Fix(es):** implement a non-Windows credential store behind the same two methods (libsecret via
`secret-tool`, or an AES-GCM blob keyed from a 0600 file under `~/.syxx` — plus
`SetUnixFileMode(0600)` on `ConfigPath`, which `SaveConfig` at `:162-180` also omits). Until then,
make `Protect`/`Unprotect` platform-switched and non-throwing, and have the CLI print
`Pro entitlement is not available in this Linux build` rather than crash. Promote `CA1416` to an
error for the `linux-*` RIDs so a Windows-only P/Invoke cannot reach a Linux ship again.
**Code Sample:**

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx.Kit/LicenseManager.cs:31-34
[DllImport("crypt32.dll", SetLastError = true, CharSet = CharSet.Unicode)]
private static extern bool CryptProtectData(
    ref DATA_BLOB pDataIn, string? szDataDescr, ref DATA_BLOB pOptionalEntropy,
    IntPtr pvReserved, IntPtr pPromptStruct, int dwFlags, out DATA_BLOB pDataOut);
```

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Program.cs:684 — Glutton, no try/catch around the throwing call
var check = await LicenseManager.IsFeatureUnlockedAsync(); // tuple — not ProbeRunner-wrappable
Console.WriteLine($"• Feature status: {check.Message}");
```

**[E082]** **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** NullResolverSwitcher.Restore now returns (false, false, "system DNS switching is not implemented for this OS") instead of fake (true, false, null); Disable() correctly reports failure on Linux.
**Criticality:** MEDIUM-HIGH — fabricated success: reports a system change that cannot happen
**Location:** `Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/UnboundCommand.cs:66-71`, `:73-97`;
`Windows/dotNET/Syxx.Kit/UnboundManager.cs:100-102`, `:152-166`, `:288-295`
**Issue:** On Linux `UnboundManager` is constructed with `NullResolverSwitcher`
(`UnboundManager.cs:100-102` — the real switcher is `WindowsSystemResolverSwitcher`, chosen only
under `OperatingSystem.IsWindows()`). `NullResolverSwitcher.SetServers` honestly returns
`(false, false, "system DNS switching is not implemented for this OS in Syxx.Kit yet")`, so
`syxx unbound enable` fails honestly. But `Restore` returns **`(true, false, null)`** with the
comment *"nothing was changed, so 'restore' is a no-op success"*. `Disable()` propagates that
straight to `UnboundResultKind.Disabled` (`UnboundManager.cs:166`), and the CLI prints:

```
  Disabling local Unbound; restoring the original system resolver…
  DISABLED — restored: (DHCP-provided)
```

So on Ubuntu `syxx unbound disable` claims it restored the user's original system resolver when it
is *structurally incapable* of touching system DNS on that OS — the exact "fabricated value shown
as measured" doctrine #4 forbids. An operator who ran `enable`, saw it fail, and then ran `disable`
to be safe is told the system was reverted; nothing was ever inspected. The `--help` line
(`Program.cs:107`) advertises `enable | disable` with no platform caveat.
**Cross-ref. Delta:** none — new.
**Fix(es):** give `ISystemResolverSwitching` a tri-state return, or have `NullResolverSwitcher.Restore`
return `(false, false, "system DNS switching is not implemented for this OS")` so `Disable()` maps
to `UnboundResultKind.Inconclusive` and the CLI prints
`INCONCLUSIVE — system DNS was never switched by Syxx on this OS; nothing to restore`. Implement a
real Linux switcher (`resolvectl dns <iface> 127.0.0.1` / `systemd-resolved` drop-in, with the
snapshot/auto-revert failsafe the doc promises) before advertising `enable`/`disable` on Linux.
**Code Sample:**

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx.Kit/UnboundManager.cs:288-295
public sealed class NullResolverSwitcher : ISystemResolverSwitching
{
    public IReadOnlyList<string> Snapshot() => Array.Empty<string>();
    public (bool ok, bool elevationDenied, string? reason) SetServers(IReadOnlyList<string> servers) =>
        (false, false, "system DNS switching is not implemented for this OS in Syxx.Kit yet");
    public (bool ok, bool elevationDenied, string? reason) Restore(IReadOnlyList<string> servers) =>
        (true, false, null); // nothing was changed, so "restore" is a no-op success   <-- prints "DISABLED — restored"
}
```

**[E083]** **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Five Windows-specific strings fixed: sentinel --forget now prints resolved path; cage help text and unbound enable use platform-switched "administrator"/"root (sudo)"; CageCommand already had E075 fix for PowerShell reference.
**Criticality:** MEDIUM — Windows-only instructions and a Windows path shown to Linux users
**Location:** `Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/SentinelCommand.cs:31`,
`Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/CageCommand.cs:74`, `Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Program.cs:807`, `:104`,
`Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/UnboundCommand.cs:61`
**Issue:** Five user-facing strings assume Windows and are printed verbatim on Linux. The most
concrete is `sentinel --forget`, which tells a Linux user where their erased data lived using a
**Windows environment-variable path with backslashes**:

> 🧹 Forgotten: Sentinel baseline, home baseline, and the passive-DNS answer ledger erased (`%USERPROFILE%\.syxx`).

The same file gets it right 24 lines later (`SentinelCommand.cs:55` says `~/.syxx/home-baseline.json`),
so the two halves of one command disagree about where the user's own files are. The rest:
`CageCommand.cs:74` "Open Command Prompt/PowerShell as Administrator" (see [L4-04]);
`Program.cs:807` "accept the elevation prompt … the capture opens in an elevated window" (see
[L4-05]); `Program.cs:104` help text "cage — Packet capture (requires administrator)";
`UnboundCommand.cs:61` "(requires Administrator; …)". "Administrator" is not a role that exists on
Ubuntu; the word for it is root/sudo. A user who cannot find `%USERPROFILE%` reasonably concludes
the deletion did not happen.
**Cross-ref. Delta:** none — new. Catalog target: `outputs-catalog.csv`.
**Fix(es):** route every path through one helper that prints the real resolved directory
(`Path.Combine(Environment.GetFolderPath(SpecialFolder.UserProfile), ".syxx")`) rather than a
platform token, and replace "Administrator" with a platform-switched word ("administrator" /
"root (sudo)"). These are user-facing strings — copy-gate per `AGENTS.md`.
**Code Sample:**

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/SentinelCommand.cs:31
Console.WriteLine("🧹 Forgotten: Sentinel baseline, home baseline, and the passive-DNS answer ledger erased (%USERPROFILE%\\.syxx).");
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/SentinelCommand.cs:55 — same command, correct path
Console.WriteLine("\n⚠️  The home baseline file (~/.syxx/home-baseline.json) appears to be corrupted and cannot be read.");
```

**[E084]** **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Banner box now built programmatically from a single width constant with PadRight; content rows guaranteed to match border width on any terminal.
**Criticality:** LOW — the flagship command's banner is visibly broken
**Location:** `Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/FirstRunCommand.cs:39-43`
**Issue:** The `syxx firstrun` banner box does not close. Decoding the `\uXXXX` escapes and counting
cells (all characters involved are East-Asian-width *Narrow*, so display width == code-point count):

```
39  width=69  ╔═══…═══╗
40  width=66  ║                    Syxx First-Run Scan                         ║
41  width=67  ║       One-button full scan — graded result before config        ║
42  width=66  ║   © J.J. Warne d/b/a MilkandGin · feedback@milkandgin.com      ║
43  width=69  ╚═══…═══╝
```

The three content rows are 2–3 cells short of the borders, so the right-hand `║` never lines up
with `╗`/`╝` on any terminal. This is not a font or locale problem — the literals are simply
mis-counted. It is the first output of the command the product markets as the one-keystroke entry
point, on the platform that ships first. (Note: I found **no** ANSI-colour emission anywhere in
`Program.cs` or `Commands/**` — `grep` for escape sequences and `Console.ForegroundColor` returns
nothing — so there is no colour-when-not-a-TTY defect to report; the output problems are width and
glyph choice only.)
**Cross-ref. Delta:** none — new.
**Fix(es):** pad the three content strings to 69 cells, or build the box programmatically from a
single width constant so it cannot drift. Add a test that asserts all five lines of the banner have
equal display width.
**Code Sample:**

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/FirstRunCommand.cs:40  (66 cells inside a 69-cell box)
Console.WriteLine("║                    Syxx First-Run Scan                         ║");
```

**[E085]** **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Added LinuxArpParser (ip neigh show + Linux arp -a fallback); LANCartographer uses platform-appropriate command/parser; LANSnapshot.IsPartial/PartialReason convenience properties added; LanCommand and Program.cs Portal both check IsPartial before reporting empty LAN.
**Criticality:** HIGH — `syxx lan` returns "no devices" on every Linux box, and the CLI drops the
Kit's own "this is partial" flag
**Location:** `Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/LanCommand.cs:53-57`, `:76-82`;
`Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Program.cs:641-652`; underlying
`Windows/dotNET/Syxx.Kit/LAN/LanCartography.cs:352-361` and `WindowsArpParser.ParseRow:132-153`
**Issue:** `LANCartographer.Snapshot()` runs `arp -a` and parses the result with a class literally
named `WindowsArpParser`, whose row rule is:

```csharp
string ip = tokens[0];
// A row must start with a dotted-quad; otherwise it is noise.
if (ip.Count(c => c == '.') != 3) return null;
```

Linux `arp -a` emits `? (192.168.1.1) at 3c:37:86:aa:bb:cc [ether] on wlp2s0` — token 0 is a
hostname or `?`, never a dotted quad — so **every row is discarded even on a machine with a full
ARP cache**. And on a default Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 there is no `arp` binary at all (`net-tools` is
not installed by default, and the snap stages only `libicu74`,
`Linux/snap/snapcraft.yaml:30-31`), so `Process.Start` throws and the Kit returns
`new LANSnapshot(..., isPartial: true)`.

The CLI then converts both of those into a **negative measurement**:

- `syxx lan` → "No devices found in the ARP cache. **(Try generating traffic first, e.g. ping your
  gateway.)**" (`LanCommand.cs:55`) — blaming the user's traffic for a missing/incompatible tool.
- guided Portal → `• On-link devices  : 0` (`Program.cs:645`) with no caveat, immediately above a
  route trace that also cannot run ([L4-01]).

Worse, the Kit *does* signal the difference: `LANSnapshot.IsPartial` (`LanCartography.cs:278,284`).
A repo-wide grep shows `IsPartial` is **written in those two lines and read nowhere in the entire
.NET tree** — not by `LanCommand`, not by `Program.cs`, not by the GUI. The honest
"this snapshot is incomplete" bit is computed and thrown away, which is exactly how an
empty-but-normal report gets manufactured (doctrine #2).
**Cross-ref. Delta:** D081 is cited at `LanCartography.cs:359` for the *error-collapse* fix that
introduced `isPartial` — the flag was added but never surfaced.
**Fix(es):** (1) add a `LinuxArpParser` (or read `/proc/net/arp`, or shell `ip neigh show`, which
is always present on modern Ubuntu and needs no `net-tools`); (2) make both call sites branch on
`snapshot.IsPartial` and print `UNTESTED — the ARP table could not be read (<reason>); this is not
evidence that the LAN is empty`; (3) never print the "generate traffic" hint when the device list
is partial rather than genuinely empty.
**Code Sample:**

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx.Kit/LAN/LanCartography.cs:356-367
output = _runner.Run("arp", new[] { "-a" });   // absent on default Ubuntu; different format when present
...
var devices = WindowsArpParser.Parse(output)   // rejects every Linux row
```

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/LanCommand.cs:53-57 — partial becomes "empty, and it's your fault"
if (snapshot.Devices.Count == 0)
{
    Console.WriteLine("No devices found in the ARP cache. (Try generating traffic first, e.g. ping your gateway.)");
    return;                       // snapshot.IsPartial never consulted, here or anywhere
}
```

**[E087]** **FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Trust.cs (AnswerLedger.Save, Sentinel.SaveSnapshot, HomeBaseline.Save) and LicenseManager.SaveConfig now call SyxxPaths.EnsurePrivateDir on ~/.syxx dirs and SyxxPaths.RestrictToOwner on all written files; IntegrityTag HMAC sidecars also restricted.
**Criticality:** HIGH — the user's passive-DNS history and home-network baseline are world-readable
**Location:** `Windows/dotNET/Syxx.Kit/Trust/Trust.cs:105,118-120` (answer ledger),
`:241,246-247` (sentinel snapshot), `:312,317-318` (home baseline);
reached from `Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/SentinelCommand.cs:44-51` (`--set-home`),
`Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Program.cs:943-965` (guided Witness → `Sentinel.SaveSnapshot`)
**Issue:** Every persistent state file the CLI writes on Linux is created with the umask default —
**0644 inside a 0755 `~/.syxx`** (measured; see [L4-06] for the raw numbers). Three files:
`answer-ledger.json` is the **passive-DNS ledger**, i.e. a running record of the domains this user
has resolved and the answers they got; `sentinel-snapshot.json` and `home-baseline.json` record the
user's resolvers, interfaces, VPN state and home-network fingerprint. All three are written via a
bare `Directory.CreateDirectory(...)` + `File.WriteAllText(...)` pair with **no `File.SetUnixFileMode`
anywhere in `Trust.cs`** — the single such call in the entire .NET tree is `WitnessCommand.cs:420`.
On any multi-user or container-shared Ubuntu host, `cat ~victim/.syxx/answer-ledger.json` yields
their browsing history. The same applies to `LicenseManager.SaveConfig`
(`LicenseManager.cs:162-180`), which writes `~/.config/Syxx/license.json` at 0644.

This is a Linux-only exposure: on Windows these paths inherit a per-user profile ACL, which is why
it was never noticed. Linux ships first.
**Cross-ref. Delta:** none — new. Same root cause as [L4-06] and [L4-07]; filed separately because
the files, the writers and the reaching commands are different.
**Fix(es):** one shared helper — `SyxxPaths.EnsurePrivateDir(path)` doing
`Directory.CreateDirectory` then `File.SetUnixFileMode(dir, UserRead|UserWrite|UserExecute)` on
non-Windows — used by `Trust.cs`, `LicenseManager.SaveConfig`, `CageCommand`, and
`WitnessCommand`; and write files through `FileStreamOptions.UnixCreateMode = UserRead|UserWrite`
so they are never briefly readable. Add the Linux-gated permission test described in [L4-15].
**Code Sample:**

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx.Kit/Trust/Trust.cs:117-120 — the passive-DNS ledger, 0644 in a 0755 dir
Directory.CreateDirectory(Path.GetDirectoryName(path)!);
...
File.WriteAllText(path, json);
```

**[E088]**
**Criticality:** MEDIUM — `syxx firstrun --help` runs a multi-minute network scan instead of printing help
**Location:** `Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/FirstRunCommand.cs:13-26`;
`Windows/dotNET/Syxx.Kit/SyxxConfig.cs:19-42`; `Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Program.cs:73-76`
**Issue:** `SyxxConfig.HandleGlobalFlags` is the shared `--help`/`--version` gate that every
subcommand calls first. `grep -L` across `Commands/*.cs` shows exactly one file that does **not**
call it: `FirstRunCommand.cs`. Its argument loop (`:18-26`) recognises only `--domain`/`-d` and
silently ignores everything else, so `syxx firstrun --help` and `syxx firstrun -h` fall straight
through to `FirstRunScan.RunAsync` (`:52`) and execute the full scan — the one the top-level help
advertises as the "Five-minute first-run scan" (`Program.cs:109`). A user probing an unfamiliar
command with `-h` gets several minutes of live DNS probing against their resolver instead of a
usage string.

Secondary, same area: the version flag is spelled inconsistently. The dispatcher accepts
`--version` / **`-v`** (`Program.cs:73-74`); `HandleGlobalFlags` accepts `--version` / **`-V`**
(`SyxxConfig.cs:26`). So `syxx -v` works and `syxx nslook -v` does not, while `syxx nslook -V`
works and `syxx -V` does not — the same binary, two conventions.
**Cross-ref. Delta:** none — new.
**Fix(es):** add the `HandleGlobalFlags(args, "syxx firstrun", "Usage: syxx firstrun [--domain <d>]")`
guard as the first statement of `FirstRunCommand.RunAsync`, and reject unrecognised flags rather
than ignoring them (an unknown flag on a command that spends five minutes probing should be an
error, exit 3). Accept both `-v` and `-V` in both places.
**Code Sample:**

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/FirstRunCommand.cs:13-18 — no HandleGlobalFlags guard
public static async Task RunAsync(string[] args)
{
    string? domain = null;

    // Parse --domain / -d
    for (int i = 0; i < args.Length; i++)
```

```csharp
// Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/FilterCommand.cs:15-16 — what every other command does
if (SyxxConfig.HandleGlobalFlags(args, "syxx filter",
    "Usage: syxx filter [@resolver]   (verifies DNS blocklist enforcement + bypass paths)")) return;
```

**FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code).** Added HandleGlobalFlags guard to FirstRunCommand, reject unknown flags with exit 3, accept both -v and -V for --version in both dispatcher and HandleGlobalFlags.
