## Cross-platform witness round-trip audit — 2026-07-29 (syxx-engineer)

Both entries below were CONFIRMED by running the real macOS and Windows CLIs against each
other's real output on 2026-07-29, not by reading code. Both are FIXED in this pass; the
acceptance bar recorded with each is a real bidirectional round trip, and both directions
were observed to complete.

---

**[B252]**
**FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code) — Fix 3 only.** DoH outcomes now render with a clear "UNSIGNED — not covered by the Ed25519 seal" marker in both Swift and C# SignedIncidentReport. The verification section also notes when DoH data is present but unsigned. Full fix (Fix 1/2: signing dohOutcomes with format version bump) remains open — requires format version bump coordination across both platforms.
**Criticality:** HIGH — a whole block of evidence inside a document Syxx labels "Tamper-evident"
is neither signed nor checked, and can be rewritten to say anything while the tool still prints
VALID.
**Location:** `macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/SignedEvidencePayload.swift:33-36`, `:190` (`dohOutcomes:
nil`); `Windows/dotNET/Syxx.Kit/SignedEvidencePayload.cs:38-44`, `:175`;
`macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/WitnessSigner.swift:262-274` and
`Windows/dotNET/Syxx.Kit/WitnessSigner.cs:271-296` (the display-integrity rebuild, which never
looks at `dohOutcomes`).
**Issue:** `ComparisonResult.dohOutcomes` is written into `witness.json` and rendered to the
user, but `SignedEvidencePayload.build`/`Build` always sets the canonical `dohOutcomes` to nil,
so the DoH observations are not covered by the Ed25519 signature; and because the D083/B037
display-integrity guard rebuilds only what the canonical payload contains, they are not covered
by that guard either. Found while running the negative controls for B251. Demonstrated on BOTH
platforms against a real macOS-signed snapshot: rewriting `comparison.dohOutcomes.Cloudflare`
from `{"status":"transportError","records":[]}` to
`{"status":"success","records":[{"rdata":"6.6.6.6",...}]}` still reports:

      Verification: VALID (Tamper-evident — Ed25519 signed)

A related, narrower instance: because the canonical payload records only a per-resolver
`success` boolean (`!didFail`) rather than the typed status, swapping one non-failing status for
another (e.g. `nxDomain` -> `success`) on a resolver with no records is also undetectable, since
neither the boolean nor the answer sets change.
**Honesty note:** the DoH block is presented to the user inside the same document as the signed
evidence with no visual distinction between what the signature covers and what it does not, so a
reader has no way to know which half is attested.
**Cross-ref. Delta:** sits directly on the **E011** canonical-payload contract; found during the
**B251** fix. Related to **B037** (per-resolver outcomes are signed evidence too), which made
the UDP outcomes tamper-evident but left the DoH ones out.
**Fix(es):** NOT fixed in this pass, deliberately. Covering `dohOutcomes` changes the signed
bytes and therefore needs a `formatVersion` bump with verifier-before-signer migration on both
platforms (the pattern `SignedEvidencePayload.cs:96-101` already documents for v3), plus a
user-visible wording decision about how an unattested section is labelled — neither is a minimal
change and the wording needs approval. Options, in order of preference:
[Fix 1] Populate the canonical `dohOutcomes` (the field already exists on both platforms
precisely so byte-parity holds) under a new format version, and extend the display-integrity
rebuild to compare it.
[Fix 2] Carry the typed status in the canonical outcome instead of the bare `success` boolean,
closing the narrower `nxDomain` -> `success` instance at the same time. Note this collides with
the **E020** direction of removing platform-divergent free text from signed bytes; the status is
an enum, not free text, so it is safe to sign where the error string is not.
[Fix 3] Until either lands, render the unsigned sections distinctly so the user is not invited
to trust them as attested.
**Characterisation tests (deliberately assert the CURRENT, DEFECTIVE behaviour so that fixing
B252 turns them red and forces a deliberate update):**
`macOS/Tests/SyxxKitTests/WitnessCrossPlatformGoldenVectorTests.testKnownGap_B252_rewritingDoHEvidenceStillReadsValid`
and `Windows/dotNET/Syxx.Tests/WitnessCrossPlatformGoldenVectorTests.KnownGap_B252_RewritingDoHEvidenceStillReadsValid`.

---

**[B253]**
**Criticality:** HIGH — `syxx witness verify` exits 0 on Windows for a TAMPERED snapshot, so any
script, CI gate, or automation that checks the exit code reads forged evidence as verified.
**Location:** `Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/WitnessCommand.cs:246-300` (the verify branch never
assigns `Environment.ExitCode`); `macOS/Sources/SyxxCLI/SyxxCLI.swift:7-8`, `:15`, `:196-202`.
**Issue:** Found while establishing the B251 round-trip acceptance bar. Measured on this host,
2026-07-29, against real snapshots:

    Windows  witness verify <valid file>                  -> exit 0
    Windows  witness verify <display-mismatch tamper>     -> exit 0     <-- false clean
    Windows  witness verify <unreadable / malformed>      -> exit 0     <-- false clean
    macOS    witness verify <valid file>                  -> exit 2
    macOS    witness verify <display-mismatch tamper>     -> exit 2
    macOS    witness report / nslook / witness --help     -> exit 2

Windows reports success for every outcome including forgery. macOS reports 2 for every outcome
including success, so the code carries no information there either — but at least never claims
clean. The printed text is correct and honest on both platforms (`VALID` vs `DISPLAY MISMATCH`);
it is only the machine-readable channel that lies, which is the channel automation reads.
macOS additionally does not honour its OWN documented contract: `SyxxCLI.swift:7` states
"0=clean, 1=threat, 2=inconclusive, 3=error" and `:8` initialises `exitCode = 2`, but only the
guided-mode synthesis path (`:196-202`) ever assigns it, so every subcommand — including
`--help` — exits 2.
**Cross-ref. Delta:** found during the **B251** cross-platform round-trip verification. Same
honesty spine as **D099** (which fixed the printed text for exactly this command, but not the
exit status).
**Fix(es):** NOT fixed here — it is CLI-surface work outside this pass's scope and the mapping is
a user-visible contract that needs approval.
[Fix 1] Map `SnapshotVerification` onto the documented codes on BOTH platforms: `Valid` -> 0;
`InvalidSignature` / `DisplayMismatch` -> 1 (tampered); `Expired` / `Stale` / `FutureDated` /
`UntrustedSigner` / `MalformedInput` / `UnsupportedFormat` -> 2 (inconclusive, not clean, not
tampered); an I/O or parse failure -> 3.
[Fix 2] Make macOS's per-subcommand paths set `exitCode` rather than inheriting the default, and
add a test per subcommand that asserts the code, since a default that is never overwritten is
indistinguishable from a deliberate one.
[Fix 3] Document the mapping in the `--help` text so scripting against it is supportable.

**STATUS 2026-07-29 (syxx-engineer): PARTIALLY FIXED — Fix 1 landed on both platforms, Fix 2 landed
for `witness` only, Fix 3 NOT landed (needs owner approval for the `--help` wording).**

Fix 1 implemented at `macOS/Sources/SyxxCLI/Commands/SyxxWitness.swift:16-43`
(`WitnessExitStatus` + `forVerification`) and its C# twin
`Windows/dotNET/Syxx/Commands/WitnessCommand.cs:30-67` (`ExitStatus` + `ForVerification`), wired to
the process at `macOS/Sources/SyxxCLI/SyxxCLI.swift:38` and via `Environment.ExitCode` at every
`return` in `WitnessCommand.RunAsync`. `--help`/`--version` now exit 0
(`SyxxCLI.swift:52-57`). Windows' unknown-subcommand code changed from 1 (which the contract reads
as THREAT DETECTED) to 3, matching macOS `SyxxCLI.swift:58-60` (`Program.cs:81-91`).

Measured AFTER the fix, both CLIs against the SAME files, including a snapshot produced by the
Windows CLI and verified by both:

    file                    outcome              macOS  Windows
    valid.json              VALID                    0        0
    tampered-display.json   DISPLAY MISMATCH         1        1
    tampered-sig.json       INVALID SIGNATURE        1        1
    valid.json --max-age 0  STALE                    2        2
    malformed.json          unreadable               3        3
    nonexistent.json        unreadable               3        3
    win-made.json           VALID                    0        0
    win-made-tampered.json  INVALID SIGNATURE        1        1
    witness --help / syxx --help / --version         0        0
    witness (usage) / witness bogus / bad subcmd     3        3

Printed text unchanged on both platforms. Regression tests spawn the REAL binary and assert on the
PROCESS exit code (a unit test on `ForVerification` would not have caught this defect, because
nothing was ever wired to the process): `macOS/Tests/SyxxKitTests/WitnessVerifyExitCodeTests.swift`
(8 tests) and `Windows/dotNET/Syxx.Tests/WitnessVerifyExitCodeTests.cs` (8 tests). Mutation-verified
RED: reverting the wiring fails 8/8 macOS and 5/8 Windows; mapping `DisplayMismatch -> Clean` fails
exactly the tamper test on both.

**FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code) — Fix 2 extended to `mirror`.** `syxx mirror` now returns meaningful exit codes: 0=clean, 1=tampering detected, 2=inconclusive, 3=error. Pattern established for remaining subcommands. Other subcommands now set `exitCode = 0` after running (B232), but don't differentiate outcomes — the remaining 13 subcommands need similar treatment.

**REMAINDER OF B253, STILL OPEN.** Fix 2 is done for `witness` and `mirror`. The other 13 macOS subcommands
(`nslook`, `leak`, `key`, `route`, `lan`, `forensics`, `sentinel`, `cage`, `warp`,

**[D122]**
**FIXED 2026-07-30 (qwen-code), already resolved.** `ResolveSecurelyAsync` now wraps its body in `SyxxTracer.StartSpan("dns.resolve.secure", ActivityKind.Client, ...)` and sets the outcome from the response's tri-state — `Inconclusive` is reported as `Inconclusive`, not success. Parity with the macOS twin is complete.
**Criticality:** MEDIUM — one platform's secure-resolution path is invisible in telemetry
**Location:** `Windows/dotNET/Syxx.Kit/DNSResolver.cs:305-307`
(`ResolveSecurelyAsync`); macOS twin `macOS/Sources/SyxxKit/DNSResolver.swift:300-310`
**Issue:** macOS `DNSResolver.resolveSecurely` wraps its body in
`SyxxTracer.span("dns.resolve.secure", kind: .client, ...)` with a `classify` closure that carries
the response's own tri-state onto the span. The Windows twin `ResolveSecurelyAsync` emits NO span
at all. `dns.resolve.secure` is the only span name that exists on one platform and not the other.
Every dashboard, alert or SLO built on that span covers macOS only, and the DoH secure-resolution
path — including its inconclusive outcomes, which are exactly what this product must surface —
is unobservable on Windows.
**OPEN — NOT FIXED, deliberately.** Found by the new parity gate (**D120**) on its first real run;
the fix is production code in `Syxx.Kit`, outside the QA lane's scope. Confirmed to be the ONLY
outstanding divergence: applying the one-line span in an isolated source copy took the gate from
exit 1 to exit 0 with no other change. Required fix: instrument `ResolveSecurelyAsync` with
`SyxxTracer.StartSpan("dns.resolve.secure", ActivityKind.Client, ...)` and set the outcome from the
returned `SecureResolutionResponse.Result` so an `Inconclusive` response is not reported as a
success span. Until then the `parity` job is RED on this, correctly.
**Cross-ref. Delta:** detected by **D120**.
